name: ArmaturaSec d.o.o.
products: NetGuard-OT: network access control appliance for industrial Ethernet segments; NetGuard-OT Mini: DIN-rail form factor variant for smaller substations and pump stations; ProtoSense: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic; ArmaturaSec Managed Support: annual firmware maintenance and remote monitoring subscription; SecAudit Report: one-time on-site assessment and written security findings report
tech: Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build); Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP protocol parsing; C and Rust for firmware components; iptables and nftables for packet filtering; GPRS and LTE-M cellular backhaul; Python for internal tooling and test scripts; Hardware-in-the-loop bench testing with physical PLC simulators; X.509 certificate management for device identity
challenges: C001-CH1: We need to detect unusual behaviour on Modbus and BACnet networks without labelled attack data — our clients have never been breached (or don't know it), so we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us. | C001-CH2: Our appliance firmware update process currently requires a technician on-site at the customer's substation; we want secure over-the-air updates, but every approach we've prototyped either has an unacceptable attack surface or fails when the GPRS link drops mid-transfer. | C001-CH3: Three clients in Serbia and one in Bosnia asked us to provide a risk quantification report in euros — how much financial loss a specific vulnerability exposes them to — and we have no methodology for that; it's becoming a dealbreaker in contract negotiations. | C001-CH4: Our quality assurance team writes regression tests by hand for every firmware release; with four hardware variants and monthly release cycles that's eating about 35% of total engineering time and we're still shipping bugs that automated tests should catch.
plans: ArmaturaSec intends to release a fifth hardware variant in late 2025 with a dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency. We are also evaluating whether to open a small office in Sarajevo to reduce travel time for Bosnian client support.
rd_capacity: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA.
past_collaborations: We ran a one-semester student project with a technical faculty in Novi Sad in 2021 that produced a prototype BACnet fuzzer; the code was useful but the collaboration was not continued formally.
about:
ArmaturaSec d.o.o. has been building network security hardware in Zrenjanin since 2008. We started by selling simple firewall appliances to regional electricity distributors who needed to segment their control networks from corporate IT. Over fifteen years that focus narrowed: today every product we ship is designed specifically for operational technology environments — the kind of networks that run pumps, switchgear, and assembly lines, not office computers.

Our customers are energy utilities, water treatment operators, and discrete manufacturers in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. They are not looking for cloud dashboards or vendor lock-in; they need a device that sits in a metal cabinet at a substation or pump station, runs for years without attention, and tells someone when something is wrong.

We have 67 people in Zrenjanin. About half write firmware or do hardware bring-up; the rest handle sales, installation, and support. Our head of engineering, Radovan Čičić, joined from a SCADA integrator in 2011 and has led every product generation since. We do not resell other vendors' software. Everything that runs on our appliances — the protocol parsers, the access control engine, the alerting logic — is written and maintained by our own team.

name: Zrenjanin Game Works d.o.o.
products: Browser-based math games for grades one through four; Serbian and Hungarian language literacy games for early primary; Basic natural-science quiz modules for grades three and four; Custom educational game development for municipalities and NGOs; Annual content-update and hosting service contracts for existing deployments
tech: HTML5 / JavaScript (vanilla and Phaser 3 game framework); PHP backend with MySQL for session and score storage; Custom clickstream event logging (JSON over REST); Figma for UI and asset design; Aseprite for pixel-art and sprite animation; Audacity for sound editing; Shared Linux VPS hosting (self-managed); Git with self-hosted Gitea
challenges: C002-CH1: Teachers tell us our math games are fun but they can't see whether a child is actually learning — we have clickstream data for 4,200 students but no way to tell if a pupil is guessing randomly versus genuinely understanding the material. | C002-CH2: We want to make our games accessible to children with dyslexia — about 12% of our user base based on teacher reports — but we don't know which font choices, colour contrasts, and text-presentation speeds actually help versus what is just marketing. | C002-CH3: We applied for an Innovation Fund Voucher six months ago and the application was returned twice for administrative corrections — we don't have the internal capacity to manage grant paperwork and it's pulling our lead developer away from product work for weeks at a time.
plans: We want to expand our catalogue to cover grades five and six by the end of 2026, and we are exploring a pilot with one Hungarian school district for a fully bilingual game set tied to their local curriculum. We are also considering moving from VPS hosting to a managed cloud setup to reduce maintenance load on Miroslav.
rd_capacity: Miroslav Kovačević is available for roughly one day per week for research-related work, with Tatjana available for pedagogy input on a similar basis, but both are constrained by ongoing contract delivery.
past_collaborations: We worked informally with a primary school teacher network in Zrenjanin — coordinated by a local NGO called Vojvodina Creative Schools — to gather playtesting feedback during the development of our first math module in 2020, but we have no formal research or university collaboration history.
about:
Zrenjanin Game Works d.o.o. was founded in 2019 by siblings Miroslav and Tatjana Kovačević, who grew up in Zrenjanin and wanted to build something useful for the region's schools rather than chase the international mobile market. We make browser-based educational games for primary school children in Serbia and Hungary, sold mainly to municipalities, school boards, and NGOs that work in bilingual Serbian–Hungarian communities in Vojvodina.

Our games run in any modern browser without installation, which matters in schools where IT budgets are tight and devices are old. Subjects covered include mathematics, Serbian language, Hungarian language, and basic natural sciences for ages six to twelve.

We are a team of eight: two developers, one graphic designer, one illustrator, one sound designer, one pedagogy consultant, and two people handling sales, contracts, and support. Tatjana leads product and pedagogy; Miroslav leads development. Most of us have known each other since secondary school or university in Novi Sad.

Our customers include the City of Zrenjanin education office, three NGOs operating across Vojvodina, and two municipal education departments in southern Hungary. We work on fixed-price B2B contracts, usually tied to a school year, and we spend real time talking to teachers before we build anything.

name: AutomVoj a.d.
products: PLC-controlled conveyor systems for chilled and ambient food production lines; Automated sorting and grading equipment for fruit, vegetable, and packaged goods; Electrical control panels and drive cabinets for industrial automation; On-site commissioning, maintenance contracts, and spare-parts supply; System retrofits and capacity upgrades on legacy conveyor installations
tech: Siemens S7-1500 and S7-300 PLC platforms; Ladder logic and structured text programming in TIA Portal; Siemens SINAMICS and SEW-EURODRIVE servo and frequency drive systems; Mild steel and stainless steel MIG/MAG welded frame fabrication; EPLAN Electric P8 for electrical schematic design; Profibus and Profinet industrial networking; HMI development with Siemens WinCC and Weintek panels; AutoCAD Mechanical for conveyor layout and structural drawings
challenges: C003-CH1: Our conveyor frames crack at the weld joints after roughly 18 months of operation in chilled environments; we've replaced 14 assemblies under warranty this year and we can't reproduce the failure in our workshop because we test at room temperature. | C003-CH2: Our PLC programs for different customers are each a custom spaghetti of ladder logic; when we want to push a safety patch we have to touch 38 separate codebases and it takes three engineers two full weeks. | C003-CH3: We need a €2 million investment to open a second assembly hall, and our bank wants a three-year cash-flow model with sensitivity analysis that our CFO doesn't have the capacity to prepare before the Q3 deadline. | C003-CH4: Noise from our servo drives is injecting harmonics back into client factory grids and we've had two complaints from clients whose measurement instruments were affected; we don't have the tools to characterise the emission spectrum properly.
plans: AutomVoj intends to increase its export share to 55 percent of revenue within three years, targeting food logistics customers in Central Europe, and is evaluating an entry into automated poultry processing lines as a second vertical. The second assembly hall, once financed, is expected to be operational by mid-2026.
rd_capacity: We have no dedicated R&D department; technical development happens informally through project work, led by our chief engineer and two senior automation engineers who allocate time between live projects and improvement work.
past_collaborations: AutomVoj completed a one-year joint development project with Fakultet tehničkih nauka in Novi Sad in 2019 on drive energy monitoring, which resulted in an internal measurement tool but was not published or commercialised.
about: AutomVoj a.d. has been building conveyor and sorting automation systems from its base in Zrenjanin since 1983. What started as a small workshop supplying domestic food processing plants has grown into a team of 212 engineers, electricians, and technicians shipping systems to customers in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, Austria, Slovenia, Croatia, and Slovakia. Our core business is straightforward: we design, manufacture, and commission PLC-based conveyor lines and automated sorting equipment for food and beverage producers who need reliable throughput in demanding environments — cold stores, wet wash areas, high-dust packaging halls. We do not chase every sector; we know food and beverage and we do it well. Our fabrication shop, electrical assembly area, and in-house testing floor are all under one roof on our Zrenjanin site. Most of our project managers started as commissioning engineers, so they understand what a line stoppage costs a customer at three in the morning. We have long-term supply relationships with component makers in Germany and Italy and we carry enough spares stock to respond within 48 hours on any system we have installed. Roughly 60 percent of our revenue now comes from repeat customers or referrals.

name: OsiguroMi d.o.o.
sector: Insurtech — embedded micro-insurance and parametric products
products: Parametarsko osiguranje useva po vremenskim okidačima; Automatsko osiguranje od kašnjenja leta ugrađeno u platforme za rezervaciju; Osiguranje od otkazivanja festivala i open-air događaja; White-label API za ugradnju mikro-osiguranja u aplikacije trećih strana; Nadzorna tabla za B2B partnere sa isplatnom analitikom u realnom vremenu
tech: REST API sa OAuth 2.0 autentifikacijom za partnerske integracije; Automatizovana obrada zahteva za naknadu bazirana na pravilima (rules engine); Integracija sa eksternim API-jem za status letova (FlightBridge Data Services); Mreža meteoroloških stanica i RHMZS podaci za agro-proizvode; PostgreSQL baze podataka sa vremenskim serijama za istorijske gubitke; Python okruženje za aktuarsko modelovanje i kalibraciju okidača; Kubernetes orkestracija za skaliranje tokom vršnog prometa rezervacija
challenges: C004-CH1: Our weather-triggered crop parametric product pays out when measured rainfall at the nearest official station drops below a threshold, but farmers tell us the station is sometimes 30 km away and their field got rain while the station recorded drought — we're paying out when we shouldn't and refusing when we should. | C004-CH2: We process around 9,000 travel-delay claims per month fully automatically, but our internal audit found that 3.1% of payouts were triggered by data errors from the flight-status API rather than genuine delays — that's real money leaking out every month. | C004-CH3: We want to price parametric festival-cancellation policies based on historical weather and event cancellation data, but we have fewer than 200 historical festival events in our database and standard actuarial methods need far more data points to produce stable loss curves. | C004-CH4: We need to appoint a licensed insurance intermediary in Austria to distribute through a Vienna-based travel platform, and the FMA licensing process has been stalled for seven months because our legal representative resigned.
plans: Do kraja 2025. planiramo da proširimo agro-liniju na Bugarsku i Rumuniju kroz partnerstvo sa regionalnim zadrugama, i da uvedemo novi okidač za osiguranje od mraza. Razmatramo i mogućnost sopstvene licencirane distribucije u još jednoj EU jurisdikciji kako bismo smanjili zavisnost od spoljnih posrednika.
rd_capacity: Imamo jednog internog istraživača za modelovanje podataka i dva seniorna inženjera koji mogu da izdvoje deo kapaciteta za zajedničke projekte, uz uslov da rezultati budu primenjivi u roku od šest do devet meseci.
past_collaborations: U 2022. godini sarađivali smo sa jednom lokalnom softverskom firmom Logosfera d.o.o. na razvoju prototipa nadzorne table za partnere, ali formalna istraživačka saradnja sa akademskim institucijama do sada nije uspostavljena.
about:
OsiguroMi d.o.o. je insurtech kompanija iz Novog Sada, osnovana 2019. godine sa jednom idejom: da osiguranje prestane da bude papirologija i postane tihi servis ugrađen u alate koje ljudi već koriste. Umesto da korisnik kupuje polisu na posebnom sajtu, naša tehnologija se integriše direktno u aplikacije za rezervaciju putovanja, agro-platforme i prodajne sisteme organizatora festivala — i polisa nastaje u trenutku transakcije.

Radimo sa B2B partnerima širom Srbije i EU: putničkim platformama, zadrugama, organizatorima open-air događaja. Naš tim od 58 zaposlenih dolazi iz osiguranja, softverskog inženjerstva i analize podataka. Osnivači Milena Čabarkapa i Dragan Horvat prethodno su radili u reosiguranju i fintech sektoru, što je oblikovalo naš pristup: prvo model, pa produkt.

Ono što nas razlikuje nije marketing — razlikuje nas API koji se može uključiti za manje od jednog radnog dana i parametarski okidači koji ne zahtevaju korisnikov zahtev za naknadu. Isplata se dešava automatski ili ne, na osnovu merljivih podataka: kašnjenje leta, količina padavina, otkazivanje događaja. Nema formulara, nema čekanja. Klijenti naših partnera to retko primete dok im ne zatreba, a onda primete odmah.

name: Kardiolink a.d.
products: KL-Patch 72: 72-hour single-use adhesive ECG monitoring patch; KL-Patch 14: 14-day extended-wear cardiac event recorder; KardioPortal: cloud platform for ECG data management and clinical reporting; KL-Reader: clinic-side docking station and data upload terminal; Custom OEM patch manufacturing for third-party remote monitoring programmes
tech: ADS1293 and ADS1298 analog front-end ICs for ECG acquisition; nRF52840 SoC for Bluetooth Low Energy communication and firmware; FreeRTOS on ARM Cortex-M4 for embedded firmware; Lossless ECG compression using modified SZ algorithm; AWS S3 and Glacier tiered storage for signal archives; IEC 62304-compliant software lifecycle toolchain (Jira, Confluence, Polarion); Altium Designer for PCB layout and design verification; Python and MATLAB for signal processing algorithm prototyping
challenges: C005-CH1: Our 72-hour ECG patch consumes 18 mAh per day when Bluetooth is on, which means the battery barely lasts the full wear period in patients who move a lot; we need to cut active current draw by at least 35% without reducing sampling rate below 250 Hz. | C005-CH2: We generate roughly 2 TB of raw ECG signal per month from field devices; our current lossless compression gives us only 3:1 ratio and storage costs at our cloud provider have reached €7,400 per month, which is unsustainable at the patient volume we are projecting for next year. | C005-CH3: Our CE MDR technical file was submitted eight months ago and the notified body has come back with 23 queries about our software lifecycle documentation under IEC 62304; we do not have in-house regulatory affairs staff experienced with the new MDR annexes and hiring one is taking longer than expected.
plans: Kardiolink plans to launch the KL-Patch 14 in the German and Dutch markets following CE MDR certification and to expand KardioPortal with a structured reporting module aimed at high-volume cardiology outpatient departments. Over the following two years we intend to grow the device fleet to 6,000 active patches per month and bring cloud infrastructure costs back in line with 2022 levels.
rd_capacity: We have twelve people working across hardware, firmware, and algorithm development, with a shared lab equipped for electronics prototyping, signal acquisition testing, and device-level EMC pre-compliance testing.
past_collaborations: Between 2019 and 2021 Kardiolink worked with the engineering faculty in Subotica on a student project to evaluate alternative electrode materials, which informed the adhesive layer redesign in the KL-Patch 72 revision three.
about:
Kardiolink a.d. has been designing and manufacturing cardiac monitoring devices in Novi Sad since 2004. We started as a small team of electrical engineers and cardiologists who believed that continuous ECG monitoring should not require a hospital stay. Twenty years later, we employ 112 people across hardware design, firmware, clinical affairs, and software, and our patches are used by cardiology clinics and remote patient monitoring programmes in fourteen EU countries.

Our core product is the KL-Patch line: single-use, adhesive ECG patches that patients wear for up to 72 hours while going about their normal lives. Clinicians receive processed reports through our cloud-based KardioPortal platform. We handle everything from electrode chemistry and PCB layout to the signal processing algorithms and the regulatory documentation that lets our devices reach patients legally.

What keeps us grounded is that we manufacture in-house at our Novi Sad facility. We control tolerances, can trace every component, and can respond to field feedback without waiting on a contract manufacturer. Our clinical team works directly with cardiologists at partner clinics to make sure what we ship is actually useful at the bedside, not just impressive on a datasheet. We are a mid-size company and intend to stay close to the product.

name: PravniPilot a.d.
products: AI-assisted legal research portal with full-text search across three jurisdictions; Case-outcome prediction module for commercial, labor and property disputes; Document annotation and summary tool with source citation; Court-decision bulk data export API for enterprise customers; Custom legal dataset licensing for insurers and financial institutions
tech: Python (data pipelines and ML model training); PyTorch for transformer-based text classification; Elasticsearch for full-text document indexing; PostgreSQL for structured case metadata; React front-end with TypeScript; Docker and Kubernetes on-premises cluster at NTP Novi Sad; Custom PDF and HTML parser for court-document ingestion; Internal annotation tool for labeling case outcomes
challenges: C006-CH1: Our case-outcome prediction model achieves only 61% accuracy on commercial-dispute rulings from Serbian courts, which is barely better than a lawyer's gut feeling; we suspect the problem is that our training set has only 9,000 labelled decisions and courts don't publish enough structured data. | C006-CH2: We are trying to raise a €2.5 million Series A round to fund expansion into the German legal market but all three venture funds we spoke to in Q1 said our cap table structure is too messy from the 2019 convertible note round; we need legal restructuring advice, not technology. | C006-CH3: Law firm users copy our AI-generated research summaries directly into briefs without reading them, and twice this year the summaries contained an outdated precedent; we need a way to attach confidence scores and source provenance to every generated sentence. | C006-CH4: We store full-text court decisions for three jurisdictions and search response time has degraded from 0.4 seconds to 3.1 seconds since we crossed 2 million documents; our database engineers say we need a fundamentally different indexing architecture.
plans: PravniPilot intends to launch a German-language pilot of its research platform with at least five German law firms by mid-2026, contingent on completing the Series A round. In parallel, the company plans to release a public confidence-scoring API for legal summaries that smaller legal-tech vendors in the region can license.
rd_capacity: Our development team of 14 engineers and two data scientists can allocate roughly two days per week to collaborative research work, provided any research output can be integrated directly into the production codebase.
past_collaborations: PravniPilot ran a six-month data-labeling project with a Novi Sad-based language annotation firm, LinguaNova d.o.o., in 2022 to produce a cleaned subset of Croatian court decisions, but has no current active research partnerships.
about:
PravniPilot a.d. was founded in 2012 in Subotica by a small team of practicing lawyers and software developers who were tired of spending hours manually searching court archives. We started with a simple keyword-search tool for Serbian civil cases and, over twelve years, grew that into a full AI-assisted research and case-prediction platform now used by 230 law firms in Serbia, Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Our platform ingests published court decisions, extracts key legal arguments, and gives lawyers a structured view of how similar disputes have been decided. The prediction module estimates probable outcome ranges for commercial, labor, and property disputes. We do not replace legal judgment — we give lawyers faster access to better evidence so their judgment is better informed.

Our development office sits inside NTP Novi Sad, where most of our engineering and data team works. The Subotica headquarters handles commercial, finance and client relations. Across both offices we employ 78 people, roughly half of them with legal backgrounds.

Our current customers range from two-partner boutique firms in Banja Luka to mid-size litigation practices in Zagreb and Belgrade. We have processed over two million court decisions and continue to add new documents daily. We are not the fastest-growing company in legal tech, but our retention rate — 91% of firms renew annually — tells us we are building something genuinely useful.

name: Suncokret Eko d.o.o.
sector: Cleantech — biomass and organic waste valorisation
products: Wood-free biomass pellets (ENplus-equivalent grade) from sunflower husks and maize cobs; Agricultural biochar for soil amendment and carbon sequestration; Custom pelletising service for third-party agricultural waste streams; Bulk biochar supply for industrial composting and land reclamation projects; Carbon removal documentation support package for biochar buyers seeking credit eligibility
tech: Rotary drum drying for feedstock moisture control; Hammer-mill particle-size reduction and screening; Flat-die and ring-die pellet presses; Slow-pyrolysis reactor (batch, 400–700 °C operating range); Proximate and ultimate analysis of biochar (fixed carbon, ash, volatile matter); Feedstock moisture monitoring with in-line NIR sensors; Mass-balance and carbon-yield tracking spreadsheets (internally developed); ISO 17225 pellet quality testing protocols
challenges: C007-CH1: Our biochar product tests at around 55% fixed carbon but customers in Germany need at least 70% for soil-amendment certification; we've tried raising pyrolysis temperature but that cuts yield by nearly a third and makes the economics fall apart. | C007-CH2: We want to enrol our biochar in the European Biochar Certificate scheme to sell carbon removal credits but the documentation requirements are in German and English and keep changing; we've already spent six months on paperwork without submitting a complete application. | C007-CH3: Our pellet press breaks down about once a month because the sunflower husk feedstock has inconsistent moisture and particle size coming from different suppliers; downtime costs us roughly 15,000 EUR per incident when we have delivery commitments.
plans: Suncokret Eko is expanding pyrolysis capacity with a second batch reactor expected to be operational by mid-2026, targeting a combined biochar output of 400 tonnes per year. We are also exploring co-processing of food-industry digestate with our existing agricultural residue streams to diversify feedstock supply.
rd_capacity: We have two technically trained staff who can run controlled production trials and maintain detailed process logs, but we do not have dedicated research personnel or laboratory equipment beyond basic moisture and proximate-analysis tools.
past_collaborations: We completed a six-month feedstock characterisation project in 2022 with the Institute for Food Technology in Novi Sad (FINS) to benchmark the energy content of regional sunflower husk varieties.
about:
Suncokret Eko d.o.o. was founded in 2017 in Novi Sad by a small group of agricultural engineers and process technicians who wanted to do something practical with the mountains of sunflower husks and maize cobs left behind every harvest season in Vojvodina. We started with a single pellet press in a rented hall near the Danube and now operate a full processing line at the NTP Novi Sad campus with 31 people on staff.

We buy agricultural residues directly from farms and food-processing plants across the region, dry and sort them, and convert them into two main products: pressed pellet fuel sold to district heating operators and private households, and biochar used as a soil amendment and carbon-sequestration material. Our domestic heating customers include several municipal utility companies in Serbia and a growing number of commercial greenhouse operators in Hungary and Romania. On the biochar side we are working toward export sales in Germany and the Netherlands.

What separates us from larger biomass processors is that we stay close to the feedstock supply chain. Our head of procurement, Milica Vranić, maintains direct contracts with fourteen farms, which gives us visibility on quality before material arrives at the gate. Our process lead, Dragan Ostojić, has run more than two hundred pyrolysis batches and keeps detailed logs that we use to tune every run. We are not the biggest operation in the region, but we know our material well.

name: Elekron Sistemi a.d.
products: Ruggedised electronic control panels for water and district-heating substations; Remote terminal units (RTUs) for SCADA integration over licensed radio and GSM; LoRaWAN collar retrofit kits for legacy water and heat meters; Custom sheet-metal enclosures and powder-coated housing fabricated in-house; Field maintenance and remote diagnostics service contracts
tech: LoRaWAN (Class A and Class C devices, custom network server integration); Embedded C firmware on STM32 and NXP Kinetis microcontrollers; IEC 61131-3 ladder logic for panel PLC configuration; Modbus RTU and DNP3 communication protocols; In-house MIG welding and CNC press-brake sheet-metal fabrication; Epoxy primer and polyester powder-coat finishing line; JTAG and SWD-based hardware debugging toolchains; GIT-based firmware version control with Jenkins CI
challenges: C008-CH1: We are retrofitting legacy water and heat meters for three municipal clients in Bosnia and North Macedonia with our LoRaWAN collar device, but the received signal strength inside basement meter rooms is between -120 and -125 dBm, which is at the edge of our gateway sensitivity — about 9% of readings are missing per day and the clients are threatening penalty clauses after six months of missed SLA. | C008-CH2: Our sheet-metal enclosure workshop in Subotica produces around 2,400 panels a year; we bend and weld everything in-house but we are seeing a 6% rework rate on powder-coated parts because weld spatter creates surface defects that only appear after coating — we lose roughly 140,000 dinars per month in rework labour and materials. | C008-CH3: We want to expand into Romania and Bulgaria but our sales team of five people has no experience with public procurement rules there — we have lost two tenders already because we submitted the wrong notarial documents and missed a local-content clause we did not know existed. | C008-CH4: The RTU firmware we ship has grown to 340,000 lines of C code over 20 years and nobody on the team fully understands the interrupt-handling layer anymore — we had two field failures in the last year caused by race conditions that took an average of 11 weeks each to reproduce and fix, which is unacceptable for critical infrastructure clients.
plans: Elekron Sistemi intends to release a second-generation LoRaWAN collar with an integrated signal-boost relay option and to qualify the product line for sale in Romania and Bulgaria by the end of 2026. We are also evaluating whether to bring a small electronics assembly line in-house to reduce dependence on contract PCB assemblers in Novi Sad.
rd_capacity: We have four engineers who can dedicate part of their time to a development collaboration, plus access to our production hardware, field-test sites at three municipal utilities, and a small lab in Subotica with oscilloscopes, protocol analysers, and environmental test chambers.
past_collaborations: We completed a two-year product-development agreement with Integra Automatika d.o.o. from Novi Sad between 2019 and 2021 covering firmware portability across two RTU hardware revisions.
about: Elekron Sistemi a.d. was founded in 1987 in Subotica by the Vukičević family, who started by building custom relay control panels for local factories. Over the following decades the company grew into a recognised supplier of ruggedised electronic control panels and remote terminal units for municipal water, heating, and waste-water operators across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. In 2014 the founding family transferred ownership to an employee trust, and today the 117 people who work here are also the owners. That structure suits us: decisions are made by people who understand the hardware and stand behind every unit that leaves Subotica. Our sheet-metal workshop bends and welds roughly 2,400 panels a year entirely in-house. Our RTU product line communicates over licensed radio, GSM, and, since 2021, LoRaWAN — a direction we are pushing hard because municipal clients need affordable ways to connect meters that were installed before wireless was an option. We hold framework contracts with seven municipal utilities and work through regional integrators in Sarajevo and Skopje. Quality certification to IEC 61439 and a service team that can reach most Western Balkans sites within 24 hours are what clients mention most when they explain why they keep reordering.

name: LinguaBot d.o.o.
products: LinguaBot Assist — multi-turn customer support chatbot for web and mobile; LinguaBot Search — knowledge-base retrieval with morphology-aware indexing; LinguaBot Studio — no-code flow builder for client content teams; LinguaBot Analytics — conversation quality dashboard with intent drift alerts; Managed integration service for core-banking and CRM connectors

challenges: C009-CH1: Our search misses answers because Serbian words change form (e.g. 'kartica', 'karticu', 'karticom') and users mix Latin and Cyrillic. | C009-CH2: Clients want the bot on the phone too; speech recognition for Serbian is poor on call audio.
plans: Voice channel in 2027.
rd_capacity: Four ML engineers.
past_collaborations: Internships for FTN students.
about: LinguaBot d.o.o. was started in 2020 by three engineers who had spent years watching Serbian-language customer support run on copy-pasted email templates and overloaded call centres. We build conversational AI products specifically for Serbian-speaking users, which sounds narrow until you realise almost no one else bothers to do it properly. Our first client was a regional bank in Vojvodina; today we serve four banks and two telecoms providers across Serbia, handling roughly 140,000 chat sessions per month. Our team of 22 people sits inside the Science and Technology Park in Novi Sad — mostly engineers, with a small product team and two computational linguists who focus exclusively on Serbian morphology and dialect variation. What makes us different is that we do not drop a generic multilingual model on top of a client's FAQ and call it done. We maintain our own annotated Serbian-language datasets, we run our own fine-tuning pipelines, and we treat morphological variation and script mixing as first-class engineering problems rather than edge cases. Clients stay with us because the bot actually understands what their customers type, not just the textbook version of it.

challenges: C010-CH1: Micro firms often have under a year of history; our scoring rejects good borrowers. | C010-CH2: The central bank wants every automated decision explained.

about: Kredo Fintech was founded in 2020 by a small group of people who had spent years watching Serbian micro and small businesses struggle to get loans from banks that wanted three years of audited accounts before they would even open a conversation. We built an online lending platform specifically for firms with one to nine employees — bakers, logistics operators, small manufacturers, web shops — who need between 500 and 50,000 euros and need it in days, not months. Our underwriting pulls transaction data, tax filings, and sector benchmarks to build a picture of a business that a traditional credit officer would never take the time to construct. Since launch we have funded over 1,400 loans and our default rate sits comfortably below the Serbian banking sector average for SME portfolios. Our team of 26 works out of the Science and Technology Park in Novi Sad, and our data team of five handles everything from pipeline engineering to model monitoring. We are regulated by the National Bank of Serbia and take that responsibility seriously. What makes us different is not speed alone — it is that we try to say yes to businesses that are genuinely creditworthy but simply do not fit the standard template.

Sentinel Byte was started in 2021 by Dragan Kovačević and his son Nikola Kovačević in Subotica. Dragan spent over twenty years maintaining IT infrastructure for a regional logistics company before deciding to put that experience toward helping smaller organisations understand their actual security exposure. Nikola came in from a computer science background with hands-on experience in network scanning and web application testing. Together they built a six-person team that covers penetration testing, security audits, and basic security consulting for clients across northern Vojvodina.

Our clients are mostly small and medium businesses — accountancy firms, medical clinics, small manufacturers — and a handful of local municipalities who have formal obligations under Serbian information security regulations but limited in-house expertise to meet them. We do not sell fear. We run structured tests, document what we find in plain language, and sit with the client until they understand what each finding means for their daily operations.

What separates us from larger firms is geography and availability. We are based in Subotica, we know the local regulatory environment, and our clients can call Dragan or Nikola directly. about: Pannonia Osiguranje-Tech a.d. was established in 2009 in Subotica, when a small group of insurance professionals decided that the Vojvodina market deserved a carrier built around data rather than paperwork. We started with straightforward motor and household policies for private customers in the northern Serbia corridor, then spent the following decade quietly replacing manual underwriting steps with sensor-driven and rules-based processes. Today our 187 staff serve roughly 41,000 active policyholders across Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and North Macedonia, with a Romanian branch application under review. Our motor book covers private cars, light commercial vehicles and agricultural machinery; our property book covers urban apartments, rural households and, increasingly, farm buildings and standing crops in the Vojvodina plains. What sets us apart is the combination of a regional insurer's knowledge of local claim patterns with the tooling usually found in larger markets: telematics hardware fitted in about 9,400 vehicles, a smart-home sensor kit sold under our own label, and a pricing function that reruns rating factors every quarter rather than every renewal cycle. Our leadership team is led by Chief Executive Mirela Bogdanović and Chief Actuary Dragan Fekete, supported by product, claims and technology heads based in Subotica and a small Belgrade office.

about: Kvantor Inženjering d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 1997 by a small group of engineers who had spent the previous decade building industrial control software for domestic factories. Our clients are production companies with between 150 and 2,000 employees who need reliable data infrastructure but cannot justify the overhead of a large in-house IT department. We handle ERP integration, business intelligence dashboards, and managed infrastructure — work that is unglamorous but critical. What keeps clients with us is consistency: our average client relationship runs seven years, and the same engineers who onboarded a client typically continue to support them. We are not a consultancy that sells transformation roadmaps; we build and operate systems. Our technical staff average nine years of industry experience. We are headquartered at Novi Sad Science and Technology Park, which gives us access to applied research contacts we use when a problem outgrows standard tooling.

Our clients range from small family bakeries to mid-sized dairy operations processing several thousand litres of milk per day. When something goes wrong at a dairy in Kikinda at six in the morning, Miroslav or one of our technicians picks up the phone. name: TloCare d.o.o.
products: Uzorkovanje zemljišta po mreži (4 ha po tački) sa terenskim timom; Nutrientne mape i preporuke za đubrenje dostupne kroz web portal; Izveštaji o potrebi za kalcifikacijom po parcelama; Godišnji praćeni programi za kooperative (višegodišnje baze podataka po parceli); Usluga tumačenja rezultata i direktna podrška agronoma klijenata

plans: U naredne dve godine planiramo da uvedemo bar jednu vrstu terenskog senzorskog merenja (elektrokonduktivitet ili blisku infracrvenu spektroskopiju) kako bismo ponudili gušće prostorno pokriće bez proporcionalnog rasta troškova uzorkovanja. rd_capacity: Imamo dva programera i jednog GIS specijalista koji mogu da odvoje do trećine radnog vremena za razvoj novih funkcija, uz povremenu podršku terenske ekipe za testiranje u polju.
past_collaborations: 2019. godine učestvovali smo u kratkom pilot projektu sa institutom 'Vojvodina Agro Centar' iz Sombora na temu optimizacije gustine uzorkovanja, ali saradnja nije formalizovana i nije objavljen zajednički rezultat.
about:
TloCare d.o.o. osnovan je 2013. godine u Novom Sadu sa jednom idejom: da kooperativama i agro-input trgovcima u Vojvodini pruži jasnu sliku o tome šta se dešava ispod površine njihovih njiva. Počeli smo sa dva agrohemičara, terenskim vozilom i dogovorom sa jednim regionalnim laboratorijem. Danas nas je dvadeset dvoje i radimo sa više od četrdeset kooperativa i distributivnih centara od Subotice do Zrenjanina.

Naša osnovna usluga je uzorkovanje zemljišta po mreži, laboratorijska analiza i dostava nutrientnih mapa kroz naš web portal koji su stranicu dizajnirali sami naši klijenti — bez nepotrebnih funkcija, samo ono što agronomu treba kada stigne s polja. Rezultati koje klijent vidi odnose se na pH, fosfor, kalijum, humus i potrebu za kalcifikacijom, uz preporuku za đubrenje po parcelama.

Ne prodajemo softver kao proizvod. Nudimo uslugu od uzorkovanja do preporuke, i ostajemo uz klijenta tokom sezone. Naš tim čine agrohemičari, jedan GIS specijalista i dva programera koji održavaju portal. Terenska ekipa poznaje specifičnosti vojvođanskih serija zemljišta, posebno parcela uz Tisu gde se hidromorfna i aluvijalna tla smenjuju na kratkim rastojanjima.

Razlikujemo se po tome što ne tražimo od klijenta da uči novi sistem — mi donosimo podatke njemu u format koji već razume.

name: DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o.

challenges: C018-CH1: We manually generate around 3,200 AUTOSAR software component configuration files per project and it takes two engineers three weeks; one of our competitors apparently automated this and turned around the same job in four days — at current rates we are losing bids on price. | C018-CH2: Our test coverage reports show 87% branch coverage but we keep finding integration bugs in the CAN communication stack after delivery; we suspect the problem is at the boundary between components from different suppliers but we have no systematic way to find those interaction faults before shipping. | C018-CH3: Three of our five engineers who do ECU flashing and diagnostic tooling learned on the job and have no formal training in UDS or OBD-II protocol internals; last year two of them left for a bigger company in Novi Sad within 18 months of joining and we had to restart their replacements from scratch — the training cost alone was over €25,000 each time.

about:
DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o. was founded in 2004 by Miroslav Vučić, a mechanical and electronics engineer who spent fifteen years at a German Tier-1 supplier, and his son Andrej Vučić, who joined after finishing his electrical engineering degree in Novi Sad. The two of them started with three workstations in a rented room and a single contract to port BSW modules for a mid-size European passenger car program. Twenty years later we are a team of twenty-seven engineers, all based in Novi Sad, and we have delivered software integration work on more than forty OEM projects.

We focus entirely on AUTOSAR-based embedded software: configuration, integration, and V-cycle testing for powertrain, body and chassis ECUs. We do not build hardware, we do not sell IP, and we do not resell tools. Customers come to us because we do one thing and we do it carefully. Our engineers work directly inside the customer's development environment, using their toolchains and following their process rules.

Our main customers are Tier-1 and Tier-2 suppliers delivering ECUs to European OEMs. We have worked with companies such as Hartfeld Automotive Systems (Germany), Rennova Electronics (Czech Republic) and Balkon Drive Solutions (Slovakia). Most contracts run between six and twenty-four months.

What keeps customers coming back is straightforward: we document everything, we flag problems early, and we do not hide schedule risk.

name: BrzaPošta Logistics d.o.o.
products: Next-day parcel delivery across Vojvodina; Same-day express delivery within Novi Sad city limits; E-commerce fulfilment and short-term warehousing; Cross-border courier service to southern Hungary; Returns handling and re-dispatch for online retailers
tech: Zebra ZT411 industrial label printers and Honeywell Voyager barcode scanners at sorting stations; Custom-built transport management system (TMS) developed in-house in 2019, running on a local Dell PowerEdge server cluster; Off-the-shelf route optimisation software (RouteMax Pro, version 4.2, purchased 2017); Motorola handheld devices for driver proof-of-delivery capture; PostgreSQL database storing two years of parcel transaction, delivery-attempt and return records; Excel-based daily staffing and returns-desk scheduling; Basic CCTV monitoring across the sorting hub floor
challenges: C019-CH1: Our hub processes around 4,200 parcels a day and we sort them manually into route bins; mis-sorts run at roughly 3%, which means 120 wrong deliveries daily and a re-delivery cost we estimate at €18,000 a month. We need an automated vision system that reads label barcodes and diverts parcels to the right chute, but our conveyor belts move fast and labels sometimes wrap around curved surfaces. | C019-CH2: We are expanding into same-day grocery delivery for three Novi Sad supermarket chains starting Q3, and our current route-planning software (off-the-shelf, bought in 2017) recalculates a full day's routes in about 22 minutes — that is fine at 6 a.m. but useless when 40 new orders drop at noon and drivers are already on the road. We need re-optimisation in under 90 seconds on our existing server. | C019-CH3: Driver turnover hit 38% last year — we trained 31 new drivers and lost 29 — mostly because younger people don't want fixed shifts and the pay band is capped by what our retail clients will tolerate. We've tried signing bonuses and a referral scheme, but nothing is sticking, and HR costs for constant onboarding are eating our margin. | C019-CH4: About 11% of our parcels are returned by recipients and have to travel back through the hub; we have no reliable forecast of how many returns will arrive on a given day, so we either overstaff the returns desk or create a backlog that delays re-dispatch by 48 hours. We want a model that predicts daily return volumes at the SKU-sender level using our two years of transaction history.
plans: BrzaPošta plans to launch same-day grocery delivery in Novi Sad by Q3 2024 under contract with three local supermarket chains, and intends to extend cross-border parcel service northward to cover the full Bács-Kiskun region of Hungary by early 2025.
rd_capacity: We do not have a dedicated R&D team, but our operations manager and two senior dispatchers can commit time to test and validate technical solutions on live hub operations, and our in-house TMS developer can integrate external outputs into our existing systems.
past_collaborations: In 2022 BrzaPošta participated in a six-month process-improvement programme run by NTP Novi Sad's business support office, which produced a revised hub layout that reduced average parcel dwell time by roughly 11 minutes.
about:
BrzaPošta Logistics d.o.o. was founded in 2011 by Miroslav Đurić and Tamara Vuković, two former freight-forwarding coordinators who saw that small Serbian online retailers had no reliable way to get parcels to customers the next morning. We started with four vans and a rented garage in Futog. Today we operate 34 vehicles, a 2,400 square-metre sorting hub located just off the Novi Sad bypass near the Science and Technology Park, and a team of 87 people covering every postal code in Vojvodina plus a cross-border corridor into southern Hungary through our partner carrier KelInfo Szállítás Kft.

Our clients are mostly online retailers — fashion, electronics, pet supplies, home goods — ranging from two-person startups to regional warehouse operations moving a few hundred parcels a day. We also handle fulfilment storage for six clients who prefer not to manage their own warehouses.

What separates us from national carriers is local knowledge and direct accountability. Our dispatchers know Novi Sad street by street. When something goes wrong, clients reach a real person, not a call-centre script. We are not the cheapest option and we do not pretend to be; we compete on reliability and on actually delivering within the promised window. Our current on-time rate across standard shipments is 94.2%, measured against confirmed delivery timestamps.

name: DriveCore Software
products: Body control module software development; Software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing services; AUTOSAR configuration and integration; Functional safety consulting aligned to ISO 26262; Custom verification tooling and script libraries
tech: AUTOSAR Classic; C (C99 and C11); MATLAB/Simulink; dSPACE SCALEXIO and MicroAutoBox; CANoe and CANalyzer; DOORS for requirements management; Jenkins for continuous integration; Git and Gerrit for version control
challenges: C020-CH1: Writing ISO 26262 test cases by hand takes most of our verification budget. | C020-CH2: We need a cheaper hardware-in-the-loop bench for smaller projects.
plans: A test-automation product line.
rd_capacity: Twenty engineers in verification.
past_collaborations: Guest lectures at FTN.
about:
DriveCore Software was founded in 2010 by a small group of embedded engineers who had spent the previous decade writing low-level firmware for automotive suppliers across Central Europe. We set up in Novi Sad because the engineering talent here is strong and the cost structure lets us compete with much larger firms. Today we are 85 people, most of them software engineers and verification specialists, working out of the Science and Technology Park in Novi Sad.

Our core business is embedded software for automotive tier-1 suppliers. That means body control modules, lighting systems, door and window management, and the testing services that go alongside them. We do not make hardware ourselves; we write and verify the software that runs inside it. Our customers are mid-sized tier-1 suppliers who need a reliable subcontractor that understands AUTOSAR, functional safety, and the practical realities of getting a module from prototype to production.

What sets us apart is that we have built a verification team of twenty engineers who do nothing but test. That is unusual for a company our size. Most firms of 85 people mix verification in with development. We keep them separate on purpose, because the cost of a defect found late in a project is much higher than the cost of a dedicated tester found early. We have delivered software for body control units that went into series production at two European tier-1 customers, and we are currently working on a third programme. We are now building a test-automation product line to turn the tools and scripts we have developed internally into something we can sell.

name: FinPuls Tehnologije d.o.o.
sector: Fintech — B2B payment infrastructure and reconciliation
products: Platforma za rekoncijaciju plaćanja u realnom vremenu; Konektor paket za Stripe, Adyen, Klarna i lokalne acquirere; Izveštajni modul sa revizijskim tragom za interne i eksterne revizore; Widget za praćenje cash-flow trendova na dnevnom nivou (beta)

challenges: C021-CH1: Reconciliation jobs that match transactions across Stripe, Adyen, Klarna and local acquirers take up to 90 minutes to run for clients with 50,000 daily orders — merchants need the numbers closed before their morning finance meeting. | C021-CH2: We want to add a cash-flow forecasting widget to the dashboard — merchants keep asking for it — but we only have 60 to 90 days of transaction history per client and seasonal patterns are hard to capture with that little data. | C021-CH3: We are trying to close our seed round — we've spoken to seven regional VCs and two said our data-processing terms in the standard merchant contract create GDPR liability that could block a German institutional lead investor.
plans: Do kraja 2025. godine planiramo da servisiramo dvadeset aktivnih klijenata i da uvedemo podršku za još dva payment providera relevantna za DACH tržište. U narednih dvanaest meseci fokus je na stabilizaciji platforme i zatvaranju seed runde.
rd_capacity: Tim može da odvoji jednog do dva inženjera za istraživačku saradnju u trajanju do tri meseca, uz uslov da postoji jasan cilj koji se može implementirati u postojeći sistem.
past_collaborations: Do sada nismo imali formalnu saradnju sa istraživačkim institucijama; neformalne konsultacije vodili smo sa jednim predavačem sa Fakulteta tehničkih nauka vezano za arhitekturu baza podataka, ali bez potpisanog ugovora.
about:
FinPuls Tehnologije d.o.o. osnovana je 2021. godine u Novom Sadu, u okviru Naučno-tehnološkog parka Novi Sad, od strane tima koji je pre toga radio na procesiranju plaćanja u nekoliko regionalnih fintech kompanija. Uočili smo konkretan problem: srednje veliki e-commerce prodavci koji koriste više payment providera istovremeno ne mogu da zatvore dnevni obračun na vreme, jer svaki provider isporučuje podatke u drugačijem formatu i u drugačije vreme. Naš odgovor je oblak-nativna platforma za rekoncijaciju plaćanja koja prima transakcione podatke od četiri ili više providera, normalizuje ih i isporučuje usklađen izveštaj pre jutarnjeg sastanka finansijskog tima.

Danas servisiramo deset aktivnih klijenata — uglavnom e-commerce operatere iz Nemačke, Austrije i Srbije koji procesiraju između 10.000 i 80.000 porudžbina dnevno. Osnivački tim čine Milena Vuković (CEO, ranije Payrix Adriatic), Dragan Stanković (CTO, bivši arhitekta u Konto Systems) i Jovana Ilić (CPO). Tim broji dvanaest zaposlenih. Ono što nas razlikuje nije lista funkcionalnosti — to je garantovano vreme zatvaranja: klijent zna tačno kada će imati broj.

name: Njivomer Agro d.o.o.
products: GPS-based parcel boundary mapping and cadaster integration; AgriGIS consulting and variable-rate application layer preparation; NjivaManager – farm management information system for Android; Drone-based crop scouting and multispectral index mapping; Soil sampling coordination and spatial soil-type mapping
tech: GNSS RTK field surveying (Topcon HiPer HR receivers); QGIS and PostGIS for spatial data processing; Python scripting for cadaster data cleaning and layer alignment; Android (Java/Kotlin) for NjivaManager tablet application; DJI Agras and Phantom series drones with Pix4Dfields processing; PostgreSQL database backend for farm records; REST API integration with Serbian state cadaster web services; Raster soil-type maps derived from legacy Yugoslav soil surveys and own sampling
challenges: C022-CH1: When we import parcel boundaries from the state cadaster they frequently have 2–4 metre positional errors, which means our variable-rate application layers do not line up with the physical field edges and clients get under- or over-application strips along headlands; we lose about half a day per farm correcting this manually. | C022-CH2: Our farm management software is used on cheap Android tablets in tractor cabs and it crashes on older firmware versions (Android 8 and 9) which still account for about 40% of our installed base; we have tried three times to fix it but each patch introduces new problems on a different device. | C022-CH3: We want to add a water-balance module so farmers can plan irrigation scheduling, but none of our staff understands evapotranspiration modelling or how to couple it with our existing soil-type maps; we need someone to build and validate that calculation engine.
plans: Njivomer Agro intends to extend NjivaManager coverage to farms in southern Bačka and the Srem region by the end of 2026, and to offer the water-balance irrigation module as a standard feature of the platform once it is validated. The company is also evaluating whether to add a subscription tier for remote crop monitoring using monthly drone flyovers.
rd_capacity: We have two in-house developers and one GIS analyst who can dedicate partial time to a research collaboration, but we do not have a dedicated R&D budget line and all practical work must connect directly to the software or field services we already run.
past_collaborations: Njivomer Agro completed a one-year data-sharing arrangement with the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture of Vojvodina in 2021 to supply anonymised parcel-boundary accuracy statistics for a regional cadaster quality review, but has not previously worked with a university or research institute.
about:
Njivomer Agro d.o.o. was founded in 2008 by Branko Šeremešić, a land-surveyor who spent thirty years measuring parcels across Bačka and Srem before deciding that farming deserved better maps. He built the company around one idea: that accurate spatial data, put directly in a farmer's hands, produces better decisions than any agronomist's estimate. Today his daughters, Milica and Jovana Šeremešić, run the business from offices in Sombor, with a team of sixty-one people covering field service, software development, and agronomic consulting.

We work with roughly 320 farms across western Vojvodina, ranging from family holdings of forty hectares to cooperative operations running several thousand. Our clients grow sunflower, maize, soy, sugar beet, and winter wheat. Most of them came to us because their previous mapping was either missing entirely or built on sketchy hand-drawn boundaries. We give them clean parcel layers, soil-type overlays, and a farm-management information system they can actually open on the tablet bolted to their tractor cab.

What sets us apart is that we still go to the field. Our surveyors walk headlands, our agronomists talk to operators, and our developers hear about crashes the same week they happen. We are not a platform company selling subscriptions from a city; we are a regional service company that has been driving dirt roads in Vojvodina for sixteen years.

name: InspektAI
products: InspektAI Line — camera and software bundle for inline defect detection; Defect dashboards — real-time and historical quality reporting for shift supervisors; InspektAI Audit — offline batch review tool for quality managers; Model Refresh Service — periodic retraining when a client's product changes
tech: PyTorch; NVIDIA Jetson Orin and NX modules; C++ inference runtime; GigE Vision industrial cameras; ONNX Runtime; Docker on embedded Linux; PostgreSQL for defect logging; Python for training pipelines
challenges: C023-CH1: Scratches on polished metal parts: reflections fool our model, and clients only have a few dozen defect photos. | C023-CH2: Clients want inference on cheaper edge devices than Jetson.
plans: Enter the automotive supply chain.
