past_collaborations: Hackathon sponsor in 2024.
about: InspektAI was founded in 2020 by a small group of engineers who had spent years watching factory workers manually inspect parts under fluorescent lights, catching maybe eighty percent of what slipped through. We thought we could do better with cameras and software, and four years later we are doing exactly that. Our system, InspektAI Line, sits above a conveyor or a robot arm, grabs frames at production speed, and tells the line whether a part passes or fails in under thirty milliseconds. We work mostly with metal fabricators and plastics processors in Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia — companies running one or two shifts who cannot afford a dedicated quality team on every line. Our defect dashboards give shift supervisors a live view of what is going wrong and when, so they can act before a bad batch ships. The team is eighteen people, mostly engineers, with a small sales and integration group. We do our own model training, our own edge deployment, and our own on-site installation. No third-party integrators in the middle. That keeps costs down and means we actually understand what is happening on the factory floor. We are based at NTP Novi Sad, which puts us close to the University of Novi Sad and a steady stream of engineers who know what they are doing.

name: Elektro Bačka a.d.
products: Medium- and low-voltage substation design and installation; Low-voltage switchgear and distribution cabinet manufacturing; Grid maintenance and periodic inspection contracts for municipalities; Emergency fault-response and cable-fault location services; Technical documentation and commissioning support for EU-funded grid projects
tech: AutoCAD Electrical for schematic and panel layout design; SCADA integration using IEC 60870-5-104 protocol; IP54/IP65 sheet-steel enclosure fabrication with powder-coat finishing; Thermal imaging and partial-discharge testing for predictive maintenance; Proprietary legacy maintenance log database (custom dBase-derived system, Serbian-language records); SAP PM module for spare-parts inventory management; IEC 61439 testing procedures for low-voltage switchgear assemblies
challenges: C024-CH1: We are tendering for EU-funded smart-grid projects in Hungary and Romania but our technical documentation is not meeting the IEC 61968 data-model requirements that the contracting authorities demand; we've lost two tenders in the last 18 months on documentation grounds alone. | C024-CH2: Our switchgear enclosures are rated IP54 but field returns show condensation forming inside in about 8% of outdoor cabinets after two winters; we can't reproduce the failure reliably in our test room and we don't know whether it's a sealing design issue or a material issue. | C024-CH3: We have 14 years of maintenance logs from 600+ distribution cabinets, but it's all text in Serbian in a legacy database and nobody has ever extracted anything useful from it; we suspect the data could tell us which cabinet types are most likely to need a repair in the next 12 months.
plans: Elektro Bačka a.d. plans to qualify for at least one cross-border EU smart-grid contract by the end of 2025 and to launch a refreshed outdoor cabinet product line with improved ingress-protection characteristics by mid-2026.
rd_capacity: We have two senior engineers who can dedicate part of their time to development work, access to our production hall and test equipment, and the maintenance dataset, but no dedicated research budget or data-science capability in-house.
past_collaborations: We completed a joint technical-training program in 2019 with Elektrodistribucija Sever d.o.o., a regional grid operator, covering IEC protection-relay calibration, but have not previously worked with a university or research institute.
about: Elektro Bačka a.d. has been working in the electrical contracting and grid-services sector since 1983, when the company was founded in Subotica to serve the growing industrial needs of northern Vojvodina. Over four decades we have built, maintained, and upgraded medium- and low-voltage infrastructure for municipal utilities, agro-industrial complexes, and manufacturing parks across Bačka and into neighboring counties. Today our team of 210 people covers everything from primary substation installation to low-voltage switchgear manufacturing in our own production hall. Our clients include the industrial zones of Subotica, Kanjiža, and Senta, as well as several district heating operators and a number of food-processing plants that require continuous power availability. What separates us from general electrical contractors is the combination of field maintenance experience accumulated over more than forty years and an in-house manufacturing capacity that lets us build and test switchgear against the same specifications we install on site. Our engineers know how cabinets behave in Vojvodina winters, which is knowledge that comes from service records, not only from catalogues. We are currently expanding into cross-border smart-grid tendering and investing in the data side of our maintenance operation.

name: Nexara Embedded d.o.o.
products: Contract embedded hardware design and PCB layout; EMC pre-compliance testing service; IPC-certified PCB assembly and low-volume production; Functional safety consulting for automotive and industrial boards; Firmware development for ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V targets
tech: Altium Designer for schematic and PCB layout; Ansys SIwave and HyperLynx for signal and power integrity simulation; Rohde & Schwarz ESR pre-compliance receiver; IPC-A-610 and IPC-J-STD-001 certified assembly processes; JTAG and SWD-based in-circuit test fixtures; ARM Cortex-M4/M33 and RISC-V microcontrollers; CAN FD and LIN bus for automotive subsystems; ISO 13485:2016 quality management system
challenges: C025-CH1: Three of our last five PCB designs failed radiated emissions at a third-party EMC lab on the first submission, typically between 150–450 MHz, which costs us on average €9,000 per re-test visit and delays client projects by six to ten weeks; we need a systematic way to predict and fix emission hotspots during layout review rather than after the fact. | C025-CH2: One of our automotive clients requires that we deliver a functional safety analysis (FMEDA) for a new brake-system sensor interface board to ISO 26262 ASIL-B; our engineers have attended one training course but have never produced a full FMEDA document and the client's deadline is in five months. | C025-CH3: We are trying to break into the German medical-device market with a contract manufacturing offer, but a Munich distributor told us we need to be listed as a compliant contract manufacturer under MDR Annex IX before they will sign; we have no idea what that audit process looks like or how long it takes. | C025-CH4: We want to automate the optical inspection of our assembled boards — we currently have two operators checking solder joints by eye for 6 hours a day — but our component mix changes every two weeks and training a new vision model for every board variant is not practical with our current approach.
plans: Nexara Embedded is expanding its pre-compliance lab with a conducted emissions bench and a second antenna set to reduce the turnaround time on EMC screening from five days to two. Over the next two years we plan to grow our medical-device assembly capacity and pursue a second contract with a domestic automotive Tier-2 supplier.
rd_capacity: We can allocate one senior hardware engineer and one firmware engineer part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our lab equipment and internal board archives under NDA.
past_collaborations: We worked with Polaris Sensing Systems d.o.o. from Subotica on a joint development of a CAN FD gateway module for agricultural machinery between 2021 and 2022.
about: Nexara Embedded d.o.o. has been designing electronics since 2004, when four engineers left a local telecom equipment maker to start a contract design shop in Novi Sad. Twenty years later we employ 83 people across hardware design, firmware, and PCB assembly, and we work from our premises at NTP Novi Sad. Our clients are mainly in medical devices, automotive subsystems, and industrial automation — sectors where a marginal design mistake costs real money and real time. We run our own EMC pre-compliance lab with a biconical antenna, a log-periodic antenna, and a 3-metre semi-anechoic setup, so most emission problems get caught before a board leaves our building. Our IPC-certified assembly line handles boards from prototype to low-volume production runs, and our IPC-A-610 inspectors sign off every batch. What sets us apart is that we keep hardware design, layout, firmware, and first-level testing under the same roof and the same project manager. That means fewer handover gaps and a shorter cycle from schematic to working prototype. We have delivered more than 340 projects. Current team leads are Miroslav Tanić (hardware), Jelena Kovačević (firmware), and Dragan Ostojić (quality and compliance).

name: Zelena Petlja a.d.
sector: Municipal solid waste collection, sorting and recycling
products: Municipal solid waste collection across six municipalities; Mixed-stream and source-separated recyclables sorting; Polyethylene and polypropylene regranulate production; Industrial and bulky-waste removal on contract; Leachate and site environmental monitoring services
tech: Near-infrared (NIR) optical sorting line (secondhand, 2019 installation); Baling press for paper, cardboard, PET and PE fractions; Single-shaft shredder for oversized waste pre-processing; Twin-screw extruder and pelletising line for PP/HDPE regranulate; Fleet telematics on twelve collection vehicles; COD and heavy-metal leachate sampling with in-house wet chemistry bench; Manual quality-check stations downstream of optical sorter
challenges: C026-CH1: Our optical sorting line was bought secondhand in 2019 and misclassifies dark-coloured HDPE and PP at a rate of about 18%, meaning those bales sell for 40% less to commodity traders because purity is too low; we've tweaked the conveyor speed but it hasn't helped. | C026-CH2: We're trying to issue a small bond to refinance our sorting hall expansion — 2.5 million EUR — but the two investment funds we approached said our financial reporting isn't structured the way they need it and we don't have a proper credit rating. | C026-CH3: The leachate from our temporary storage yard has started seeping toward the site boundary; our last sampling showed COD at 3,400 mg/L and we're worried about the groundwater monitoring wells the inspectorate has ordered us to install.
plans: Over the next three years Zelena Petlja intends to complete the sorting hall expansion, add a second optical sorting line with improved dark-polymer detection, and extend collection contracts to two additional municipalities in northern Bačka. We are also exploring a small-scale pyrolysis pilot for non-recyclable plastic fractions that currently go to landfill.
rd_capacity: We have two technicians with process engineering backgrounds who track sorting-line performance data daily, but we have no dedicated research budget or laboratory beyond the basic wet-chemistry bench used for leachate monitoring.
past_collaborations: Between 2020 and 2022 we participated in a regional waste-data project coordinated by the Subotica Development Agency alongside two other Vojvodina waste operators, which produced a shared municipal waste composition database but no joint products.
about: Zelena Petlja a.d. has been collecting, sorting and reprocessing waste in and around Subotica since 1975, when Branko Fekete started the business with a single truck and a handshake agreement with the city. Nearly five decades later the company employs 214 people, operates twelve collection routes across six municipalities, and runs a 4,800-square-metre sorting hall on the Bajmok road. A plastics reprocessing line added in 2011 converts recovered polyethylene and polypropylene into regranulate sold to packaging manufacturers in Serbia and Hungary. The Fekete family remains the majority shareholder; day-to-day management passed to the second generation in 2018. Our customers include the municipalities of Subotica, Kanjiža and Mali Iđoš, as well as several industrial parks whose tenants pay separately for bulky and hazardous-item removal. What sets us apart is continuity: drivers who have worked the same street for fifteen years, relationships with depot managers built over decades, and a maintenance crew that keeps old equipment running longer than the manuals say it should. We are currently restructuring our ownership and reporting to bring in outside capital for a sorting hall expansion, and we are looking for technical partners who work with real operational numbers rather than ideal-case assumptions.

name: Lumina Data Solutions d.o.o.
products: Platforma za analitiku radne snage — modularan SaaS proizvod za HR odeljenja; Modul za planiranje smena sa automatskim optimizatorom rasporeda; Modul za praćenje dobrobiti zaposlenih kroz periodične ankete i analitiku; Modul za produktivnost zasnovan na metapodacima o korišćenju aplikacija i kalendara; Usluga implementacije i konfiguracije platforme za nove klijente
tech: Python (optimizacija: PuLP, OR-Tools); PostgreSQL i TimescaleDB za skladištenje vremenskih serija; React frontend sa prilagodljivim kontrolnim tablama; REST API integracije sa popularnim HRIS sistemima; Scikit-learn i XGBoost za modele prediktivne analitike; Docker i Kubernetes za isporuku i skaliranje usluge; Anonimizacija i pseudonimizacija podataka u skladu sa GDPR zahtevima
challenges: C027-CH1: Our platform recommends shift schedules for shift-based clients, but when we run the optimiser on a plant with 340 workers and 28 skill categories it takes 6 hours to produce a two-week plan — clients want a result in under 20 minutes and we don't know how to cut the solve time. | C027-CH2: Our employee wellbeing survey module produces scores that line managers say feel arbitrary; one HR director showed us that two teams with identical scores had completely different absence rates, so the construct we're measuring probably isn't what we think it is. | C027-CH3: We collect keyboard and application-usage metadata as a productivity proxy, but two clients in Slovakia have been contacted by their works councils saying this data collection may breach the Slovak Labour Code and GDPR Article 88 — we need a legal opinion fast or we could lose both contracts. | C027-CH4: When we present our platform to CFOs the conversation always stalls at ROI; we can show engagement scores going up but we have no rigorous way to translate that into a euro figure that a finance director will trust — we lose about one in three deals at this stage.
plans: U narednih 18 meseci planiramo da proširimo pokrivenost na tržište Češke i uvedemo modul za planiranje sukcesije koji koristi postojeće podatke o veštinama. Istovremeno radimo na certifikaciji naše platforme prema zahtevima ISO 27001 kako bismo olakšali ulaske u veće korporativne klijente.
rd_capacity: Imamo interni tim od petoro data inženjera i jednog istraživača koji mogu da učestvuju u zajedničkim projektima, s kapacitetom od oko 20% radnog vremena za eksperimentalne zadatke van redovnog razvoja proizvoda.
past_collaborations: Sarađivali smo s NTP Novi Sad kroz program mentorstva za startape 2018–2019. godine, a 2022. smo imali kratak tehnički angažman s IT kompanijom Softera Balkans d.o.o. iz Beograda na integraciji HRIS konektora.
about: Lumina Data Solutions d.o.o. osnovana je 2017. godine u Novom Sadu, u poslovnom inkubatoru NTP Novi Sad, sa jednim jasnim ciljem: pomoći HR odeljenjima srednje velikih kompanija da donose bolje odluke na osnovu podataka koje već poseduju. Umesto po meri pravljenih projekata koji traju mesecima, razvili smo konfigurabilan softverski proizvod — platformu za analitiku radne snage koja kombinuje podatke iz internih anketa, metapodatke iz kalendarskih sistema i signale produktivnosti. Danas naš tim čini 74 stručnjaka, od data inženjera i istraživača do konsultanata i menadžera za korisničku podršku. Klijenti su nam HR direktori i operativni direktori u Srbiji, Sloveniji i Slovačkoj — kompanije sa 200 do 2.000 zaposlenih, najčešće u proizvodnji, logistici i finansijskim uslugama. Ono što nas razlikuje od klasičnih HR konsultanata jeste to što isporučujemo platformu koja ostaje kod klijenta i radi kontinuirano, a ne jednokratni izveštaj. Među prvim klijentima bio je distributer prehrambenih proizvoda Voćar Komerc iz Subotice; danas radimo s više od 30 kompanija. Verujemo da je analitika radne snage korisna samo ako je razumljiva menadžerima koji nisu statistički stručnjaci.

name: PlastiPak Vojvodina a.d.
products: Injection-moulded PP food trays for retail and food-processing customers; Thermoformed PET and PP lids for fresh produce and dairy packaging; Stackable polypropylene industrial crates for logistics and food transport; Custom rigid tray formats produced to buyer specifications; Regrind-blended packaging grades for non-food industrial clients
tech: Injection moulding (PP, HDPE, PS) on 180–650 tonne presses; Thermoforming of sheet PET and PP; In-house tool room with EDM and milling for mould maintenance; Pad printing for batch codes and panel graphics; Regrind processing and blend-back into non-food lines; Cooling-circuit monitoring via plant-floor SCADA (Fenix DataLog v4); Manual coordinate measurement for dimensional inspection; ISO 9001:2015 quality management system
challenges: C028-CH1: We run eight injection-moulding presses around the clock and we are seeing a 7–9% rejection rate on our PP food-tray line because of warpage that shows up after the parts cool on the conveyor — the reject pile costs us roughly 140,000 dinars a week in material alone, and our process engineers are still tuning cooling-time and hold-pressure by trial and error. | C028-CH2: A German retail chain that takes 30% of our crate volume says they will require us to have an ISO 14001 environmental management certificate by January 2026 or they will delist us — we have never done an environmental audit and we do not know where to start with our waste plastics, regrind reuse documentation, or cooling-water discharge reporting. | C028-CH3: We print batch codes and nutrition panels directly onto our trays with pad printing and the ink adhesion fails the cross-hatch tape test about once a week, forcing us to rework or bin a full production lot of 8,000 units — we suspect it is a surface-energy issue with our mould-release agent but we have no way to measure or control it reliably. | C028-CH4: We applied for an IPARD III grant nine months ago to co-finance a new thermoforming line and we still have not received a decision; meanwhile we signed a supply contract with a Hungarian buyer that requires us to double our tray capacity by Q3 next year and we cannot start the investment without knowing whether the grant will come through.
plans: PlastiPak Vojvodina plans to expand thermoforming capacity within the next twelve months, subject to financing conditions, and to pursue ISO 14001 certification ahead of the January 2026 customer deadline. Over the following two to three years the company intends to grow its share of food-contact tray supply in the Hungarian market.
rd_capacity: We do not have a dedicated research function, but our process engineering team of four keeps systematic production records and can run controlled trials on our presses during off-peak windows.
past_collaborations: We worked informally with a polymer testing laboratory at a technical college in Novi Sad in 2019 to characterise a batch of off-spec PP regrind, but we have no ongoing formal collaboration with any university or research institution.
about: PlastiPak Vojvodina a.d. has been shaping plastic packaging in northern Serbia since 2004. Founded in Subotica by a group of engineers with backgrounds in polymer processing, we started with two injection-moulding presses and a single client. Today we run eight presses and a thermoforming cell, employ 183 people across two shifts, and supply rigid trays, lids, and industrial crates to retail chains and food processors in Serbia and Hungary. Our plant sits on 11,000 square metres on the Subotica industrial zone, close to the Hungarian border, which keeps transport times short for our northern customers. Our main contacts in the market include regional grocery distributors such as Meridian Retail Group and food processors such as Danubefresh d.o.o. We work to tight dimensional tolerances because our customers run automated filling and sealing lines that cannot tolerate warped or undersized lids. What sets us apart is that we handle tooling modifications in-house — our tool room can adjust cavity inserts and cooling channels without sending moulds to outside contractors. Our process engineers know our machines well, and we keep detailed production logs going back to 2011. We are not a research laboratory, but we are methodical, and we are willing to bring in outside expertise when a problem goes beyond what our own team can resolve.

name: EkoGradnja Sistem a.d.
sector: Sustainable construction materials and prefabricated building systems
products: Prefabricated low-energy wall panels with recycled aggregate concrete and hemp-fibre insulation core; Prefabricated floor and ceiling panels for residential multi-storey construction; Custom-dimension structural panels for non-standard residential projects; Recycled aggregate concrete mix supply to third-party precasters; Technical advisory service for developers on panel integration and thermal detailing
tech: Wet-cast concrete panel production with vibration-table compaction; Recycled concrete aggregate processing: jaw crushing, washing, and grading; Hemp-fibre batt insulation core insertion and edge-sealing; In-house compressive strength testing (press to EN 12390-3); Chloride content measurement by potentiometric titration; Thermal conductivity spot-testing with heat-flow meter plates; ERP-based production batch tracking (ERPAG platform); AutoCAD-based panel layout and reinforcement design
challenges: C029-CH1: We introduced hemp-fibre insulation cores into our wall panels two years ago, but some batches absorb moisture during storage and the thermal resistance drops by up to 30 percent before the panels ever reach a construction site; we cannot predict which batches will fail. | C029-CH2: Our recycled concrete aggregate comes from three demolition contractors and the quality varies a lot — chloride content and residual cement paste fraction change from batch to batch — and this causes compressive strength variability in our panels of plus or minus 20 percent, which is forcing us to over-design and use more virgin cement than we want to. | C029-CH3: We want to claim an Environmental Product Declaration for our panels to open the German market, but preparing a full life-cycle assessment in-house is beyond our team; we have production data but no idea how to structure the inventory or which impact categories the German clients will scrutinise. | C029-CH4: We tendered for a large social-housing project in Novi Sad and lost on price to a competitor importing standard panels from Poland; our production cost per square metre is about 12 percent higher and we have not been able to identify where the inefficiency is coming from in our manufacturing line.
plans: Over the next two years EkoGradnja Sistem intends to certify at least one panel product with a verified Environmental Product Declaration and to enter the German residential market through a distribution agreement with a Central European building-materials trader. In parallel, the company is evaluating an investment in covered, climate-controlled panel storage to reduce weather-related quality variation.
rd_capacity: We have an in-house testing laboratory staffed by two materials technicians and a senior engineer, capable of routine mechanical and chemical testing, but we do not have research staff or data-analysis capacity beyond basic spreadsheet work.
past_collaborations: EkoGradnja Sistem participated in a two-year applied research project with the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad between 2018 and 2020, focused on mix-design optimisation for recycled aggregate concrete, resulting in an updated internal mix specification but no published output.
about: EkoGradnja Sistem a.d. has been producing structural building components in Novi Sad since 1975. Founded as a state enterprise manufacturing large-format concrete panels for Vojvodina's housing programme, the company was privatised in 2003 and rebuilt around a new generation of prefabricated wall and floor panel systems designed for low-energy construction. Today our 143-person team covers everything from aggregate processing and panel casting to technical sales and logistics. Our panels use recycled concrete aggregate sourced from regional demolition sites, combined with biosourced insulation cores — currently hemp fibre — to reduce both embodied carbon and operational heat loss. We sell to residential developers across Serbia and export to Romania and Croatia, working with clients such as Beodom Nekretnine, Construcția Vest S.R.L. in Timișoara, and Adriadom Gradnja d.o.o. in Osijek. What distinguishes us from importers is that our supply chain, technical support and product adjustments are all handled locally: a developer in Novi Sad can speak directly to the engineer who signed off the mix design. Our factory on Industrijska Street operates three production lines and an on-site materials testing laboratory. We are a mid-sized company with no ambitions to become something we are not — we want to make better panels, at a fair price, with a measurable environmental footprint.

name: GridLogic Systems d.o.o.
products: Uređaj za regulaciju napona na distribucijskoj mreži (VR-400 serija); Softverski modul za volt-VAR optimizaciju u realnom vremenu; Platforma za nadzor i telemetriju terenskih uređaja; Usluga integracije s SCADA sistemima operatora; Konsultantska podrška pri sertifikaciji opreme za zaštitu mreže
tech: DSP mikrokontroleri (Texas Instruments C2000 familija); IEC 61850 komunikacioni protokol; Python i C++ za firmware i backend; PostgreSQL s TimescaleDB ekstenzijom za telemetrijske serije; MQTT broker za komunikaciju s terenskim uređajima; 4G/LTE modemi s lokalnim baferovanjem podataka; Interni solver za mrežnu optimizaciju baziran na semidefinitnom programiranju; Osciloskopska merenja i analiza prenosnih pojava (Rigol i Yokogawa instrumenti)
challenges: C030-CH1: Our voltage-regulation device works well in steady state but when it encounters high-frequency switching transients from nearby industrial variable-speed drives, it trips on overcurrent about once a week per installation — we have oscilloscope captures but no model that predicts when this will happen. | C030-CH2: We want to offer a real-time volt-VAR optimisation service across a feeder with 200+ nodes, but our current solver takes 4–6 minutes on a standard server, which is too slow to respond to the 5-minute SCADA update cycle the operators use. | C030-CH3: We are expanding into North Macedonia and need to register our product as certified grid-protection equipment under their national technical regulations, but our legal team has no experience with Macedonian energy law and the process has been stuck for seven months. | C030-CH4: Our field devices send telemetry over 4G but in agricultural areas signal drops cause gaps of 10–40 minutes in the measurement stream; the missing data corrupts our state-estimation results and operators lose confidence in the dashboard.
plans: U narednih godinu dana planiramo da završimo sertifikaciju u Severnoj Makedoniji i potpišemo prve ugovore na tom tržištu, a zatim počnemo pripremu za ulazak u Albaniju. Paralelno radimo na novoj verziji VR-400 s poboljšanom otpornošću na elektromagnetne smetnje.
rd_capacity: Imamo interno četiri inženjera koji rade na istraživanju i razvoju s punim radnim vremenom, s pristupom laboratorijskoj opremi za testiranje zaštitnih uređaja u NTP Novi Sad.
past_collaborations: Sarađivali smo s firmom Elektromont Inženjering d.o.o. iz Beograda na terenskoj validaciji VR-400 uređaja tokom 2022. godine, bez formalne akademske saradnje do sada.
about: GridLogic Systems d.o.o. osnovana je 2018. godine u Novom Sadu, u okviru Naučno-tehnološkog parka Novi Sad, od strane grupe inženjera koji su prethodno radili na projektima modernizacije distributivnih mreža u jugoistočnoj Evropi. Naš fokus je praktičan: razvijamo uređaje i softverske alate koji pomažu operatorima distributivnih sistema da upravljaju napajanjem u realnom vremenu, bez oslanjanja na zastarele metode ručnog podešavanja. Trenutno imamo 47 zaposlenih, od kojih su dve trećine inženjeri elektrotehnike i računarskih nauka. Naši proizvodi su instalirani kod tri distributivna operatora u Srbiji i jednog u Bosni i Hercegovini. Sarađujemo s lokalnim izvođačima radova na ugradnji i podršci. Razlikujemo se od većih igrača time što projektujemo hardver i softver zajedno, što nam omogućava da brzo rešavamo probleme koji nastaju na granici između uređaja i sistema za upravljanje. Ne obećavamo revoluciju — radimo na tome da svaki feeder koji koristimo naš sistem bude stabilniji i predvidljiviji nego pre. Naš tim predvodi Miloš Vujanović kao izvršni direktor, a tehnički razvoj vodi Dragana Petrić.

name: Ekran Media Group d.o.o.
sector: Marketing tech, media and creative studios
products: Kanal 7 – local television channel broadcasting news, culture and sport across Banat; Banat.rs – online news portal covering Zrenjanin, Kikinda and Pančevo; Banat Outdoor – LED out-of-home advertising network across 48 panels in three cities; Banat Programmatic – display advertising unit serving targeted inventory to regional and national buyers; Studio Ekran – video production and post-production services for commercial clients
tech: OpenRTB-based programmatic header-bidding stack (in-house ad server); Custom Django/PostgreSQL CMS for Banat.rs; Scala-based playlist scheduling software for LED panel CMS; FFmpeg pipelines for video transcode and web delivery; Google Analytics 4 and Matomo for portal audience measurement; Basic keyword-list brand-safety filter integrated into bid evaluation layer; Climate-controlled tape archive (DV and BetaSP formats, ~14 000 tapes)
challenges: C031-CH1: Our programmatic display network serves 12 million impressions a month but our brand-safety filter blocks roughly 22 % of premium inventory because it over-classifies Serbian news articles as sensitive content; that misclassification is costing us around 9 000 EUR a month in refused bids. | C031-CH2: Our 48 out-of-home LED panels currently show the same playlist regardless of weather, traffic or time of day; we want dynamic content triggers but have no data pipeline connecting traffic counts or weather feeds to our CMS. | C031-CH3: We commissioned an audience-perception study two years ago, but we have no ongoing way to measure how editorial tone and topic mix on our news portal affects trust scores among different age cohorts; we're flying blind when making programming decisions. | C031-CH4: The TV channel's archive of 35 years of local broadcasts sits on about 14 000 DV and BetaSP tapes in a climate-controlled room; digitising and indexing them is urgent but we have no budget line approved for it and the project estimate came in at 280 000 EUR.
plans: Over the next two years Ekran Media Group intends to extend the Banat Outdoor network to at least 20 additional panels in Novi Bečej and Senta, and to launch a subscription tier on Banat.rs offering ad-free reading and exclusive local reporting. We are also evaluating a joint-venture arrangement with a Novi Sad production house to offer packaged TV and digital campaigns to national advertisers.
rd_capacity: We have one full-time developer and one part-time data analyst who can engage with a research collaboration, primarily on integration and testing work rather than core algorithm development.
past_collaborations: We ran a six-month applied project with a Subotica-based IT training centre, Infocentar Sever, in 2021 to rebuild the Banat.rs comment moderation workflow, which resulted in a deployable tool we still use today.
about: Ekran Media Group d.o.o. has been part of everyday life in the Banat region since 1987, when our founders launched a small production studio in Zrenjanin to cover local news that larger broadcasters overlooked. Over the decades we grew into a regional media group operating Kanal 7, a full-schedule local television channel; Banat.rs, an online news portal attracting around 340 000 unique visitors each month; and an out-of-home advertising network of 48 LED panels spread across Zrenjanin, Kikinda and Pančevo. In recent years we added a programmatic display unit that delivers roughly 12 million impressions per month for advertisers who want to reach Banat audiences with measurable results. Our 210 colleagues include journalists, video editors, field technicians, ad-operations staff and software developers who maintain our in-house content management systems. Our clients range from regional retail chains and car dealerships to national fast-moving-consumer-goods brands that want a genuine foothold in smaller Serbian cities. What keeps us different from national competitors is a 35-year archive of local footage, direct relationships with municipal governments and local businesses, and the ability to run a campaign across television, outdoor and digital display from a single point of contact. We are not a flashy startup; we are a regional institution that is modernising deliberately.

name: SecureEdge Labs
products: EdgeWatch sensor — passive network tap and protocol parser for OT environments; SOC service — 24/7 analyst monitoring with incident triage for industrial and building networks; FloorMap — lightweight asset discovery and topology visualisation for OT segments; PolicyAudit — one-time configuration review and hardening report for BACnet and Modbus deployments
tech: Zeek network analysis framework; Rust (sensor firmware and edge processing); Python (backend pipeline and analyst tooling); Modbus and BACnet protocol parsers (in-house); Elasticsearch for log storage and search; Grafana for operational dashboards; MQTT for sensor telemetry transport; Custom firmware signing chain based on Ed25519
challenges: C032-CH1: We need to detect unusual behaviour on Modbus and BACnet networks without labelled attack data. | C032-CH2: Clients ask whether our firmware signing will survive quantum computers.
plans: Certify under the EU Cyber Resilience Act.
rd_capacity: Four security engineers.
past_collaborations: None.
about:
SecureEdge Labs was founded in 2019 by a small group of industrial control system specialists who noticed that most cybersecurity products were built for office networks and simply did not work well in factory floors or building automation environments. We set up shop at NTP Novi Sad and have spent the years since building monitoring tools that understand the protocols that real industrial equipment actually speaks.

Today we serve a handful of manufacturers in the Vojvodina region, a district heating operator, and two commercial real estate management companies. Our customers run Modbus RTU lines, BACnet IP segments, and the assorted legacy devices that come with any real plant. They need to know when something unusual is happening on those networks, and they need that answer without shutting down production to collect training data first.

Our team is nineteen people: four security engineers who do the core research and product work, a small software group, field technicians who handle sensor deployment, and operations staff. We do not outsource our detection logic or our SOC analyst work. When a customer calls at two in the morning about a strange spike on a PLC, it is one of our own engineers who picks up.

What makes us different is narrow focus. We do not sell a platform that does everything. We sell a sensor that sits on your OT network and a monitoring service staffed by people who have read the Modbus specification more than once.

name: Senzorika Petković i sinovi preduzetnik
products: Wireless microclimate sensor nodes for greenhouses and open-field orchards; Custom sensor enclosures and mounting hardware for polytunnel installations; Hardware maintenance and calibration contracts; On-site installation and network commissioning service; Data logging gateway units with local SD-card backup
tech: LoRa radio (868 MHz, custom firmware); Semtech SX1276 transceiver modules; ATmega328P and STM32L0 microcontrollers; Hand-soldering and reflow oven assembly; IP65 polycarbonate enclosures with custom gasket fitting; Capacitive soil moisture sensing; Modbus RTU for wired legacy integrations; Simple CSV-based data export over serial or USB
challenges: C033-CH1: Our sensor nodes transmit over LoRa and we are seeing packet loss rates of up to 40% on parcels where the farm has metal-framed poly-tunnels — the signal reflection and multipath interference is killing reliability and clients are calling us every other week. | C033-CH2: We produce about 400 nodes per year by hand-soldering and we have no quality control step after assembly — roughly 6% of units come back under warranty within the first three months, which is eating our margin and our reputation. | C033-CH3: We want to expand into Hungary and Romania but we have no CE documentation for our sensor enclosures and we have no idea what the process or the cost looks like — it has been sitting on the to-do list for two years.
plans: We want to supply and service farms in southern Hungary and western Romania within the next two to three years, starting with growers we already have contact with. To do that we need CE documentation in place and a more reliable product leaving our workshop.
rd_capacity: We have one technically capable person, Miroslav Petković, who can spend roughly one day per week on development or testing work alongside his regular installation duties.
past_collaborations: We worked informally with an electronics teacher at a secondary technical school in Zrenjanin, Branko Dević, who helped us rewrite our gateway firmware about four years ago, but we have had no formal research or institutional partnerships.
about:
Senzorika Petković i sinovi has been building measurement equipment for farms in the Banat region since 1998, when Dragan Petković assembled his first temperature and humidity logger for a cucumber greenhouse outside Zrenjanin. Back then the wiring was thick and the boxes were metal and nothing was wireless. Over the years, his sons Miroslav and Teodor joined the workshop, and together we moved to battery-powered wireless nodes that growers can clip to a polytunnel frame or stake into an orchard row without calling an electrician.

Today we design, manufacture, and install custom microclimate sensor nodes for greenhouses and orchards. We build roughly 400 units a year, mostly by hand, in our workshop on the edge of Zrenjanin. Our clients are fruit and vegetable growers across Vojvodina — people like the Horvat family estate near Kikinda and the cooperative run by the Stojanov brothers in Opovo — who need accurate data on temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and canopy conditions without paying for industrial SCADA systems they do not need.

What makes us different is that we stay after the sale. Every node we ship comes with a maintenance contract option, and when something breaks we drive out, not just send a manual. Our team of seven knows every installation we have ever done.

We are a small, family-run operation and we do not pretend otherwise.

name: Agroprerada Kević
products: Roasted red pepper ajvar (standard and hot varieties); Single-fruit jams: plum, quince, apricot, sour cherry; Mixed pickled vegetables in brine (turšija assortment); Quince cheese (membrillo-style solid preserve); Seasonal gift sets for corporate and private orders
tech: Open copper pan batch cooking; Brix refractometer for sugar/solids measurement; Wood-fired and gas-assisted roasting oven for peppers; Hand-peeling and de-seeding line for ajvar production; Glass jar hot-fill and vacuum-seal capping; Brine pH testing with handheld pH meter; Basic stock and order tracking in a spreadsheet (LibreOffice Calc); WooCommerce webshop on shared hosting
challenges: C034-CH1: Our ajvar from this season's red peppers has a noticeably bitter aftertaste that we can't explain — the pepper variety is the same as last year, the roasting time is identical, but about 30% of customers who ordered last year are not reordering and three have mentioned the taste difference explicitly. | C034-CH2: We produce about 4 tonnes of jam per year and our sugar use is rising — we are adding 55% w/w sugar to hit a 65 Brix final product, but customers increasingly ask for reduced-sugar versions and we do not know how to reformulate without losing gelling and shelf stability. | C034-CH3: We want to sell on a major regional online marketplace but their onboarding requires a food safety management plan and HACCP documentation that we have never written and don't know where to start.
plans: Over the next two years Dragoljub and Milena plan to add a reduced-sugar product line and expand the webshop to serve customers in Slovenia and Croatia. They are also considering a small on-site tasting room to support direct sales during the Fruška Gora tourism season.
rd_capacity: The team can dedicate one person (Nikola Kević) roughly one day per week to testing and documentation work alongside an external collaborator, and can provide raw materials and kitchen access for small-scale trials.
past_collaborations: None formal; occasional informal advice from a retired food technologist, Vera Ostojić, who lives nearby and has helped them interpret labelling regulations.
about: Agroprerada Kević has been making preserves in Sremska Mitrovica since 2003, when Dragoljub Kević and his wife Milena started cooking down their orchard surplus in a rented kitchen and selling jars at the Saturday market on Trg Svetog Dimitrija. Two decades later we are still a family business — our son Nikola manages logistics and the online shop, and we have six full-time and two seasonal employees, all from the surrounding villages. Our fruit comes from small growers we have known for years: plum orchards near Laćarak, quince gardens outside Martinci, and pepper fields in the Fruška Gora foothills. We do not use artificial preservatives or thickeners. Every batch of ajvar is roasted and peeled by hand, every jam is cooked in open copper pans and checked with a refractometer before it goes into the jar. Our customers are households who remember what home-made preserves taste like, specialty food shops in Novi Sad and Belgrade, and an increasing number of buyers through our own webshop. We are not the cheapest option on the shelf and we do not try to be. What we offer is traceability — we can tell you which field the peppers came from — and consistency, batch to batch, year to year. That consistency is something we work hard to protect, which is also why we are honest when something is not right and we are actively looking for ways to improve.

name: Indigo Atelier Studio d.o.o.
products: Small-batch women's ready-to-wear collections (spring-summer and autumn-winter, 1,500–2,500 pieces per run); Natural and low-impact dyed woven and knit fabrics sourced from domestic and Hungarian mills; Direct-to-consumer EU webshop with EU-wide delivery; Size-inclusive fit range (EU 34–52, introduced autumn-winter 2023)
tech: Shopify (webshop and order management); Adobe Illustrator and CLO 3D (garment technical drawing and 3D fit preview, limited use); Instagram and TikTok organic content (in-house video and photo); Google Analytics 4 (basic traffic and funnel tracking); Fiber reactive and plant-based low-impact dye processes (outsourced to mill partners); Manual spreadsheet-based bookkeeping (Google Sheets); Email marketing via Klaviyo (basic flows, welcome series and abandoned cart)
challenges: C035-CH1: We launched a size-inclusive line last season and returns are running at 34% — almost all customers say the fit was wrong — which is killing our margin because return shipping from Germany or the Netherlands costs us €6–8 per parcel and we're on a 2,000-piece run. | C035-CH2: Our Instagram and TikTok content drives traffic but we can't convert it — our webshop session-to-purchase rate is 1.2% and the EU average for fashion is around 3.5%; we've changed the layout twice and hired a photographer but nothing moved the needle. | C035-CH3: We want to market our fabrics as 'low environmental impact' but a German wholesale buyer is now asking for a full life-cycle assessment document before they'll list us — we have no idea how to produce one and can't afford a consultancy that quoted us €12,000 for the study. | C035-CH4: We need a seed investment round of €150,000 to fund the next two collections and a warehouse deposit, but three angel investors passed because we don't have audited financials and our bookkeeping is done in a spreadsheet by the founder's partner who has no accounting background.
plans: In 2025 we want to open a small physical showroom in Novi Sad to reduce returns through in-person fit appointments and to host wholesale buyers visiting from the region. We are also exploring a fabric co-sourcing arrangement with two other small Serbian labels to get better mill pricing on shared orders.
rd_capacity: We have no dedicated R&D staff, but our two pattern makers and production coordinator can allocate time to structured tests or pilots if the scope is defined and doesn't pull them fully off active collection work.
past_collaborations: In 2023 we worked informally with a textile technology student group at a local faculty who mapped our dye supplier's process documentation as a course project, but there was no formal agreement and the output was not taken further.
about:
Indigo Atelier Studio d.o.o. was started in 2019 by Marta Vujić and textile designer Petra Oláh in a rented room in Novi Sad's Liman district. The idea was straightforward: make small runs of women's ready-to-wear that are worth keeping for more than one season, sewn from fabrics sourced within a day's drive — domestic mills around Novi Sad and partners across the Hungarian border. We moved into NTP Novi Sad in 2022, which gave us stable workspace and access to people who think about problems differently than we do.

We sell directly to customers across the EU through our own webshop, with the largest markets in Germany, the Netherlands, and Austria. Each collection runs between 1,500 and 2,500 pieces. We don't do trend cycles. We release two collections a year — spring-summer and autumn-winter — and when they're gone, they're gone.

The team is fourteen people: pattern makers, a production coordinator, two marketers, a customer-care person, and the rest split between design and operations. We keep production local, which means slower lead times than fast-fashion competitors but real visibility into who is cutting and sewing each piece.

Our customers tend to find us through social content and stay because the quality holds up. We're not trying to be the cheapest option. We're trying to be the one you don't regret.

name: FreshPak Solutions
products: Thermoformed PET and rPET punnets in 125 g, 250 g and 500 g formats; Sealed lidding films with anti-fog and controlled-atmosphere options; Corrugated and solid-fibre export cartons rated for refrigerated sea and road freight; Printed paper and film labels including QR traceability codes; Custom-cut foam and pulp tray inlays for high-value soft-fruit lines
tech: Single-screw and twin-screw film extrusion; Rotary and shuttle thermoforming; Heat-seal and ultrasonic sealing; Modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) gas-flush trials; Oxygen and CO₂ transmission rate measurement (OTR/CO₂TR benchtop analysers); Seal-strength pull testing to EN 15507; Drop and vibration simulation testing for export carton validation; Basic compostability screening against EN 13432 parameters
challenges: C036-CH1: Raspberries for Germany arrive with mould on day 9; buyers want 14 days. | C036-CH2: Big retailers will stop taking conventional plastic lidding film by 2028; we need a compostable one that still seals.
plans: Compostable range by 2028.
rd_capacity: Quality lab with three technologists.
past_collaborations: Tested packaging with a faculty lab in 2020.
about: FreshPak Solutions was set up in 2012 by two former food-logistics managers, Dragan Kovačević and Marta Ilić, who kept watching Serbian berry exporters lose shipments to bad packaging. We started with a single thermoforming line in a rented hall and a list of about a dozen growers in the Fruška Gora corridor. Twelve years later we have 60 people, three production lines, and a quality lab that runs seal-strength, permeability and drop tests every day. Most of what we make ends up under raspberries, blueberries and sour cherries heading to Germany, Austria and the Netherlands. Our direct customers are packing houses and export cooperatives; we work closely with their agronomists and logistics teams to match packaging spec to cold-chain conditions. What separates us from the large Western suppliers is response time and willingness to run short customised batches. A grower can call on a Tuesday and have trial punnets by Friday. We are not the cheapest, but our reject rate at destination is consistently below two percent, which is what keeps buyers coming back. The next step for us is moving the whole lidding-film range to certified compostable materials before the retail mandates kick in.

name: SolarStep preduzetnik
products: Residential rooftop photovoltaic installation (3 kWp – 12 kWp); Battery storage add-on for new and existing PV systems; Grid-tie inverter supply and commissioning; Annual system health check and panel cleaning; Small agricultural holding electrification packages
tech: Monocrystalline PERC panels (Sunvara 400 W series); Hybrid string inverters (Voltara HV series); Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery modules; PV*SOL Express for basic shading and yield estimates; Victron Energy monitoring via VRM portal; Manual consumption logging from utility bills and smart meter exports; WhatsApp-based customer support and photo fault reporting
challenges: C037-CH1: We size battery storage by rule of thumb — usually 1.2 times the average daily consumption — and about one in five customers ends up with a system that cycles the battery too hard in summer, which degrades it faster than we promised. We need a sizing method we can actually use during a 30-minute site visit. | C037-CH2: We can't get financing to stock more than 20 panels and 4 inverters at a time; the bank wants three years of audited accounts and we only have two. Every time a big order comes in we lose two weeks waiting for supplier delivery.
plans: SolarStep intends to add agrivoltaic installations — panels mounted over polytunnel structures — as a service line by late 2025, starting with two pilot farms in the Zrenjanin municipality. The family also wants to hire a part-time bookkeeper so Milica can spend more time on customer technical follow-up.
rd_capacity: We can offer a cooperating researcher access to our sixty-installation dataset, site visits with customers who have agreed to share monitoring data, and two to three hours a week of staff time for testing and feedback.
past_collaborations: No formal research collaborations to date; Dragan attended a one-day energy storage workshop organised by the Chamber of Commerce in Zrenjanin in 2023.
about:
SolarStep started in 2021 when Dragan Đurić spent a weekend installing a second-hand solar kit on his father's farmhouse outside Zrenjanin and realised that most families in central Vojvodina had no one local to call for this kind of work. He registered as a sole trader, bought a van, and began visiting neighbours. By 2023 the business had grown enough to bring in his wife Milica to handle scheduling and paperwork, his brother-in-law Nenad to help on rooftops, and three more installers from the area. Today SolarStep is a family-run micro-firm of six people serving households, weekend cottages, and small agricultural holdings across the Zrenjanin, Kikinda, and Novi Bečej municipalities.

We do not take on projects we cannot finish properly. Every installation starts with a roof inspection, a look at twelve months of electricity bills if the customer has them, and an honest conversation about what a battery actually does and does not do. We source panels and inverters from a small number of distributors we trust and we stay on site until the system is commissioned and the customer understands the monitoring app. Most of our new customers come from previous customers. That is the measure we care about.

name: TalentMost d.o.o.
products: Competency-profile matching engine for open vacancies; Structured interview builder with automatic scoring guides; Applicant tracking module with vacancy pipeline view; Short cognitive and personality screening battery (beta); Reporting dashboard for time-to-hire and quality-of-shortlist metrics
tech: Python (FastAPI backend); PostgreSQL with pgvector extension; React frontend; spaCy for CV text parsing; Sentence-transformer embeddings for semantic matching; AWS S3 and EC2 (Frankfurt region); Docker and GitHub Actions CI/CD
challenges: C038-CH1: Our matching algorithm ranks candidates well for software roles but performs poorly for skilled-trades positions like CNC operators or maintenance electricians; hiring managers in manufacturing say the top-10 lists are 'basically random' and we're losing three accounts a month over it. | C038-CH2: We want to add a short cognitive and personality screening battery to the platform, but we built the current version ourselves by copying items from free online tests; a prospective German client told us our assessment has no documented reliability or validity evidence and they won't use it. | C038-CH3: We process CVs and interview recordings for candidates in Germany and Austria, which means GDPR applies, but we haven't done a Data Protection Impact Assessment and our privacy policy was written by a junior intern; if a client requests an audit we'd fail immediately. | C038-CH4: We need to hire a senior backend engineer with experience in vector databases to rebuild our matching engine, but we've been advertising the position for four months and every shortlisted candidate has dropped out when a Frankfurt or Vienna company matched their salary expectation.
plans: Over the next twelve months TalentMost intends to reach one hundred active employer accounts in the DACH region and launch a validated version of the screening battery that meets the documentation standards expected by enterprise HR buyers. We are also preparing a seed funding round targeting Serbian and Austrian early-stage investors to support a second engineering hire and localisation of the platform interface into German.
rd_capacity: We can dedicate one mid-level backend developer and our CTO, Dragan Petković, at roughly 30 percent of his time, to support any collaborative research or development work.
past_collaborations: In 2022 we completed a six-month product feedback collaboration with the Vojvodina Employers' Association under a Serbian Innovation Fund voucher scheme, which gave us structured input from eleven manufacturers on competency frameworks for industrial roles.
about:
TalentMost d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2021 by a small team that had spent years watching hiring processes in Vojvodina factories and IT offices run on spreadsheets, gut feeling, and luck. We set out to build something more systematic: a platform that reads what a vacancy actually demands, reads what a candidate can actually do, and puts the two together without the usual noise.

Today we serve around forty employers across northern Serbia, with a growing number of clients in Germany and Austria who need to fill roles in their Serbian-owned subsidiaries or remote teams. Our customers include mid-size manufacturers, logistics operators, and software houses. They use TalentMost to screen applicants, run structured interviews with automatically scored response guides, and compare candidates on a common competency scale.

Our team of nineteen works out of the Science and Technology Park in Novi Sad. Most of us came from software development or industrial HR consulting backgrounds. We deliberately kept the product narrow and practical rather than trying to cover every corner of talent management. What we do, we try to do reliably. We are currently expanding our assessment tooling and improving how the platform handles trades and technical roles in manufacturing. We are funded by an EBRD small-business credit line and a Serbian Innovation Fund proof-of-concept grant.

name: NeuroStep Solutions d.o.o.
products: StrideSense insole pressure sensor system for clinical gait measurement; RehabTrack software platform for gait data visualisation and progress reporting; SymmetryView bilateral gait symmetry analysis module; Remote Calibration Service contract for insole maintenance and quality assurance; Custom sensor integration consulting for rehabilitation equipment manufacturers
tech: Capacitive pressure sensor arrays in flexible insole form factor; Embedded C firmware on ARM Cortex-M4 microcontrollers; Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE 5.0) wireless data transmission; Python-based signal processing pipeline with scikit-learn decision-tree classifier; PostgreSQL database backend for patient session storage; React frontend for RehabTrack web application; HL7 FHIR R4 (currently in evaluation phase); ISO 13485-aligned quality management processes for medical device production
challenges: C039-CH1: Our insole pressure sensors drift by up to 8% over a six-month period in daily clinical use; we recalibrate them manually every three months at a service cost of about €180 per pair, and clients are starting to complain that the calibration windows are too infrequent between visits. | C039-CH2: We want to classify a patient's gait pattern into one of seven rehabilitation progress categories using data from 16 sensor channels at 100 Hz, but our current decision-tree model needs a 90-second walking trial to reach acceptable accuracy; clinicians want a result from a 20-second walk. | C039-CH3: Three rehabilitation hospitals in Slovenia are asking us to integrate with their Dedalus electronic health record system via HL7 FHIR, but none of our three developers has worked with FHIR before and the integration project has already slipped by four months while we look for a consultant who knows both the standard and Serbian healthcare data conventions. | C039-CH4: Patients recovering from stroke show highly asymmetric gait that causes our bilateral symmetry index algorithm to output misleading progress scores — in about 30% of post-stroke cases the score actually improves on paper while the physiotherapist observes functional decline.
plans: Over the next two years NeuroStep Solutions intends to extend its distribution into Bosnia and Herzegovina and to launch a cloud-hosted version of RehabTrack that allows multi-site rehabilitation networks to compare anonymised patient cohort data across facilities. We are also evaluating whether a wrist-worn inertial sensor add-on for upper-limb stroke rehabilitation is a viable product extension.
rd_capacity: Our internal R&D team consists of four engineers and one clinical data analyst who collectively spend roughly 40% of their working time on product development alongside their maintenance and support responsibilities.
past_collaborations: Between 2018 and 2021 NeuroStep Solutions participated in a bilateral Serbia–Austria research exchange with the Fachhochschule Technikum Wien that contributed to the sensor signal processing architecture currently used in StrideSense firmware.
about: NeuroStep Solutions was founded in 2009 by a small team of biomedical engineers and physiotherapists who believed that objective movement data should be at the centre of every rehabilitation decision. Based at the Science and Technology Park in Novi Sad, we design and manufacture sensor-based gait analysis systems used daily by neurological and orthopaedic rehabilitation teams across Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia. Our StrideSense insole system and accompanying RehabTrack software platform give clinicians quantified, repeatable measurements that complement their clinical judgement rather than replace it. Today our 51-person team covers hardware design, embedded firmware, clinical software development and direct field support. We work closely with rehabilitation centres such as the Specijalna bolnica for neurological rehabilitation in Sremska Kamenica and the Ortopedska klinika Sv. Katarina in Zabok. What sets us apart is the combination of in-house sensor manufacturing, on-site clinical training and software that was built from the start around the real conditions of busy rehabilitation wards — not laboratory settings. We are not a startup looking for a first customer; we are a mature product company looking for the right technical partners to help us solve problems that matter to patients recovering from stroke, hip replacement and spinal injury.

name: MedVizion d.o.o.
products: ClearFrame — AI-assisted X-ray and CT review for radiology departments; ClearFrame Bone — fracture detection module for emergency and orthopaedic settings; DICOM Connect — integration middleware for legacy scanner infrastructure; RadReview Dashboard — worklist management and radiologist annotation interface; MDR Compliance Package — documentation and audit-trail tooling for medical device software
tech: Python and PyTorch for model training and inference; DICOM standard and pydicom for image ingestion and metadata handling; Active learning pipeline built on Label Studio and custom queuing logic; Docker and Kubernetes for on-premises hospital deployment; PostgreSQL for study metadata and annotation storage; HL7 FHIR for integration with hospital information systems; EU MDR Class IIa quality management system under ISO 13485; DVC for dataset versioning and experiment tracking
challenges: C040-CH1: Our bone-fracture detection model hits 91% sensitivity on our test set, but when we deploy it at partner hospitals with older Siemens and Philips scanners, sensitivity drops to around 78% — we lose about 13 percentage points just from scanner-to-scanner variation in DICOM metadata and image reconstruction kernels. | C040-CH2: We are trying to close a Series A round of €2.1 million with a German medtech fund, but they want a co-investor from the Western Balkans region and our local bank contacts have no experience structuring equity rounds of this size for software-as-a-medical-device companies. | C040-CH3: Radiologists at our pilot site spend 40 minutes per shift correcting the bounding-box annotations the model generates, because our active-learning pipeline requeues the same ambiguous edge cases repeatedly instead of escalating them to a senior reviewer.

The Series A round, if closed on schedule, will fund an engineering team expansion of six positions and a federated-learning infrastructure project across partner hospitals.
rd_capacity: The engineering team dedicates approximately two days per week to research and experimentation outside of product maintenance, coordinated through a biweekly internal sprint focused on model improvement and infrastructure.
past_collaborations: MedVizion completed a six-month applied research collaboration with a Novi Sad-based signal processing group through the NTP Novi Sad programme in 2021, focused on DICOM preprocessing normalisation, which produced a preprocessing module still used in the current pipeline.
about:
MedVizion d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2017 by a small group of software engineers and radiologists who had grown tired of watching diagnostic backlogs pile up at understaffed hospitals across Central and Eastern Europe. We build AI-assisted imaging software that slots into existing radiology workflows without requiring hospitals to replace their hardware or retrain their entire staff.

Our flagship product, ClearFrame, analyses X-ray and CT studies and flags findings for radiologist review. It runs inside the hospital's own network, connects to standard DICOM infrastructure, and is certified as a Class IIa medical device under EU MDR. Today we work with seven hospital groups across Serbia, Slovakia, and Romania, processing roughly 11,000 studies per month.

The team is 34 people: radiologists, machine-learning engineers, regulatory specialists, and clinical integration consultants. Our medical director, Dr. Milena Horvat, trained in diagnostic radiology in Vienna before returning to Novi Sad. Our head of engineering, Aleksandar Čović, previously built imaging pipelines for a Ljubljana-based teleradiology firm.

What sets us apart is straightforward: we do not sell a black box. Every finding comes with a confidence score, a highlighted region, and a clear path for the radiologist to accept, edit, or reject it. Accountability stays with the clinician, and our software is designed to support that rather than obscure it.

name: TeraRoot d.o.o.
products: RhizoProbe S1 — jednosezonska sonda za korenovu zonu sa elektrohemijskim senzorom impendanse; RhizoGateway — terenski prijemnik koji skuplja podatke sa do 64 sonde i prenosi ih mobilnom mrežom; RhizoDash — veb aplikacija za praćenje zdravlja korena i upozorenja na anomalije u ishrani; Kalibracioni servis po hibridu — terensko testiranje i podešavanje modela za specifičan sortiment; API za integraciju sa farmskim upravljačkim sistemima trećih strana
tech: Elektrohemijska impedansna spektroskopija (EIS) na frekvencijama 1 Hz – 100 kHz; Mikrokontroleri STM32 serije sa niskom potrošnjom energije; LPWAN (LoRaWAN) i NB-IoT prenos podataka s terena; Python i scikit-learn za regresijske modele korelacije signala i biomase korena; InfluxDB za vremenski zasnovane serije podataka sa sondi; React i Node.js za RhizoDash veb aplikaciju; CAD projektovanje kućišta i prototipizacija u sopstvenoj radionici u NTP-u; Destruktivno uzorkovanje korena i referentna gravimetrijska merenja za validaciju modela
challenges: C041-CH1: Our probe electrode corrodes within six to eight weeks in high-clay soils with low pH, which means we have to replace them mid-season at a cost of around €18 per probe; we need a coating or electrode material that survives a full 20-week growing season. | C041-CH2: We are trying to interpret the electrical impedance spectra our probes generate and correlate them with actual root biomass, but our current regression model explains only 51% of the variance when we validate it against destructive sampling — we need a much better signal interpretation approach. | C041-CH3: We want to understand whether root morphology differences between maize hybrids actually affect what our sensor reads, so we can calibrate hybrid-specifically, but we have no agronomic expertise in-house and cannot design a proper field trial ourselves. | C041-CH4: Our probe produces a continuous data stream of about 500 KB per day per probe, and with 600 probes deployed this season we are already over our cloud budget by 40%; we need on-device filtering or compression that keeps agronomically relevant signals but drops noise before transmission.
plans: U toku 2025. planiramo da proširimo mrežu na parcele u Mačvi i južnom Banatu i uvedemo kalibraciju po hibridu za najmanje deset sorti kukuruza. Do kraja 2026. cilj nam je komercijalizacija u Mađarskoj i Rumuniji kroz partnerstvo sa lokalnim distributivnim firmama.
rd_capacity: Razvojni tim od sedam inženjera i jednog agronoma može da vodi do tri paralelna istraživačka zadatka po sezoni, uz pristup terenskim parcelama saradnih gazdinstava i sopstvenoj prototipskoj radionici u NTP-u.
past_collaborations: Tokom 2022. i 2023. sarađivali smo sa firmom AgroSens Solutions d.o.o. iz Subotice na zajedničkom testiranju LoRaWAN mrežne infrastrukture za prenos podataka sa polja.
about: TeraRoot d.o.o. je osnovan 2020. godine kao spin-of projekta koji je trajao tri godine u okviru istraživačke grupe za preciznu poljoprivredu. Smešteni smo u Naučno-tehnološkom parku Novi Sad, gde je ostao i jezgro razvojnog tima. Bavimo se izradom minijaturnih sondi koje farmer umetne u zemlju jednom na početku sezone i koje zatim neprekidno mere stanje korena i dinamiku usvajanja hraniva — bez daljeg rada na terenu. Naši uređaji kombinuju elektrohemijsko merenje impendanse sa termičkim i vlažnim profilisanjem korenske zone. Trenutno radimo sa dvadesetak porodičnih i komercijalnih gazdinstava u Vojvodini, a prve probe su tokom 2023. prošle punu sezonu na kukuruzu i suncokretovim parcelama. Tim čini dvadeset dva zaposlena: hardverski inženjeri, softverski programeri, jedan agronom i nekoliko tehničara za teren. Direktor je Miroslav Kecman, koji je i koautor izvornog istraživačkog rada. Razlikujemo se od konkurencije po tome što naši senzori ostaju in situ tokom cele sezone i daju vremenski neprekinut niz podataka umesto pojedinačnih uzorkovanja. Ne prodajemo platformu sa puno opcija — prodajemo tačno onu informaciju koja govori da li koren funkcioniše onako kako treba.

name: AgroVid Solutions d.o.o.
products: CropView SaaS platform — field-level decision support combining satellite, drone and weather data; Drone scouting service — scheduled and on-demand multispectral flights with same-day report delivery; CropView Field App — mobile companion for in-field scouting, task logging and image capture; Agronomic alert API — machine-readable feed of crop stress and phenology events for third-party farm management systems; Onboarding and training packages for farm cooperatives and agri-input distributors
tech: Python (Flask, Celery) backend with PostgreSQL and PostGIS; React frontend with Leaflet-based field mapping; Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope satellite imagery pipelines; DJI Mavic 3 Multispectral and Autel EVO II Pro drones; MicaSense RedEdge-P multispectral sensor processing via Agisoft Metashape; PyTorch-based computer vision models for canopy segmentation; OpenWeatherMap and ECMWF ERA5 weather data integration; MinIO object storage on-premises at NTP Novi Sad
challenges: C042-CH1: Our drone flight planning tool re-routes missions in the field, but the algorithm becomes very slow once a single farm exceeds 80 parcels — a pilot with 120 parcels told us last month it took 11 minutes to replan after a no-fly zone appeared, which is completely unusable. | C042-CH2: We collect multispectral imagery at 5 cm resolution, but when we try to automatically delineate individual plant rows in maize and sunflower, our segmentation model produces 15–20% row-skip errors on fields with uneven emergence, and agronomists have to correct it by hand every time. | C042-CH3: We want to expand into Hungary and Romania next year but our legal team says we need separate data-processing agreements and potentially different operator licences for drone flights in each country, and we simply don't have the in-house legal resource to handle that.
plans: AgroVid plans to launch CropView in Hungary and Romania by Q3 2025, beginning with cooperative and agri-input distributor partnerships in each market. In parallel the team is building out an automated field health reporting feature that would deliver weekly PDF summaries to farm managers without requiring them to log into the platform.
rd_capacity: We have one dedicated R&D engineer for computer vision, one for backend data pipelines, and can involve senior agronomists for domain review, but we do not have a formal research budget line — most development time is carved out of the product roadmap on a project basis.
past_collaborations: AgroVid completed a six-month applied research project in 2022 with the Faculty of Agriculture in Novi Sad covering soil moisture modelling inputs for the CropView irrigation alert module, which led to one co-authored technical report.
about:
AgroVid Solutions d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2017 by a small team of agricultural engineers and software developers who had spent years working with arable farms across the Western Balkans and were tired of watching growers make expensive decisions based on incomplete information. We moved into NTP Novi Sad early on and have been based there ever since.

Our platform, CropView, combines satellite imagery, drone-collected multispectral data and localised weather feeds into a single dashboard that helps arable farmers decide when to scout, spray, irrigate or harvest at the level of individual fields — not whole farms. Today we serve roughly 340 active farm subscribers across Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and North Macedonia, covering a combined area of around 190,000 hectares of maize, sunflower, wheat and soybean.

We have 34 people in-house: agronomists, remote sensing specialists, backend and frontend engineers, and a small drone operations team. Our customers are not hobby growers — they run commercial arable operations between 200 and 4,000 hectares and expect the tool to save them real time and reduce input costs. Our renewal rate last season was 88 percent. We are not the biggest platform in the region, but we are the one that actually works in the field conditions farmers here deal with every day.

name: KartografTech preduzetnik
products: HD putna baza podataka za Srbiju, BiH i Crnu Goru u vlasničkom binarnom formatu; ADAS slojevi mape: geometrija traka, nagib, krivina i saobraćajna signalizacija; Licenciranje mapa za aftermarket navigacione uređaje (godišnja pretplata); Konverzija i isporuka mape u prilagođenim formatima po narudžbini; Terenska survej usluga za treće strane na celoj mreži Zapadnog Balkana
