challenges: C043-CH1: We update our road geometry database by driving survey vehicles ourselves; one full national pass takes four months and costs us around €60,000, which means our maps can be a year out of date when clients use them — new roundabouts and road closures are missing and clients complain. | C043-CH2: Three clients want map data in OpenDRIVE format for simulator use, but all our data is in a proprietary binary format and the conversion tool we built in-house produces lane-boundary errors at about 2% of intersections, which is unacceptable for ADAS simulation. | C043-CH3: We have been trying to raise a €400,000 seed round for 18 months; every investor we talk to says the addressable market in the Western Balkans is too small and wants to see a path to selling into the EU, but we do not have the sales connections or the brand recognition to open those doors on our own.
plans: U toku 2025. planiramo da proširimo bazu podataka na putnu mrežu Severne Makedonije i pokrenemo pilot survej u Albaniji. Paralelno, ako uspemo da rešimo konverziju u OpenDRIVE, nameravamo da ponudimo ADAS mape kao posebnu liniju proizvoda za simulacione kompanije u regionu.
rd_capacity: Jedan softverski inženjer i jedan od osnivača mogu da odvoje ukupno oko deset radnih sati nedeljno za razvojne projekte koji nisu direktno vezani za tekuće narudžbine.
past_collaborations: 2022. godine imali smo kratku tehničku saradnju sa firmom Geomatika Plus d.o.o. iz Novog Sada oko razmene GNSS kalibracijskih podataka, ali formalni sporazum nije sklopljen.
about: KartografTech je mali porodični studio sa sedištem u Zrenjaninu, osnovan 2019. godine. Počeli smo sa jednim terenskim vozilom i jednim jasnim ciljem: da proizvođačima aftermarket navigacionih uređaja na tržištu Zapadnog Balkana ponudimo precizne, licencirane HD mape koje velika međunarodna imena nisu smatrala dovoljno isplativim da ažuriraju. Danas imamo šest zaposlenih, dva survej vozila i bazu podataka koja pokriva putnu mrežu Srbije, Bosne i Hercegovine i Crne Gore. Naši klijenti su kompanije poput Veltron Navigation d.o.o. iz Beograda, Adria Drive Systems iz Sarajeva i Podgorica Auto Electronics – firme koje ugrađuju navigacione sisteme u vozila srednje i niže klase i kojima su tačnost i ažurnost mape važniji od brendova. Tim čine dva kartografa, jedan softverski inženjer, jedan terinski vozač-tehničar i dva osnivača koji rade sve ostalo. Ono po čemu se razlikujemo od posrednika koji preprodaju globalne izvore jeste to da mi sami vozimo puteve, sami merimo i sami isporučujemo – bez posrednika i bez podataka koji su nastali snimanjem iz orbite pre tri godine. Cilj nam je da u narednom periodu proširimo pokrivenost na Severnu Makedoniju i Albaniju.

name: Orbis Edukacija d.o.o.
products: OrbisČitanje / OrbisOlvasás — bilingual reading-comprehension app for grades 1–4; OrbisMatematika / OrbisMatemtika — bilingual numeracy exercise modules for grades 1–3; Printed bilingual workbook sets aligned to the Serbian national curriculum; School licensing portal for managing pupil accounts and tracking progress; Teacher dashboard with per-pupil performance reports in both languages
tech: Flutter (cross-platform mobile development); Unity (3D interactive scenes in reading app); Firebase (authentication, real-time database, analytics); Python scripts for content pipeline and automated exercise generation; Google Sheets + custom export scripts for curriculum mapping; Adobe Illustrator and Spine for 2D character animation; Android (primary target platform, API level 21+)
challenges: C044-CH1: Our reading-comprehension exercises work fine in Serbian, but the Hungarian-language versions consistently get poor scores from teachers — we don't know whether the problem is vocabulary level, sentence complexity or the way we sequence tasks, and we have no systematic way to test that. | C044-CH2: Schools want to use our app on the cheap Android tablets they already own, but our 3D interactive scenes lag badly on anything below a Snapdragon 665 — we need to rework the rendering pipeline but nobody on our four-person dev team has done GPU optimisation before. | C044-CH3: We applied for an Innovation Fund Serbia voucher in March; we still have no answer after five months and our bridge financing runs out in two months — the accountant says the application had a formal error we can't correct at this stage.
plans: We plan to expand the reading app to cover grades 5 and 6 by the end of 2025, adding more complex texts and a vocabulary-tracking feature. We are also in early talks with one municipality about a pilot that would cover all public primary schools in their territory under a single annual licence.
rd_capacity: We can dedicate roughly one curriculum specialist and one developer to a collaborative project at any given time, with the rest of the team continuing regular product work.
past_collaborations: We worked with the Subotica-based educational publisher Napút Kiadó d.o.o. between 2021 and 2022 to align our Hungarian-language content with their printed textbook series, which are already approved for use in Vojvodina schools.
about:
Orbis Edukacija d.o.o. was founded in Subotica in 2019 by the Fehér family, who noticed that primary school children in Vojvodina had very few digital learning materials that treated Serbian and Hungarian as equals rather than treating one language as a translation of the other. We build interactive apps and printed exercise packs that let children switch between the two languages naturally, matching the way they actually speak at home and in class.

Our customers are primary schools across Vojvodina, mostly in municipalities with mixed Serbian–Hungarian populations: Subotica, Kanjiža, Senta, Ada, and several villages around them. About 4,200 pupils used our materials in the 2023–24 school year, across 31 schools. Teachers tell us they appreciate that the content was written by people who grew up speaking both languages, not by a translation agency.

The team is eleven people: four in software development, two curriculum specialists who both have classroom experience, two graphic designers, one sales and partnerships person, and two in administration and finance. We work closely with a small network of freelance educators who review and pilot every module before release.

What makes us different is not technology for its own sake. We keep our interface simple enough for a seven-year-old to use without adult help, and we test every exercise with real classrooms before it ships.

name: Adrialink Technologies a.d.
sector: Custom software and IT services for EU clients
products: Managed cloud operations for financial-sector workloads; Legacy mainframe and monolith modernisation; Staff augmentation and embedded engineering teams; Application testing and quality assurance services; IT compliance and reporting support for regulated clients
tech: Java (Spring Boot, Spring Cloud); COBOL and IBM Z mainframe tooling; Kubernetes and Helm on AWS and Azure; PostgreSQL and Oracle Database; Terraform for infrastructure as code; Jenkins and GitLab CI/CD pipelines; Grafana and Prometheus for observability; JIRA and Confluence for project tracking
challenges: C045-CH1: We are migrating a Belgian insurance client from COBOL mainframe to a microservices stack, but automated test coverage sits at only 34% and manual regression takes three weeks per release cycle — the client wants monthly releases by Q1 next year. | C045-CH2: Hiring senior Java architects in Novi Sad is impossible right now — we have eight open positions, three projects delayed, and the salaries candidates ask for are 40% above our grade bands. | C045-CH3: Our cloud cost for EU clients jumped 28% last quarter because workload autoscaling decisions are made purely on CPU thresholds — we need smarter scheduling that considers time-of-day patterns and cross-service dependencies. | C045-CH4: Two of our biggest clients are asking us to provide a carbon footprint report for the IT services we run on their behalf — we have no methodology or tooling to do this and the first deadline is September.
plans: Adrialink intends to grow its managed services revenue from Dutch and German financial clients by 20% over the next two years, with particular focus on cloud-native migration projects. The company is also evaluating whether to open a small delivery centre in Subotica to access a wider regional talent pool.
rd_capacity: We do not have a formal R&D department, but a team of four senior engineers works on internal tooling and process improvement roughly 20% of their time, and we occasionally co-develop solutions with technology partners when there is a clear production use case.
past_collaborations: Adrialink completed a six-month tooling project with Synergy Lab d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based data engineering firm, in 2021 to build an internal data pipeline framework used in two of our banking client environments.
about:
Adrialink Technologies a.d. has been building and running software for European businesses since 1998, when three engineers from Novi Sad decided there was a real market for reliable IT services delivered from Vojvodina. Twenty-six years later, we employ 312 people across offices in Novi Sad, Belgrade, and Rotterdam, and we run production systems for banks, insurance companies, and asset managers in Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, and Austria.

Most of our work falls into three areas: taking over and modernising legacy systems that clients no longer want to maintain themselves, managing cloud infrastructure on their behalf, and supplying experienced engineers who work as part of client teams. We are not a consultancy that hands over a report and leaves — we stay on and operate what we build.

Our clients tend to be mid-to-large financial institutions that need a long-term partner rather than a short-term vendor. The average client relationship at Adrialink lasts nine years. We attribute that to straightforward communication, documented processes, and a policy of never overpromising on delivery timelines.

The technical team includes Java and Python engineers, platform engineers, database specialists, and business analysts who understand financial regulation. Leadership has been stable: CEO Miroslav Gajić and CTO Dragana Kovačević have both been with the company for over fifteen years.

about: Nordatik Solutions was founded in 2011 by a small group of software engineers who had spent years working on contract for Nordic companies and wanted to build something more permanent in Novi Sad. Today we are a team of 87 people delivering custom web and mobile applications, backend integrations, and cloud infrastructure to retail and logistics clients across Scandinavia, primarily in Denmark, Sweden, and Norway. Our clients are mid-market companies that need reliable delivery partners in a compatible time zone, without the overhead of a large consultancy. We work in long-running engagements, typically twelve to twenty-four months, embedded in our clients' product cycles rather than operating as a vendor at arm's length. Our engineering teams are organised around client verticals, with dedicated squads for e-commerce platforms, warehouse management integrations, and last-mile delivery tooling. Over the past three years we have built a DevOps practice that now covers CI/CD pipeline design, cloud cost management, and on-call runbook automation. We are not the cheapest option in the region and we do not try to be. We invest in retention, internal tooling, and code quality reviews because that is what keeps clients renewing. Our average client relationship is four and a half years.

name: GridSense Analytics
products: GridSense Assets — asset register and equipment lifecycle management for distribution operators; GridSense Outage — real-time and historical outage dashboards with root-cause tagging; GridSense Network Planner — load-flow scenario tool for medium-voltage network planning; GridSense DataBridge — ETL connectors that pull SCADA, meter and inspection data into a unified store
tech: Python; TimescaleDB; PostgreSQL with PostGIS; Azure (App Service, Blob Storage, Azure Data Factory); React; FastAPI; Grafana; Docker and Docker Compose
challenges: C047-CH1: Operators want to know which distribution transformers will fail next year; they have dissolved gas analysis results and load data, but no model. | C047-CH2: Rooftop PV is changing feeder loads; operators need a day-ahead forecast per feeder.
plans: A predictive maintenance module in 2027.

about:
GridSense Analytics was founded in Novi Sad in 2017 by a small group of engineers who had spent years working on operational software for electricity distribution companies across the Western Balkans. We noticed that most operators were still managing their networks with spreadsheets and aging GIS tools that could not talk to each other. We built GridSense Assets to fix that: a structured asset register that connects equipment records, inspection histories, and network topology in one place. From there we added outage dashboards so that control room staff could move from phone calls and paper logs to a single screen showing what broke, when, and why.

Our customers are electricity distribution operators in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. They run networks that are ageing faster than capital budgets allow, and they need software that works inside the procurement and regulatory constraints of public utilities, not software designed for liberalised Western European markets. That practical focus is what keeps customers like Elektro Morava d.o.o. and Distribucija Podrinlje coming back.

Today we are a team of thirty-one people in the NTP Novi Sad building, mostly software and data engineers with backgrounds in power systems. One of our engineers holds a PhD in electrical engineering. We do not chase every trend. We focus on distribution networks, we learn the business deeply, and we build tools that operators actually use on a Monday morning.

Razmatramo i pilot projekat s jednom zadrugom za postavljanje guste mreže od dvadeset stanica na jednom posedu radi testiranja lokalne mikroklimatske varijabilnosti.
rd_capacity: Marko Veselinović posvećuje otprilike trećinu radnog vremena razvoju firmvera i portala, ali nemamo formalnog istraživačkog procesa niti poseban budžet za razvoj odvojen od redovnih operacija.
past_collaborations: Nismo imali formalne saradnje s istraživačkim institucijama; jednom smo konzultovali tehničara iz Poljoprivredne škole u Somboru oko kalibracije senzora vlažnosti, ali bez zvaničnog ugovora.
about:
Agrosan IoT preduzetnik osnovan je 2021. godine u Somboru, kao porodična firma oca i sina Dragoljuba i Marka Veselinovića. Počeli smo od jedne garaže i petnaest prototipskih mernih stanica postavljenih na njivama naših komšija u okolini Sombora. Tri godine kasnije isporučili smo više od 280 stanica zadrugama i porodičnim gazdinstvima širom zapadne Vojvodine — od Apatina do Kule i Odžaka.

Bavimo se sklapanjem i prodajom robusnih stanica za praćenje uslova u otvorenom polju: merimo temperaturu zemljišta, vlažnost vazduha, količinu padavina i intenzitet sunčevog zračenja. Svaka stanica radi autonomno na solarnom napajanju i šalje podatke jednom mobilnom aplikacijom ili web portalom koji sami razvijamo i održavamo.

Naši kupci su uglavnom zemljoradničke zadruge i veća porodična gazdinstva koja žele pouzdane lokalne podatke, a ne prognoze sa meteorološke stanice udaljene dvadesetak kilometara. Trudimo se da svaki uređaj bude što jednostavniji za montažu i zamenu delova — farmer ne treba da zna ništa o elektronici da bi ga postavio na međe.

Tim trenutno čine Dragoljub, Marko i četiri stalna saradnika koji se bave sklapanjem, testiranjem i tehničkom podrškom. Mali smo, ali sve radimo sami i znamo svaki zavar i svaki konektor na svakom uređaju koji izlazi iz naše radionice.

name: Kadrovski Servis Vojvodina d.o.o.
products: Monthly payroll processing and contribution filing; Employment contract preparation and template management; Workforce planning consultancy for small businesses; HR document archive and client portal access; Labour-law compliance advisory retainer
tech: Microsoft Excel for payroll calculation worksheets; Microsoft Word for contract template management; Custom-built client portal (PHP, MySQL, developed 2017); Email and shared network folders for document exchange; Serbian Tax Administration e-portal (ePorezi) for contribution filing; Printed and scanned document workflow for contract sign-off; Google Drive for internal file sharing
challenges: C049-CH1: We process payroll for 420 client companies manually in Excel; we make on average three miscalculations per month that result in corrections and one formal complaint per quarter — we know we need automation but none of us are developers. | C049-CH2: The new amendments to the Serbian Labour Law that came into force in March changed 14 articles we reference directly in our standard contract templates, and we had to update them by hand over two weeks; we need a smarter way to track regulatory changes and flag which templates are affected. | C049-CH3: Three of our largest clients have asked us to add an employee wellbeing survey module to our portal so they can meet ESG reporting requirements by 2026, but we have no idea how to design a psychometrically valid questionnaire or what to do with the scores.
plans: We intend to gradually replace our Excel-based payroll workflow with a more reliable automated system over the next two years, starting with the highest-volume client accounts. We would also like to extend our portal with document e-signature capability to remove the last paper steps from our contract process.
rd_capacity: We have no dedicated research or development staff, but Jelena Đurić-Kovač can commit approximately four to six hours per week to a structured collaboration, and one junior administrator can assist with data preparation and testing.
past_collaborations: We worked briefly with a local accounting software vendor, Softver za Računovodstvo Panonija d.o.o., in 2021 to evaluate whether their payroll module could replace our Excel system, but the project was not completed after the vendor changed ownership.
about:
Kadrovski Servis Vojvodina d.o.o. has been helping small businesses in Vojvodina manage their workforce obligations since 1998. The firm was founded in Zrenjanin by Miroslav Đurić, a former labour-law practitioner who saw that most small employers in the region were struggling to keep up with payroll rules and employment legislation on their own. Today his daughter Jelena Đurić-Kovač leads the company alongside a team of ten specialists in payroll processing, contract drafting and workforce planning.

Our clients are small and medium-sized businesses — shops, workshops, transport firms, agricultural cooperatives and service providers — mostly across Vojvodina, from Subotica down to Pančevo. We handle the paperwork so they can focus on running their operations. We prepare employment contracts, process monthly payroll, file the required contributions, and advise on headcount planning when a client is growing or restructuring.

What makes us different is that we have stayed close to the detail. Every client file is handled by a named person on our team, not a call centre. Miroslav still reviews complex contract cases personally. We are not a software platform; we are a small firm with genuine labour-law expertise, and our clients have stayed with us for an average of nine years. We are based in Zrenjanin but travel regularly to clients across the region.

name: MojaKutija Commerce d.o.o.
products: Outsourced pick-and-pack fulfillment for e-commerce parcels; Bonded warehousing and inventory management; MojaVitrina white-label webshop platform; Customs documentation and EU export paperwork service; Returns handling and carrier claims management
tech: Custom warehouse management system (WMS) built on Laravel/PHP; MojaVitrina storefront platform (Vue.js frontend, REST API); Zebra ZPL label printers and Brother packing-slip printers; DPD, GLS and DHL API integrations for carrier booking; Barcode scanning with Honeywell handheld scanners; Google Sheets and manual daily planning spreadsheets for staffing; WooCommerce plugin bridge for client stores not yet on MojaVitrina; Basic stock-level alerts via email triggers in the WMS
challenges: C050-CH1: We pack between 600 and 2,200 parcels per day depending on campaigns; the swing is hard to predict so we either overstaff or rush. If we could forecast daily order volume five days ahead with reasonable accuracy we could plan temporary labour and packaging material orders properly and cut our labour cost overrun, currently about €8,000 a month. | C050-CH2: Several of our clients ship fragile ceramic and glassware; breakage claims average 2.1% of shipments. We design packaging inserts ourselves without any engineering knowledge, and we suspect the cushioning is wrong for the parcel drop heights that couriers actually produce. | C050-CH3: The EU General Product Safety Regulation that comes into force in 2024 requires us to have a responsible economic operator registered in the EU for all non-EU brands we handle. We currently have none, and our legal advisor in Novi Sad says this is outside her expertise. | C050-CH4: We print shipping labels, packing slips and customs invoices on three different printers from two vendors; about 4% of print jobs fail silently and the parcel goes out without a label or with a blank customs form, which triggers returns from German customs. We need a unified, error-checked print workflow.
plans: In the next 12 months MojaKutija intends to add a second shift to extend dispatch cut-off to 18:00 and expand the client base to 40 active brands. We are also evaluating a small cross-docking point in Budapest to shorten last-mile transit times into Central Europe.
rd_capacity: We have one full-time backend developer and one part-time data analyst who can dedicate time to a collaboration, but we have no formal research function.
past_collaborations: We completed a short digitisation project in 2022 with Fabrička Rešenja d.o.o., a local systems integrator, to migrate our inventory records from spreadsheets into the current WMS, but have not worked with a university or research institution before.
about:
MojaKutija Commerce d.o.o. was founded in 2019 by Milena Đorđević and Rastko Vukić, two former online retail managers who kept watching small Serbian makers struggle to reach buyers in Germany, Austria and Slovenia. The idea was straightforward: give artisan brands the same warehousing and webshop infrastructure that large retailers take for granted, without asking those brands to invest in their own logistics.

Today we run a 2,400-square-metre fulfillment centre at NTP Novi Sad, where 41 staff receive stock, photograph products, manage inventory and dispatch parcels across the EU. Our clients are mostly independent producers of ceramics, textiles, cosmetics and specialty food — businesses with ten to sixty employees that have a strong product but no time to argue with couriers.

We handle the full chain: bonded storage, pick-and-pack, customs paperwork, carrier booking and returns processing. On the technology side we offer a white-label webshop platform, MojaVitrina, which clients brand as their own. Orders flow automatically into our warehouse management system, so a buyer in Hamburg places an order and a box leaves Novi Sad the same afternoon.

What separates us from general freight forwarders is that we know small-batch goods. We build custom inserts for fragile items, we print multi-language packing slips, and we speak to our clients in plain language about what each EU market actually requires. Our team is small enough that the founders still walk the floor every morning.

name: PeloTrack Solutions a.d.

challenges: C051-CH1: Our route recommendation engine works well on flat terrain but dramatically underestimates physical effort on the Fruška Gora ridge trails — cyclists rated those routes as 40% harder than we predicted, which is causing churn among the athletic segment of users. | C051-CH2: Our GPS antenna assembly line has a manual calibration step that takes 4.5 minutes per unit and is the bottleneck; we produce 600 units a week but could sell 900 if we could cut that to under 90 seconds. | C051-CH3: We are trying to raise a Series A round of €2.8 million from a Vienna-based impact fund but our three-year financial projections have been rejected twice because the reviewers say our unit-economics model is not structured to institutional investor standards. | C051-CH4: Municipalities that license our trail portal want to embed it in their official tourism websites with full white-label branding, but our current map rendering pipeline takes 3–4 seconds to load a 50 km trail segment on mobile, and page-abandon rates on municipal sites are already at 67%.
plans: PeloTrack intends to release the CycloNav X5 device in early 2026, incorporating improved battery management and an updated antenna design, pending resolution of the current assembly bottleneck. In parallel the company plans to expand TrailPortal licensing into Slovenia and expand its municipal client base from 28 to 50 by end of 2026, which depends in part on closing the Series A round.
rd_capacity: We have four software developers and one electronics engineer who can dedicate time to collaborative projects, typically working in focused sprints of six to ten weeks alongside an external partner.
past_collaborations: Between 2019 and 2021 PeloTrack worked with the Subotica Chamber of Commerce on a co-funded trail-mapping survey project that resulted in 1,200 km of verified GPX data now used as the base layer of TrailPortal.
about: PeloTrack Solutions a.d. was founded in Subotica in 1998 by the Halász family as a small GPS hardware repair workshop serving cross-border freight companies. Over the following decade the business shifted toward leisure cycling, a growing market in Vojvodina, and by 2008 the company had released its first purpose-built cycling computer. A management buyout in 2015 brought in outside shareholders and a new board, though two members of the founding family still hold senior roles. Today PeloTrack employs 112 people across hardware assembly, software development, sales and customer support, all operating from a single facility on the industrial edge of Subotica. Our GPS cycling computers and the TrailPortal subscription platform are used by more than 340 tour operators and 28 municipalities across Vojvodina, northern Croatia and eastern Hungary. Customers rely on us because we know the terrain — the flat canal paths, the Fruška Gora ridge, the Dráva riverside corridors — and we have spent years collecting elevation, surface and seasonal data that generic mapping providers simply do not have. Our hardware is assembled in-house, which lets us control quality and turnaround. We are not the cheapest option on the market; we are the option that works correctly for the geography we cover.

name: NebulaFly Agro a.d.
products: Usluga preciznog prskanja pesticide i fungicide dronom po hektaru; Multispektralno snimanje i kartiranje stanja useva; Usluga setvom dronom za pokrovne i manje useve; Sezonski paket nadzora za žitarice i suncokret; Izrada vegetacijskih karata (NDVI, NDRE) sa preporukom tretmana
tech: Fiksnorilne i višerotorne bespilotne letelice sopstvene konfiguracije; Multispektralne kamere Fenix MS-6 (6-kanalni senzor); Upravljački softver za autonomne misije baziran na ArduPilot platformi; QGIS za planiranje letnih ruta i geoprostornu analizu; Python skripte za obradu vegetacijskih indeksa; RTK GPS (Harpos R2 bazna stanica) za precizno pozicioniranje; Sistemi za precizno doziranje tečnosti sa PWM regulacijom protoka; Interni portal za izveštavanje klijenata sa georeferenciiranim kartama
challenges: C052-CH1: Our spraying drones apply pesticide at a flat 120-litre-per-hectare rate regardless of crop density, and agronomists are telling us that we are over-applying in sparse zones by as much as 35% — we need the drone to adjust flow rate on the fly based on the canopy it sees beneath it. | C052-CH2: We flew 9,400 hectares last season but our flight path planning is still done manually in QGIS by one person — during peak season in May we are turning away clients because planning is the bottleneck, not aircraft or pilots. | C052-CH3: We raised a Series A of €2.1 million last year and the lead investor is now pushing us to show a clear path to profitability in the Hungarian and Slovak markets within 18 months — we need a proper financial model and go-to-market analysis but we don't have anyone internally who can build it. | C052-CH4: After a heavy rain the drone landing gear and underbelly pick up clay-heavy Vojvodina soil and the residue clogs the spray nozzles within one sortie — we are stopping flights to clean every 45 minutes in wet conditions and that is unacceptable.
plans: NebulaFly Agro planira da u sezoni 2025. proširi operacije na tržište centralne Mađarske i uvede paket usluga zasnovan na pretplati za gazdinstva sa više od 500 hektara. U trogodišnjem horizontu cilj je sertifikacija letelica prema EASA SAIL III kategoriji radi pružanja usluga i u ostalim zemljama EU.
rd_capacity: Imamo internu grupu od četiri inženjera koji se bave integracijom senzora i adaptacijom firmware-a za letelice, ali nemamo istraživački tim niti iskustvo u akademskoj saradnji.
past_collaborations: Kratka tehnička konsultacija sa jednim privatnim institutom za zaštitu bilja u Novom Sadu 2022. godine oko protokola kalibracije mlaznica, bez formalnog ugovora.
about: NebulaFly Agro a.d. osnovana je 2019. godine u Subotici sa jednim ciljem: da velikim ratarskim gazdinstvima u severnoj Vojvodini ponudi preciznu agrotehničku uslugu iz vazduha koja je pouzdanija i ekonomičnija od konvencionalnih prizemnih mašina. Danas imamo 118 zaposlenih, flotu fiksnih i višerotornih bespilotnih letelica i prošlu sezonu završili smo sa 9.400 obrađenih hektara. Naši klijenti su pretežno velika porodična gazdinstva i agrarna preduzeća na prostoru između Subotice, Sombora i Kikinde, a deo usluge pružamo i farmama u pograničnom pojasu Mađarske. Osnivač i direktor Branko Vukelić dolazi iz agrotehnike, dok tehnički direktor Maja Horváth ima iskustvo u integraciji senzora i upravljačkih sistema za letelice. Tim je podeljen na odeljenje letenja, odeljenje za obradu podataka i manji tim za tehničko održavanje. Ono što nas razlikuje nije sama letelica nego kombinacija multispektralne snimke, analitike i primenjene usluge prskanja i setve u jednom paketu — klijent ne kupuje opremu, plaća uslugu po hektaru. Podatke sa svakog leta čuvamo i vraćamo farmeru u obliku georeferencirane karte stanja useva.

name: AquaCikl d.o.o.
products: Closed-loop greywater recycling systems for industrial laundries; Process-water treatment and reuse units for food-processing plants; Remote monitoring and compliance reporting service; Annual maintenance and reagent supply contracts; Feasibility and water-audit studies for greenfield industrial sites
tech: Coagulation and flocculation with polyaluminium chloride and ferric sulphate; Multimedia sand and anthracite filtration; Activated carbon adsorption; Spiral-wound reverse-osmosis membranes; UV disinfection units; SCADA-based remote monitoring via OPC-UA; Sludge dewatering with belt-press equipment; On-site photometric water quality analysers for turbidity, pH, and conductivity
challenges: C053-CH1: Our treated greywater consistently fails the manganese and iron limits set by the new Serbian industrial discharge regulation — we're seeing 0.18 mg/L manganese where the limit is 0.10 mg/L — and we don't know whether the problem is in our coagulation step or something upstream in the client's process. | C053-CH2: We currently size every new recycling unit by hand using spreadsheets and conservative safety factors, which means we over-engineer by roughly 25–30% on capital cost and lose bids to cheaper competitors; we need a fast, reliable simulation tool we can run during a sales call. | C053-CH3: Three food-plant clients have asked us to handle their process sludge as part of the same contract, but we have no licence to transport or treat hazardous waste and the permitting process through the Vojvodina Provincial Secretariat has already taken 14 months with no end in sight. | C053-CH4: Biofilm builds up inside our stainless steel holding tanks within six to eight weeks of commissioning, raising our clients' microbiological counts above 100 CFU/mL and forcing emergency chlorination that damages the downstream reverse-osmosis membranes; we need to understand which microbial consortia are responsible and how to suppress them without continuous biocide dosing.
plans: AquaCikl intends to expand its service territory into northern Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina over the next three years, targeting industrial parks that are preparing for stricter EU-alignment discharge standards. In parallel, the company is evaluating a small pilot of constructed wetland post-treatment as a low-energy polishing step for manganese and nutrients.
rd_capacity: The company has no formal R&D department but can dedicate two senior process engineers and one lab technician to a defined project for up to four months, with access to three operating installations for field testing.
past_collaborations: AquaCikl completed a six-month applied project with a Novi Sad-based engineering consultancy, Fluidex inženjering d.o.o., in 2020 to evaluate alternative filter media for iron removal, resulting in a revised filter specification used in subsequent builds.
about:
AquaCikl d.o.o. was founded in 2011 by a small group of process engineers who believed that industrial water could be treated as a resource rather than a cost. Based in Novi Sad, we design, install, and operate closed-loop greywater recycling systems for industrial laundries and food-processing facilities across Vojvodina and the wider region. Over thirteen years we have commissioned more than forty installations, typically achieving 60 to 80 percent water reuse per site and cutting clients' municipal water bills by a measurable amount from the first billing cycle.

Our clients include mid-size laundry operators, poultry processing plants, and vegetable-washing lines that face tightening discharge limits and rising water tariffs. Each system is designed around the client's actual effluent profile: we sample, we model, and we build to fit.

The company employs 47 people, roughly half of whom work on-site as commissioning and service technicians. Our in-house team covers process chemistry, mechanical and electrical installation, and compliance documentation. Day-to-day operations are led by director Miroslav Čobanović and technical manager Dragana Feješ, who joined in 2016 from a municipal water utility.

What makes us different is that we stay involved after handover. Every system we operate is monitored remotely, and we carry out quarterly physical audits. When something drifts out of spec, we find out before the client does.

plans: Nova generacija stanica sa kamerom 2027.
rd_capacity: Dva inženjera hardvera.
past_collaborations: Diplomski radovi studenata FTN-a.
about: Polje Senzor je osnovano 2021. godine u Naučno-tehnološkom parku Novi Sad od strane trojice inženjera koji su prethodno radili na industrijskim mernim sistemima. Primetili smo da voćari u Vojvodini i Šumadiji donose odluke o zaštiti useva na osnovu vremenskih prognoza sa interneta, a ne na osnovu stvarnih uslova u svom voćnjaku. To smo hteli da promenimo. Naša osnovna linija proizvoda je PS-Orchard stanica – kompaktni bežični uređaj koji meri temperaturu vazduha, vlažnost lista i padavine direktno između redova jabuka, krušaka ili bresaka. Podaci idu preko LoRaWAN mreže do naše cloud platforme, a voćar dobija SMS ili push obaveštenje kada postoji rizik od mraza. Danas imamo oko trideset aktivnih korisnika, uglavnom porodična gazdinstva između pet i pedeset hektara, od kojih su neki preporučeni od strane Dragana Milovića iz Savetodavne službe u Sremskoj Mitrovici. Tim čini devet ljudi: dvojica hardverskih inženjera, dva programera, jedna osoba za podršku korisnicima i ostali. Nismo velika firma i ne pretvaramo se da jesmo – svaku stanicu pre isporuke ručno testiramo tri dana.

name: Roboteks d.o.o.

challenges: C055-CH1: Our welding robots drift by up to 2 mm over a single shift due to thermal expansion of the fixture, and we recalibrate manually every four hours — that alone costs us roughly 800 production minutes per week across three customer sites. | C055-CH2: We quote every new cell integration from scratch; our estimators spend 10–15 days per tender and we still lose about 30% of bids because our price is unpredictable — sometimes we over-quote, sometimes we bleed money. | C055-CH3: We want to expand to Germany and Austria but our CE documentation for machine safety is incomplete and we've had two audit failures this year; a local lawyer can't help because the Machinery Directive interpretation requires technical expertise we don't have in-house.
plans: Roboteks intends to open a small service and sales office in Germany by the end of 2026, initially to support two pilot customer installations. Domestically, we are investing in a larger acceptance-testing floor in Novi Sad to allow two full cells to run simultaneously before delivery.

about: Roboteks d.o.o. has been building and integrating industrial robotic systems since 1994, when Dragan Kovačević founded the company in a rented workshop on the outskirts of Novi Sad. Thirty years later, his son Nikola Kovačević runs day-to-day operations alongside a team of 47 engineers, programmers, and field technicians. We design, assemble, and commission turnkey robotic welding and material-handling cells, primarily for metal fabricators in Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Our customers range from mid-sized agricultural equipment manufacturers to automotive subcontractors producing structural brackets and chassis components. What sets us apart is that we stay involved after handover: every cell we deliver comes with a service agreement, and our technicians visit customer sites on a fixed schedule. We do not resell standard robot packages — we engineer the fixture, the tooling, the PLC logic, and the safety enclosure as a single integrated system. Our longest-standing customer relationship is now in its nineteenth year. We work with established robot hardware from the market and build everything else ourselves. The team includes eleven certified welding engineers and four dedicated safety and compliance officers. Our workshop in Novi Sad handles mechanical fabrication, electrical panel assembly, and full acceptance testing before any cell leaves the building.

name: PixelForge Studios d.o.o.
products: Mireille and the Hollow Road — PC and mobile narrative adventure; The Cartographer's Debt — episodic mystery game for PC; Ashveil Chronicles — ongoing mobile narrative series, three episodes released; Custom branching-dialogue engine licensed to two smaller studios; Work-for-hire narrative design and 2D art production for external clients
tech: Unity (primary engine, PC and mobile builds); C# for gameplay and dialogue scripting; In-house branching dialogue engine (proprietary); Spine 2D for character rigging and animation; Procreate and Photoshop for hand-painted asset creation; Python scripts for build automation and asset pipeline management; Plastic SCM for version control across art and code branches; Firebase and internal dashboards for player retention analytics
challenges: C056-CH1: Our procedural level generator produces playable layouts but they feel repetitive after about two hours — players on Steam are leaving reviews saying the maps all look the same, and our 30-day retention has dropped to 18% this quarter. | C056-CH2: We want to add lip-sync animation to our characters automatically from dialogue audio files, but our current tool requires animators to keyframe every phoneme by hand — it's adding three weeks to every localization pass when we release in a new language. | C056-CH3: We've been trying to close a co-development deal with a Dutch publisher for eight months and the contract negotiation keeps stalling on IP ownership clauses — we need someone who actually understands cross-border intellectual property agreements in the EU games industry.

rd_capacity: We can dedicate one senior engineer and one junior programmer part-time to a research collaboration, with the art director available for weekly consultations on any work touching visual output or animation.

about: PixelForge Studios d.o.o. was founded in 2014 by a small group of illustrators and programmers who wanted to make story-driven games that looked like moving paintings. We are based at NTP Novi Sad and currently employ thirty-four people across art, engineering, narrative design, and production. Over the past decade we have shipped seven titles for mobile and PC, reaching players primarily in Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and France. Our games are sold through Steam, the Apple App Store, and Google Play. What sets us apart is the combination of hand-painted environments — every background goes through at least three rounds of watercolour-style digital passes — and dialogue systems that let player choices reshape the story in ways that hold up across multiple playthroughs. We do not outsource our art pipeline; everything is made in-house. Our longest-running title, Mireille and the Hollow Road, has logged over four hundred thousand hours of play since its 2019 launch. We work with a modest but stable budget, grow carefully, and take on one major project at a time. Our current team includes senior developers who have shipped titles before joining us, alongside junior staff we have trained from scratch through a structured six-month onboarding programme.

name: AgroLens d.o.o.
products: AgroLens Field — web and mobile farm management platform for field records and task planning; Crop health maps — fortnightly NDVI and chlorophyll index maps per parcel delivered via the platform; Spraying plan module — generates variable-rate application recommendations from health map data; Season report export — end-of-year PDF and CSV summaries for subsidy documentation and bank reporting
tech: Python (data pipeline and backend API); PostGIS for spatial parcel storage and queries; Sentinel Hub API for satellite image retrieval; React Native (mobile client); React (web dashboard); Docker and a self-managed VPS cluster hosted in Novi Sad; QGIS for internal map QA; PostgreSQL
challenges: C057-CH1: Farmers want a yield estimate per parcel by mid-June, but our maps only show crop vigour. | C057-CH2: Ground truth for soil moisture costs too much: probes are expensive and we can't place them on every parcel.

about: AgroLens d.o.o. was founded in 2019 by a small group of software engineers and agronomists who grew up on Vojvodina grain farms and were tired of watching their parents manage hundreds of hectares with paper notebooks and gut instinct. We built our first field-record tool in a rented room at NTP Novi Sad and signed our first three customers — all sunflower and wheat growers in Bačka — before we had a proper logo. Today we serve just over 140 farms across Vojvodina and northern Hungary, ranging from 200 to 2,000 hectares each. Our platform, AgroLens Field, lets farm managers log every field operation on a phone while sitting in a tractor cab, then review satellite-derived crop health maps on a desktop the same evening. We pull imagery from Sentinel-2 and process it through our own cloud pipeline, so a farmer in Sombor sees an updated NDVI map within two days of a clear-sky pass. Our team of 24 includes agronomists, backend engineers, mobile developers, and two data scientists who focus entirely on turning satellite data into something a farmer actually finds useful. We are not a large platform trying to do everything; we focus on mid-size grain operations and we stay close to our customers. Our field support person, Milovan Crnobrnja, visits customers in person every season.

name: FlexiPack Solutions d.o.o.

products: Mono-materijalne PE kesice za suvu hranu; Višeslojni barijerski filmovi za produženi rok trajanja; Termoformirane PE posude za svežu hranu; Laminati za pakovanje neprehrambenih proizvoda (kozmetika, deterdženti); Pilot serije ambalažnih filmova po specifikaciji kupca
tech: Koekstruzija tankih filmova (blown film ekstruzija); Suvо laminiranje (dry lamination); mLLDPE zaptivni slojevi; EVOH i PVDC barijerni slojevi; Koronа tretman površine filma; Gravurna štampa (outsourcing, Mađarska); OTR i WVTR merenje (kiseonik i vodena para — outsourcing laboratoriji); DSC analiza termičkih svojstava polimera
challenges: C058-CH1: Our mono-material PE-based pouch has excellent seal integrity at room temperature but oxygen transmission rate jumps from 12 to over 80 cc/m²/day at 38°C — which rules us out of any Mediterranean or Middle-East export customer. We need to identify whether this is a coating formulation issue or a structural one in the film layering. | C058-CH2: We are trying to validate that our packaging meets the EU's upcoming recyclability criteria under the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, but we cannot find a local lab that can certify the recyclate quality class. The two Belgian labs that can do it quoted us €22,000 for the test campaign, which is more than our monthly revenue. | C058-CH3: Our sealing layer is an mLLDPE and we get a narrow process window — seal strength is acceptable between 130–138°C but outside that range it either fails to bond or makes the film impossible to peel for end users. plans: U naredne dve godine planiramo da uvedemo sopstvenu štamparsku liniju za kratke serije i da proširimo distribuciju na tržišta EU kroz certifikovanu reciklabilnu ambalažu. Takođe razmatramo uvođenje bio-baziranih PE filmova u ponudu ukoliko se potvrdi dostupnost materijala po prihvatljivoj ceni.
rd_capacity: Imamo internu pilot ekstrudersku liniju i DSC uređaj, ali nemamo kapacitete za naprednu analizu polimerne strukture ni za zvaničnu certifikaciju materijala.
past_collaborations: U 2022. godini sarađivali smo sa konsultantskom kućom Polimer Inženjering d.o.o. iz Novog Sada na optimizaciji parametara ekstruzije za naš prvi komercijalni barijerski film.
about: FlexiPack Solutions d.o.o. je osnovana 2019. godine u Novom Sadu, u okviru inkubacionog programa Naučno-tehnološkog parka Novi Sad. Počeli smo sa timom od četiri osobe i jednom ekstruderskom linijom; danas imamo 19 zaposlenih i serviramo kupce u prehrambenoj industriji širom Srbije i zapadnog Balkana. Pravimo fleksibilnu plastičnu ambalažu — višeslojne filmove, kesice i termoformirane posude — za brendove koji traže rešenja koja su u skladu sa zahtevima EU Green Deal-a i novom Uredbom o ambalaži i ambalažnom otpadu. Naš fokus su mono-materijalni i barijerni filmovi na bazi PE koji se mogu reciklirati u standardnim tokovima. Razlikujemo se po tome što razvijamo materijale interno, a ne samo kupujemo gotova rešenja od dobavljača. Naši glavni kupci su proizvođači hrane srednje veličine koji žele ambalažu koja je i funkcionalna i prihvatljiva za lanac reciklaže. Tim vodi Jovana Mirković, osnivač i tehnički direktor, zajedno sa Nemanjom Ćurčićem zaduženim za prodaju i razvoj poslovnih odnosa. Radimo u pogonu od 1.400 m² u okviru NTP kompleksa i imamo sopstvenu pilot liniju za ekstruziju i laminiranje. Nismo savršeni — suočavamo se sa realnim tehničkim izazovima — ali smo otvoreni prema saradnji s istraživačima koji razumeju materijale.

name: Dunav Kargo a.d.
products: Barge convoy freight on the DTD canal and Danube corridor; Bulk road haulage with covered and open tipper trailers; Combined river-road multimodal transport for agri-food shippers; Seasonal charter barges for construction aggregate projects; Freight documentation and customs clearance support for cross-border shipments
tech: Caterpillar and MAN diesel main propulsion engines with onboard vibration and temperature sensors (retrofitted 2019); VHF radio and AIS transponders for barge tracking; Garmin fleet GPS units on road trucks with basic mileage logging; Microsoft Excel-based payroll and overtime tracking; Paper-and-stamp maintenance logbooks, partially digitised into LibreOffice Calc; DHMZ and RHMSS public weather and hydrology bulletins used manually by dispatchers; In-house fuel consumption tracking via manual pump-station logs

We collect vibration and temperature data from sensors already fitted to the engines but no one on staff knows how to use that data to predict failures before they happen. | C059-CH2: Canal water levels are dropping more often in late summer; two years ago we had to reduce barge loads by 30% for six weeks because we couldn't predict low-water events early enough to reroute cargo to trucks in time. We need a reliable 10-to-14-day low-water forecast for the DTD canal so we can plan load factors and pre-book truck capacity. | C059-CH3: We employ 312 people and the payroll and HR administration still runs on spreadsheets. We are losing roughly two full working days per month just reconciling overtime records, and our HR manager is about to retire. We need to hire or buy a solution, but every ERP vendor we spoke to wants a six-figure licence up front.
plans: Dunav Kargo intends to replace two ageing barges with newer shallow-draft hulls by 2027 to better handle low-water conditions on the DTD canal. The company is also evaluating expansion of its road fleet by ten refrigerated trucks to serve grain-to-mill clients who require temperature-controlled transport.
rd_capacity: We have no dedicated research or data science staff, but our workshop chief and two senior dispatchers are willing to collaborate on practical pilot projects, and we can provide access to sensor data, maintenance records and operational logs.
past_collaborations: Dunav Kargo participated in a regional transport efficiency study run by the Vojvodina Development Agency in 2021, which reviewed fuel consumption patterns across the inland waterway fleet but produced no implemented changes.
about:
Dunav Kargo a.d. has been moving goods along the Danube and the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal system since 1975. What started as a small state-owned barge operator in Novi Sad has grown into one of the region's more dependable inland waterway and road freight companies, with a fleet of twelve barges organised into convoy pairs and sixty road trucks covering Serbia, Hungary, Romania and Croatia.

Our clients are mostly in agri-food and construction: grain exporters, flour mills, cement producers, gravel quarries and fertiliser distributors who need bulk tonnage moved reliably and at a predictable cost. We are not a courier service and we do not promise next-day delivery; we promise that a 1,200-tonne barge of sunflower seed leaves Titel on Tuesday and arrives at the grain terminal in Smederevo on Thursday, every time.

The 312 people who work here include licensed barge masters, certified truck drivers, diesel mechanics, dispatchers and a small commercial team. Fleet maintenance is handled in-house at our workshop on the Štrand canal bank. Our difference is straightforward: we know this waterway system in detail, we own our own equipment and we do not subcontract the work.

name: Subotička Mobilnost a.d.
products: TrasaNet – timetable planning and crew scheduling platform for municipal bus operators; TrasaNet Dispatch – real-time operations console with vehicle tracking and incident logging; PassengerView – passenger information display system for stops and mobile web; DataBridge AVL – onboard GPS and door-sensor hardware with cellular telemetry; CrossBorder Compliance Module – regulatory documentation and data-segregation tooling for multi-jurisdiction operators
tech: Java 17 backend with Spring Boot microservices; PostgreSQL with PostGIS for spatial timetable data; Custom constraint-programming solver built on Choco Solver library; Python scripts for AVL data ingestion and preprocessing; GTFS and GTFS-Realtime feed generation; Docker and Kubernetes on on-premise cluster in Subotica data centre; REST and MQTT for vehicle-to-server telemetry; Oracle Forms legacy modules still running in two older customer deployments
challenges: C060-CH1: Our route optimisation engine re-solves the whole timetable overnight; when a bus breaks down at 7 AM and we need a new schedule by 7:15, the solver takes 40 minutes and dispatchers end up doing it by hand on whiteboards. | C060-CH2: We are collecting AVL data from 340 buses — GPS pings every 10 seconds — but we have never used it to predict travel times; three Romanian municipalities are asking for passenger information screens that show live ETAs within 90 seconds of reality. | C060-CH3: The Hungarian side of our cross-border service requires licensing under Hungarian transport law and GDPR data-residency rules that differ from Serbian regulations; our legal team has spent eight months on this and we are still not cleared to go live.
plans: We plan to release a fully GTFS-Realtime-compliant version of PassengerView by mid-2025 and to expand TrasaNet Dispatch into the Romanian market with at least two additional municipal contracts. We are also evaluating whether to productise the CrossBorder Compliance Module as a standalone offering for other Balkan transit software vendors.
rd_capacity: We can dedicate one senior backend engineer and one domain specialist part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our full historical AVL dataset and timetable logs under a signed data-sharing agreement.
past_collaborations: We completed a co-development project with the Novi Sad Faculty of Technical Sciences in 2019 on GTFS data quality validation tooling, which was incorporated into an early version of DataBridge.
about:
Subotička Mobilnost a.d. was founded in 1997 as a commercial spin-off of the Subotica Regional Transport Coordination Office. Our original mandate was to bring the paper-based scheduling work of the coordination office into a software product that smaller municipalities could actually afford and maintain. Twenty-seven years later, we employ 112 people across our Subotica headquarters and field offices in Novi Sad, Timișoara and Debrecen, and our software runs the daily operations of fourteen public transit authorities across Serbia, Hungary and Romania.

Our core product, TrasaNet, handles timetable construction, vehicle assignment, driver rostering and real-time dispatch monitoring for bus and light-rail networks ranging from twelve to three hundred vehicles. Customers include the Zrenjanin City Transport Authority, the Oradea Metropolitan Transit Consortium and the Kiskunfélegyháza Municipal Bus Service. We do not serve private logistics; everything we build is designed for publicly accountable transit operators who answer to elected officials and daily commuters.

Our team includes transport planners, backend engineers, GIS specialists and a small embedded-systems group that handles onboard AVL hardware integration. Managing Director Dragana Fekete joined from a civil engineering background in 2011 and has led the company through two product generations. We are methodical rather than fast-moving, which suits customers who cannot afford surprises in their morning peak hour.

name: Zlatna Njiva d.o.o.
products: Cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil, bottled in 250 ml and 500 ml dark glass; Cold-pressed sunflower oil, unrefined; Cold-pressed hemp seed oil; Cold-pressed camelina oil; Refined sunflower oil in bulk and retail pack formats
tech: Hydraulic cold-press screw expeller (Farmet FP 500); Plate-and-frame filter press for crude oil clarification; Dark glass bottling line with nitrogen flushing; In-house titration-based free fatty acid testing; Peroxide value measurement by iodometric titration; Seed moisture analyser (Dickey-john GAC 2500); Temperature-controlled seed storage silo (concrete, passive cooling); ERP inventory tracking (custom-built local software, MS Access back-end)
challenges: C061-CH1: Our cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil goes rancid within 4 months on shelf, but competitors manage 9–12 months; we lose about 15% of each batch to returns and we have no idea what oxidation pathway is hitting us fastest. | C061-CH2: We press roughly 400 kg of oil per shift and the filter press is the bottleneck — it clogs every 90 minutes and cleaning takes 25 minutes each time, costing us almost a full shift per week. | C061-CH3: We want to enter the German organic retail market but our current EU organic certification application has been sitting with the certifier for 11 months and we cannot figure out how to move it forward.
plans: Within the next two years Zlatna Njiva intends to add a dedicated cold-press line for organic seeds, physically separated from the conventional line, to simplify certification compliance and expand the organic export range. We are also evaluating a small direct-to-consumer subscription model for the Serbian market as a way to reduce dependence on retail chain margins.
rd_capacity: We have one in-house lab technician who handles routine quality checks and can support external partners with sample preparation and basic physical-chemical measurements, but we do not have dedicated research staff or specialised analytical instruments beyond titration and moisture analysis.
past_collaborations: We worked briefly with the Agricultural Extension Service of South Banat District on a seed variety trial in 2019, which helped us select the pumpkin seed cultivar we currently use, but we have had no formal research or technical collaboration since then.
about: Zlatna Njiva d.o.o. has been pressing oil in Zrenjanin since 1991, when Dragoljub Kovačević converted a small grain cooperative building into the company's first production facility. Three decades later, his daughter Milica Kovačević-Petrić runs day-to-day operations alongside a team of 87 people, most of them from the surrounding villages. We produce cold-pressed sunflower, pumpkin seed, camelina, and hemp seed oils, as well as a conventional refined sunflower line that supplies retail chains including Merkator Serbia and Tempo. Our export business covers Slovenia and Austria, where speciality grocery buyers pick up our cold-pressed range under our Zlatna Njiva label. What sets us apart is that we still source the majority of our raw seeds directly from farms within sixty kilometres of the press, which lets us trace every batch back to a specific field and harvest. We bottle on-site, label on-site, and run our own small quality lab where we check free fatty acid content, peroxide value, and sensory properties before anything leaves the warehouse. We are not a large industrial operation and we have no intention of becoming one, but we do intend to grow into the German organic retail segment and to make our shelf-life performance match the best on the European market.

name: Terramap Subotica d.o.o.
sector: Land surveying and underground infrastructure mapping
products: GNSS land and cadastral surveying; Ground-penetrating radar underground utility mapping; As-built documentation for infrastructure construction; Permanent GNSS reference-station RTK correction network; Cross-border geodetic deliverables for Serbian and Hungarian regulatory submissions
tech: Leica GS18 and Geomax Zenith 40 GNSS receivers; MALÅ Easy Locator HDR and MALÅ X3M ground-penetrating radar systems; RADAN 7 GPR data processing software; Trimble Business Center and AutoCAD Civil 3D for survey data processing; QGIS with custom digitising workflows for utility mapping; In-house network of five permanent GNSS reference stations (NTRIP-served); Topcon HiPer HR for control traverse work; EOV / HD72 and ETRS89 coordinate transformation via established grid-shift parameters

The company is also evaluating the purchase of a second GPR antenna configuration suited to deeper utility detection on rural pipeline corridors.
rd_capacity: Terramap has no dedicated research staff, but two senior surveyors with postgraduate geodesy backgrounds can contribute ten to fifteen hours per week to a structured collaboration if day-to-day project load allows.

about:
Terramap Subotica d.o.o. has been measuring the ground beneath your feet since 1998. We started as a small team of three surveyors working the agricultural plots and drainage canals along the Serbian-Hungarian border, and over the past twenty-six years we have grown to sixty-seven people who cover everything from single-parcel GNSS surveys to full underground utility mapping on multi-kilometre road and pipeline corridors.

Our headquarters is in Subotica, which puts us close to the clients who matter most to us: municipal engineering offices, road maintenance companies, gas and water utilities, and agricultural land developers on both sides of the border. Roughly a third of our revenue comes from projects in southern Hungary, where we have worked continuously since the early 2000s.

What sets us apart is the combination of field depth and instrument range. Our crews carry Leica and Geomax GNSS receivers, operate a fleet of four MALÅ ground-penetrating radar carts, and run our own permanent reference-station network across northern Vojvodina. We produce GPS-controlled as-built documentation, GPR utility maps, and digital terrain models that feed directly into AutoCAD Civil 3D or QGIS project environments.

Our clients include Subotica Vodokanal, Kanjiža Road Maintenance, and several private construction contractors working on EU-co-financed infrastructure in Bačka. We are not the cheapest option on the market, and we do not try to be. We are the option that comes back to fix things if something is wrong.

name: Orbita Inženjering d.o.o.
sector: Custom software and IT services for EU clients
products: Custom digital-twin software for manufacturing and process plants; Physics-based simulation model development (thermal, mechanical, fluid); 3D web-based simulation visualisation and operator dashboards; Integration services connecting simulation models to SCADA and MES systems; Simulation-based operator training environments
tech: C++ for physics solver development; Python for model scripting and data pipelines; Three.js and WebGL for 3D browser visualisation; FEniCS and custom finite-element solvers; OPC-UA for real-time plant data ingestion; Docker and Kubernetes for model deployment; PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB for time-series simulation data; React for front-end dashboards
challenges: C063-CH1: Our digital-twin models for Italian factory clients run 15–20× slower than real time because the physics solvers aren't parallelised — operators can't use them for live decision support and three prospects declined for exactly this reason. | C063-CH2: A French aerospace supplier wants us to add vibration fatigue analysis to our mechanical digital twin, but we have no in-house expertise in structural dynamics — we'd need to either hire or partner fast because the tender closes in 90 days. | C063-CH3: We visualise simulation results in a 3D web viewer but rendering complex factory layouts with 200,000+ mesh elements crashes browsers on mid-range company laptops — about 40% of our end users can't view the full model. | C063-CH4: Our Slovenian clients are asking us to include a worker ergonomics assessment module in the digital twin — we know nothing about ergonomics standards and don't know whether this is an engineering or a medical problem.
plans: Over the next two years Orbita Inženjering plans to move from purely custom project work toward a configurable digital-twin platform that can be deployed more quickly across similar factory types, starting with food processing and light assembly. We are also evaluating whether to open a small office in Ljubljana to support the Slovenian client base more directly.
rd_capacity: We can allocate two to three senior engineers part-time to a joint research or development activity, and have used this arrangement successfully on two previous technical partnerships.
past_collaborations: We completed a two-year technical collaboration with Termosim d.o.o., a Slovenian thermal engineering consultancy, on a shared fluid-simulation library used in three client projects.
about:
Orbita Inženjering d.o.o. was founded in 1991 by Dragan Vuković and Miroslav Ćirić, two professors from the Faculty of Technical Sciences who believed that engineering simulation software could be built locally and sold across Europe. More than thirty years later, that belief has held. We employ 135 engineers and developers in Novi Sad and maintain long-term working relationships with industrial clients in Italy, France and Slovenia.

Our core work is custom digital-twin and simulation software for manufacturing and process industries. We build models that mirror real factory systems — thermal, mechanical, fluid, electrical — and deliver them as software products that plant engineers can actually use, not academic prototypes. Clients use our tools for process optimisation, maintenance planning and operator training.

What makes us different is the combination: our team includes both software developers and people with genuine mechanical and thermal engineering backgrounds. We write production-grade code but we also understand the physics. That combination is harder to find than it sounds.

Our Italian clients include mid-size food-processing and automotive-component manufacturers. In France we work primarily with a tier-two aerospace supply chain. In Slovenia we serve two large production facilities in the plastics and furniture sectors. We do not chase large system-integrator contracts. We prefer direct relationships with engineering departments where we can be useful over a long period.

name: Krenuti Digital d.o.o.
sector: Custom software and IT services for EU clients
products: FlowDeck – no-code workflow automation platform for logistics operations; FlowDeck Live – real-time vehicle tracking and ETA display module; Workflow Health Monitor – alerting and diagnostics dashboard for running automations; Managed Onboarding – paid implementation and configuration service for new clients

about:
OrtoPrint Solutions a.d. has been making orthopaedic aids in Zrenjanin since 1993, when Dragan Molnar and two certified orthotists set up a small workshop to serve the rehabilitation units of Vojvodina's public hospitals. In 2016 we made a deliberate shift: we brought in structured-light scanning, CAD modelling and polymer additive manufacturing, retaining all of our senior orthotists so that clinical judgment and digital production could work side by side.

Today our 142 employees — roughly a third of them trained orthotists or prosthetists — produce custom orthoses, prosthetic sockets and rigid protective components for hospitals, rehabilitation centres and private orthopaedic clinics in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, North Macedonia and Montenegro. Our main manufacturing facility is in Zrenjanin with a fitting and aftercare office in Novi Sad.

What sets us apart is the combination of in-house clinical staff and our own print floor. When a device comes back for rework, the same person who fitted it can observe the correction and feed that information back into the next job. We are not a print bureau that happens to make medical parts — we are orthotists who also run printers.

NovaByte Simulations d.o.o. has been building interactive software in Novi Sad since 2005. We started as a small consumer-game studio, shipping titles for the regional PC market, but by 2011 we had shifted our focus entirely to simulation software for professional training. That decision turned out to be the right one. Today our clients include logistics operators, construction companies, and vocational training centres from Slovenia to North Macedonia, and our simulators are used by several thousand trainees each year.

Our team of 67 people covers game engineering, 3-D art, instructional design, and client support. We run a flat structure: developers talk directly to clients, which keeps the software grounded in what actually happens on a warehouse floor or a construction site rather than what looks impressive in a demo. We do most of our core engine work in-house rather than buying off-the-shelf solutions, because industrial training clients have requirements that consumer-game tools do not anticipate — audit logs, branching scenario editors, hardware-in-the-loop inputs, and compliance documentation.

We are based at NTP Novi Sad, which has given us access to researchers and specialist suppliers we would not otherwise have met. Our simulators are not the flashiest products on the market, but they hold up under repeated daily use and our clients renew their licences.

about:
Voltiko d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2014 by a small group of electronics engineers who had spent the previous decade building industrial monitoring equipment for local automation firms. The idea was straightforward: design wireless sensor nodes that are small enough to fit inside existing enclosures, reliable enough to run unattended for years, and honest enough in their specifications that integrators can stake their own project timelines on them.

Today we have 34 people across hardware design, firmware, RF, production, and logistics. Our customers are system integrators, not end users — mostly mid-sized firms in Germany, Austria, and the Czech Republic who embed our nodes and gateways into factory monitoring, cold-chain, and building-management installations. We do not sell to consumers and we do not chase short product cycles.

What keeps clients coming back is that we control the full stack: PCB layout, antenna matching, firmware, and the gateway software that handles cloud uplink. When something goes wrong in the field, we can trace it. We manufacture in-house at our NTP Novi Sad facility, which means production changes can be turned around in weeks rather than quarters. We are not the cheapest option, but integrators tell us that our documentation and field reliability make the total project cost predictable.

about:
Subotica Interactive is a micro studio run by Milovan Fekete, a solo developer and writer based in Subotica. Founded in 2021 and registered as a sole trader, we make narrative role-playing games rooted in the folklore, landscapes, and quiet tensions of the Pannonian Plain. Our first project, *Szállás az Innenső Parton* (Working title: *Lodgings on the Near Shore*), is a story-driven RPG set in 1920s Vojvodina, where players move between Hungarian, Serbian, and German-speaking communities navigating the aftermath of border changes and old rural superstitions.

We sell through digital storefronts aimed at European audiences who are tired of generic fantasy settings. Our players tend to be adults who read historical fiction and want games that take regional culture seriously rather than using it as decoration.

The team is small by design: Milovan handles writing, design, and production management; Dorotya Varga handles 2D art and UI; Ervin Molnár is our environment artist; Tamara Ćirić does QA and community; and one part-time composer, Goran Takač, handles the folk-influenced soundtrack. We work remotely with occasional in-person sessions in Subotica.

What separates us from larger studios is that we treat the source material with care. We do primary research, talk to local historians, and try not to romanticise or flatten the complexity of the region's past. That takes more time, but it is the point.
