challenges: C073-CH1: Our platform collects clickstream and in-store sensor data and tries to infer customer mood and intent in real time, but the model we trained on Belgian retail data drops from 84% to 61% accuracy when deployed for a Romanian grocery chain — the shopping behaviour patterns are just different and we don't know how to adapt without retraining from scratch each time. | C073-CH2: A Belgian telecom client wants us to add a churn-prediction score to every customer record and show it on their CRM, but their data protection officer is asking for a full algorithmic impact assessment and documentation of feature importance in a form that satisfies the EU AI Act transparency requirements — we've never written one. | C073-CH3: Our R&D team is testing a new in-store footfall heatmap feature using overhead cameras, but the people-counting model confuses partially occluded shoppers with shelving units — in stores with tall gondola shelving the error rate reaches 22%, which makes the heatmaps useless. | C073-CH4: We want to expand into the German market but our current sales team has no German-speaking enterprise sales experience; we've been trying to hire a country manager for seven months without success and the two candidates we made offers to both declined.
plans: U naredne dve godine planiramo da CXCore platformu proširimo na tržišta nemačkog govornog područja i uvedemo modul za analitiku lojalnosti koji bi se integrisao s postojećim loyalty programima maloprodajnih klijenata. Takođe razmatramo otvaranje manje tehničke kancelarije u Varšavi radi bliže saradnje s poljskim klijentima.
rd_capacity: Interni R&D tim od 30 inženjera i istraživača radi na razvoju novih modula platforme, poboljšanju postojećih ML modela i istraživanju novih metoda obrade podataka sa senzora u maloprodajnom okruženju.
past_collaborations: Vertigo Labs je 2019. godine učestvovao u kratkoročnom istraživačkom projektu s jednom tehničkom firmom iz Krakova vezanom za anonimizaciju video podataka, ali formalne akademske saradnje do sada nije bilo.
about:
Vertigo Labs a.d. osnovana je 2004. godine u Novom Sadu kao mali tim programera koji je radio prilagođena softverska rešenja za lokalne klijente. Tokom narednih nekoliko godina preusmerili smo se ka zapadnoevropskom tržištu i razvili sopstvenu platformu za analitiku korisničkog iskustva, danas poznatu pod internim nazivom CXCore. Platforma se licencira telekomunikacionim operaterima i maloprodajnim lancima u Belgiji, Poljskoj i Rumuniji, a klijenti je koriste pod sopstvenim brendom.

Danas imamo 155 zaposlenih, od kojih 30 radi u internom R&D timu. Ostatak tima čine inženjeri, analitičari podataka, DevOps stručnjaci i tim za podršku klijentima. Naši klijenti nisu startapi — reč je o etabliranim kompanijama sa složenim infrastrukturama koje traže pouzdan softver, a ne eksperiment.

Ono što nas razlikuje od većine sličnih firmi jeste to što ne prodajemo samo kod — isporučujemo gotov, konfigurabilan proizvod koji operater ili maloprodajni lanac može da postavi pod sopstvenim imenom za nekoliko sedmica. Svaki novi klijent ne počinje od nule; koristi osnovu koju smo gradili dvadeset godina. Sedište nam je u Novom Sadu, a prodajna kancelarija u Briselu.

name: GeoStruct Inženjering d.o.o.
products: Drone LiDAR survey and point-cloud processing for bridges and transport infrastructure; BIM-based structural condition assessment and asset documentation; KatastarVid — web platform for live cadastral and utility-network overlay for municipalities; Geotechnical investigation and subsurface modelling for road and foundation projects; Regulatory and cadastral survey services for public and private clients
tech: Drone-mounted LiDAR (Velodyne VLP-32 equivalent sensors on DJI M300 airframes); Terrestrial laser scanning (Leica RTC360-class instruments); Autodesk Revit and Civil 3D for BIM modelling; CloudCompare and custom Python scripts for point-cloud pre-processing; PostgreSQL/PostGIS spatial database backend; QGIS and Mapbox GL JS for web GIS front-end; PLAXIS 2D for geotechnical finite-element modelling; GPR (ground-penetrating radar) for shallow subsurface investigation
challenges: C074-CH1: We use drone-mounted LiDAR to capture as-built data on bridges and overpasses, but converting the raw point clouds into usable structural models still takes our engineers three to four weeks per site — we need that down to under five days or we lose competitive bids. | C074-CH2: Our proptech spin-off product — a web platform that gives municipal clients a live cadastral and utility-network overlay — is seeing 40-second load times when a user queries more than 50,000 parcels at once; three pilot municipalities have complained and one is threatening to cancel the contract. | C074-CH3: We won a EU-funded project to assess foundation soil conditions along a 12 km road corridor in Srem, but our current geotechnical models rely only on borehole logs every 500 m and we're seeing unexpected settlement predictions — we need a way to interpolate subsurface stratigraphy more reliably between boreholes. | C074-CH4: We have been trying for eight months to get our updated geodetic-services licence approved by the Republic Geodetic Authority after a regulatory change in 2023; the paperwork is stuck and we can't legally sign off on cadastral surveys in the meantime, which is blocking roughly 15% of our planned revenue this year.
plans: GeoStruct intends to expand KatastarVid from three pilot municipalities to at least twelve by the end of 2026, targeting mid-size cities in Vojvodina and one cross-border contract in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In parallel, the company is preparing a bid for a multi-year bridge inspection framework with the Serbian Roads Agency, which would require a significantly faster point-cloud-to-BIM pipeline than the one currently in use.
rd_capacity: The company has no formal R&D department but can dedicate one experienced GIS engineer and up to 20 percent of a senior structural engineer's time to applied development work alongside an external partner.
past_collaborations: GeoStruct completed a short applied project with the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad in 2019, contributing field LiDAR data for a study on road pavement deflection mapping; no ongoing institutional collaboration has followed.
about:
GeoStruct Inženjering d.o.o. was established in Novi Sad in 2008 by a small team of civil engineers and geodesists who saw a gap between traditional surveying practice and the emerging possibilities of digital spatial data. Over the past sixteen years we have grown to 47 people and built a steady client base among public road agencies, municipal utilities and EU-funded infrastructure programmes across Vojvodina and the Western Balkans.

Our core work sits at the boundary of geospatial data acquisition and structural engineering. We capture high-density field data — through drone-mounted LiDAR, terrestrial scanning and geotechnical investigation — and convert it into BIM models, condition reports and asset registers that public clients can actually use to plan maintenance and investment. A younger part of the business, launched in 2021, develops a web-based platform that gives municipal governments a live view of their cadastral and utility-network data.

Long-term contracts with the Vojvodina Roads Directorate, the City of Zrenjanin Utility Service, and the Srem Regional Development Agency form the backbone of our work. Day-to-day operations are led by director Branimir Ostojić, with technical direction split between chief geodesist Milena Vukić and lead structural engineer Dragan Stanković. What keeps clients coming back is straightforward: we deliver models and reports that hold up under scrutiny, and we are honest about what the data can and cannot tell you.

name: Voltmreža a.d.
products: Low- and medium-voltage network design; Underground and overhead line construction; Smart metering infrastructure deployment; Transformer station installation and commissioning; Prosumer grid connection and inspection services
tech: AutoCAD-based network drafting; DIgSILENT PowerFactory for load-flow analysis; Trimble GPS survey equipment; DLMS/COSEM smart meter protocol; PLC and RF mesh AMI communication networks; GIS asset registry (custom-built on QGIS); IEC 61850 substation configuration tools
challenges: C075-CH1: We are connecting more and more small prosumer solar installations — sometimes 20 to 30 on a single rural LV feeder — and our field teams report voltage rising above 253 V at the far end of the feeder on sunny afternoons, which is causing nuisance tripping and complaints from neighbours who do not even have solar; our network planning tool was designed for one-way power flow and simply does not handle this. | C075-CH2: We installed 18,000 smart meters in the last contract cycle and the utility is asking us to provide a report showing the carbon footprint of their entire low-voltage network operation — we have no methodology, no internal expertise, and the tender for the next phase explicitly requires an ISO 14064 compliant calculation. | C075-CH3: Our civil crews have to dig exploratory trenches to locate old underground cables before every excavation because the as-built drawings from the 1970s and 1980s are either missing or wrong by up to 4 metres — last year we had two cable strikes that cost us a combined 340,000 dinars in repairs and project delays. | C075-CH4: We want to move into battery energy storage system (BESS) integration for industrial clients but we cannot find electricians or commissioning engineers in Vojvodina who have any hands-on experience with lithium iron phosphate battery management systems — the two people we tried to hire in the last six months both took offers in Germany.
plans: Voltmreža intends to qualify for BESS installation contracts by the end of 2025 and is actively expanding its smart metering portfolio into the Mačva and Kolubara districts of central Serbia. The company is also investing in updating its underground asset registry to reduce pre-excavation survey costs across its main service territory.
rd_capacity: We have a four-person internal engineering office that can contribute data, field testing time and practical evaluation, but we have no dedicated research staff and cannot lead scientific work independently.
past_collaborations: Voltmreža completed a joint equipment-testing programme with the Electrical Engineering Faculty workshop in Subotica in 2019, evaluating meter communication reliability under agricultural electromagnetic interference conditions.
about: Voltmreža a.d. was established in 1991 in Zrenjanin by the Kukić family, who began with a four-person crew laying medium-voltage cable in the flat agricultural stretches of Banat. Thirty-three years later the company employs 187 people across engineering, civil works, metering and project management, and delivers grid design and construction services to distribution utilities throughout Vojvodina and into Bosnia-Herzegovina, Montenegro and North Macedonia. Our core business covers three areas: network planning and design for low- and medium-voltage systems, physical construction including trenching, cable laying, transformer installation and switchgear commissioning, and metering infrastructure — from smart-meter rollout through to data concentrators and communication backhaul. We work primarily for regulated distribution utilities but also for large industrial connection projects. What sets us apart is the combination of a dedicated in-house survey team, a licensed engineering design office and civil crews who have worked together for years. Our longest-standing customer relationship, with a Vojvodina distribution utility, goes back to 1997. Managing director Predrag Kukić, son of the founder, leads a management team that keeps engineering decisions close to field experience. We are headquartered at our Zrenjanin facility, which houses design offices, a cable testing bay and a vehicle and equipment yard.

name: UrbanVizion d.o.o.
products: ZoneSim — scenario modelling and land-use simulation module; CityView 3D — browser-based three-dimensional zoning visualisation; PublicVoice — structured public consultation and comment collection tool; DataBridge — spatial data import, transformation and validation pipeline; PlanExport — regulatory-format plan document generation
tech: CesiumJS for 3-D terrain and building rendering; PostGIS / PostgreSQL for spatial data storage; GDAL and Proj for coordinate reference system transformations; Python (GeoPandas, Shapely) for spatial processing pipelines; React and TypeScript for the frontend application; Docker and Kubernetes on a managed cloud cluster; OpenStreetMap-derived base layers supplemented by national cadastral feeds; FreeCAD-based procedural roof generation (experimental)
challenges: C076-CH1: Our platform generates 3-D urban models from cadastral footprints and building heights, but the models look obviously wrong in historic city centres where buildings have irregular roof forms — clients in Austria and Slovenia have flagged this as a dealbreaker for public consultation sessions. | C076-CH2: We want to add a pedestrian comfort layer to the simulation — showing wind speed and shadow patterns at street level — but our team has no background in microclimate modelling and the CFD tools we tried take eight hours per scenario, which is too slow for interactive planning sessions. | C076-CH3: Spatial plans in Serbia are legally referenced to the national geodetic datum and our EU clients work in ETRS89; the coordinate transformation introduces visible misalignment of up to three metres in some regions, and we do not fully understand why. | C076-CH4: We are trying to close a Series A round with a Vienna-based proptech fund and they want audited financial statements for the past three years, but our accountant has produced them in the Serbian statutory format and the fund's lawyers say they cannot use them without an IFRS restatement.
plans: UrbanVizion intends to reach ten paying municipal clients in German-speaking and Adriatic markets by the end of 2025, with the Series A round funding a expanded engineering team and localisation for German and Slovenian regulatory export formats. We are also scoping a mobile companion application that would let field inspectors link site photographs directly to parcels inside the platform.
rd_capacity: We can dedicate one senior software engineer and our in-house GIS specialist to a structured collaboration for up to six months, and we have access to anonymised spatial datasets from three active municipal deployments for testing purposes.
past_collaborations: In 2022 we completed a three-month technical exchange with Geopolis Institute, a privately funded spatial-data consultancy in Belgrade, who helped us design the initial version of our DataBridge import pipeline.
about:
UrbanVizion d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2019 by a small group of software engineers and urban planners who had grown tired of watching municipalities make multimillion-euro decisions using static PDF maps and spreadsheets. We build a cloud-based platform that lets city planners and municipal staff model land-use scenarios, view zoning proposals in three dimensions, and collect structured written feedback from residents — all inside a single browser window, without installing anything.

Our paying customers are mostly mid-sized municipalities and regional planning agencies in Central and Western Europe. We currently work with clients in Austria, Slovenia, and Serbia, and we are in late-stage talks with two German regional authorities. Every project we take on involves real spatial data — cadastral footprints, official zoning layers, infrastructure networks — so accuracy and legal compliance matter as much as good visuals.

The team is nineteen people, based almost entirely at NTP Novi Sad. We have software engineers, a GIS specialist, a product designer, and an in-house urban planner. We are not a consultancy; we write software. What makes us different is that our platform is built around the planning workflow, not the other way around: planners can compare scenarios side by side, version their decisions, and export outputs that meet local regulatory formatting requirements.

name: RoboFleks d.o.o.
products: Projektovanje i integracija kobot pick-and-place ćelija; Automatizovane paletizacione linije za mešovitu proizvodnju; Ćelije za robotsko MIG/MAG zavarivanje; Električni ormarići i PLC upravljanje za robotske stanice; Servis, kalibracija i reintegracija postojećih robotskih sistema
tech: Kollmorgen AKD servo pogoni; Siemens S7-1500 PLC platforma; Universal Robots UR10e i UR16e koboti; Sick nSafe sigurnosni skeneri i laserske barijere; ROS 2 za prototipove upravljačke logike; Mitsubishi MELFA industrijski roboti za zavarivačke aplikacije; Keyence IV3 vizijski sistemi za detekciju pozicije; AutoCAD Electrical za elektro dokumentaciju
challenges: C077-CH1: Our cobots slow down or stop entirely when a human worker gets within the safety envelope, which cuts throughput by up to 35% on mixed human-robot assembly lines; clients are starting to complain that promised cycle times aren't being met and two contracts are at risk of penalty clauses. | C077-CH2: We reprogram each new workcell from scratch and it takes our engineers an average of 11 days per installation; we've turned down four projects this quarter alone because we simply don't have the engineering hours, and at our current day-rate that is roughly €38,000 in lost revenue. | C077-CH3: A German Tier-2 automotive supplier wants us to provide a full CE Declaration of Conformity package under the new EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 before they will sign a €620,000 framework agreement, and we have never prepared this documentation for the German market before. | C077-CH4: The welding robot on our flagship cell leaves inconsistent bead width — varying between 3.8 mm and 6.1 mm on the same joint — when the steel workpiece temperature drifts during long production runs, and we have no sensor feedback loop to compensate in real time.
plans: Do kraja 2025. planiramo da proširimo tim za dva integracionа inženjera i da otvorimo servisni punkt u Sarajevu koji bi pokrivao klijente u Bosni i Hercegovini. Razmatramo i uvođenje usluge daljinskog monitoringa ćelija u realnom vremenu kao pretplatničkog modela.
rd_capacity: Imamo jednog inženjera koji je delom oslobođen od projektnih obaveza i može da posveti do 30 posto radnog vremena razvoju internih alata i testiranju novih rešenja na demonstracionoj ćeliji u našem prostoru.
past_collaborations: Sarađivali smo sa Fakultetom tehničkih nauka u Novom Sadu na jednokratnom studentskom projektu merenja sila u hvatačima 2019. godine, bez formalnog ugovora o istraživanju.
about:
RoboFleks d.o.o. je osnovan 2011. godine u Novom Sadu, sa jednim jasnim ciljem: da malim i srednje velikim proizvođačima u Vojvodini i širem regionu Zapadnog Balkana dostavi robotiku koja zapravo radi u njihovim pogonima — bez nepotrebne složenosti i bez astronomskih budžeta karakterističnih za velika postrojenja. Počeli smo sa dva inženjera i jednom montažnom ćelijom na pozajmljenoj površini u industrijskoj zoni na Klisi. Danas nas je 47, radimo u sopstvenim prostorijama na Naučno-tehnološkom parku Novi Sad i integrišemo robotske ćelije za klijente od Subotice do Sarajeva.

Naši klijenti su uglavnom proizvođači u sektorima prehrambene industrije, ambalaže, metaloprerade i automobilskih komponenti. Sarađujemo sa kompanijama poput Palić Pakovanja, Kovačević Metal iz Zrenjanina i grupom pogona Adriatik Plast. Tim čine mašinski i elektro inženjeri, programeri i tehničari koji su prošli obuke kod proizvođača kobot platformi. Ono što nas razlikuje nije marketing — to je činjenica da inženjer koji je projektovao ćeliju dolazi i na puštanje u rad. Nema posrednika, nema iznenađenja na licu mesta.

name: Aroma Natura a.d.
products: Lavender and chamomile moisturising creams (daily and intensive range); Steam-distilled essential oils — lavender, chamomile, yarrow and mint; Herbal extract concentrates for cosmetic formulators (B2B); Mineral sunscreen lotions SPF 30 and SPF 50 (launch pending validation); Aromatic room and linen sprays for retail and hospitality
tech: Steam distillation (batch vessel, 1980s Slovenian-built unit, 500 L capacity); Cold maceration and percolation for herbal extract production; HPLC for active compound quantification in extracts; In-house stability chamber testing (ICH zones II and IV conditions); Injection-moulded PP packaging with in-house quality inspection; EU Cosmetics Regulation compliance documentation (CPNP portal); ERP system (domestic vendor, Poslovni Softver d.o.o.) for batch traceability; GC-MS for essential oil composition profiling
challenges: C078-CH1: Three of our best-selling moisturisers have a shelf life of only 14 months, which is too short for some German and Austrian distributors who need at least 24 months to cover their warehouse cycle. We've tried increasing the preservative load but it pushes us over the EU Cosmetics Regulation limits and changes the smell. | C078-CH2: We extract lavender and chamomile in-house using a 1980s steam-distillation vessel, and our yield is about 20% lower than benchmarks we see from Turkish and Bulgarian competitors. We suspect the raw material pre-treatment and distillation time profiles are suboptimal but we've never done a systematic study. | C078-CH3: Our new sunscreen line needs SPF validation testing before we can put SPF 30 or SPF 50 on the label, and every accredited lab we've contacted in Serbia says they don't do in-vivo or in-vitro SPF testing — the nearest option is Budapest and they quoted us 9,000 EUR per SKU. | C078-CH4: We've seen a 30% rise in returns of our hand-cream jars from pharmacy chains because the injection-moulded PP lid warps in summer heat during transport, causing the seal to fail. Our packaging supplier says the tooling is fine but we think the wall thickness distribution is wrong.
plans: We want to qualify the sunscreen line for EU market entry by mid-2026 and expand our B2B herbal extract business toward cosmetic formulators in Central Europe. We are also evaluating whether to replace the 1983 distillation vessel or retrofit it with automated temperature control.
rd_capacity: Our in-house laboratory team of eight handles formulation, stability testing and GC-MS analysis but does not include process engineers, packaging specialists or regulatory testing experts.
past_collaborations: Aroma Natura completed a raw-material authentication study in 2019 with the Institute for Food Technology in Novi Sad (FINS), focused on HPLC fingerprinting of chamomile extracts from different growing regions.
about:
Aroma Natura a.d. has been making natural cosmetics and aromatic preparations in Subotica since 1975. What started as a small cooperative distillery on the edge of the Vojvodina plain has grown into a company of 214 people, with our own fields, extraction facility, and a formulation laboratory that handles everything from raw herb to finished jar.

We sell under the Aroma Natura brand in pharmacies, health stores and supermarkets across Serbia, and we export to Hungary, Austria and Romania through regional distributors. Our best-known lines are moisturising creams built around our own lavender and chamomile extracts, essential oil blends for home and professional aromatherapy use, and a recently launched mineral sunscreen range.

What separates us from contract manufacturers is that we control the raw material from the start. We work with around forty herb growers in Bačka and source additional botanicals from trusted suppliers in Bosnia and Bulgaria. Our head formulator, Mirjana Vuković, has been with the company for nineteen years and leads a team of eight in the lab.

We are not a fast-moving trend brand. We move carefully, test thoroughly, and keep our ingredient lists honest. That approach has built steady relationships with pharmacy chains like Farmeko Plus and Zelena Lekarnica, and it is the reason our Austrian distributor, Kräuterweg GmbH, has worked with us for eleven years.

name: Activora Sport d.o.o.
products: Activora Mobile — player app for passive movement data collection during training sessions; Activora Coach Dashboard — web interface showing per-player and squad-level training load and injury-risk summaries; Weekly Load Report — automated PDF digest sent to coaches every Monday morning; Activora Physio View — read-only portal for club physiotherapists and medical staff
tech: Python (data pipeline and model training); FastAPI (REST backend); React (coach web dashboard); Flutter (cross-platform mobile app); PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB extension; scikit-learn and PyTorch (movement classification and risk models); MQTT broker for real-time sensor event streaming; Docker and a self-hosted VPS cluster in Novi Sad
challenges: C079-CH1: We collect accelerometer and gyroscope data from players' phones during training, but our movement-pattern model was trained on professional-athlete datasets from Western Europe and the injury-risk scores it produces for our amateur users in Serbian regional leagues are uncorrelated with the actual injury events coaches report — we have 340 players worth of data now and need to retrain. | C079-CH2: Coaches tell us the dashboard is hard to understand — they spend more time figuring out what the charts mean than actually coaching, and our 30-day retention is only 19% among coaches over 40 years old. | C079-CH3: We need to hire two senior backend engineers to handle the real-time data pipeline before the next season starts in August, but every candidate we approach is immediately counter-offered by companies in Belgrade or remotely for EU salaries we simply cannot match at our current funding stage.
plans: Activora plans to expand to clubs in Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia during the 2025 season, using Vojvodina as a reference market. We are preparing a seed funding application for Q4 2024 that would allow us to grow the technical team and begin a formal validation study with a sports medicine partner.
rd_capacity: We have one full-time data analyst and one part-time physiotherapist who together spend roughly two days per week on model evaluation and feature work, with limited capacity for structured research outside of direct product needs.
past_collaborations: We ran a three-month informal advisory arrangement in 2023 with a sports performance consultant based in Novi Sad, Dragan Cvejić, who reviewed our injury-risk feature set and suggested changes to our acute load calculation; no formal institutional partnership has been completed.
about:
Activora Sport d.o.o. was founded in Zrenjanin in 2021 by a small group of football coaches and software developers who were tired of watching amateur players get hurt for reasons that better data could have prevented. We build tools that help coaches in Serbian and wider Southeast European regional leagues track how hard their players are working and spot warning signs before an injury happens.

Our platform combines data collected from players' own phones with a coach-facing web dashboard that turns raw numbers into simple weekly summaries. We do not target professional clubs with large budgets and dedicated analysts. Our users are volunteer and semi-professional coaches running sessions two evenings a week, often without any support staff.

Today we work with fourteen clubs across Vojvodina and Central Serbia, covering around 340 active players in the system. Our team of nine includes mobile and backend developers, a data analyst, two people who came directly from grassroots coaching, and a part-time physiotherapist who reviews our injury-risk logic.

What sets us apart is not the technology itself but the focus: every design decision starts with the question of whether a coach with a tablet and ten minutes between drills can actually use this. We are early stage, we are honest about what we do not yet know, and we are actively looking for people who can help us fill those gaps.

name: Košava Tekstil d.o.o.
products: Flame-retardant protective jackets and trousers certified to EN ISO 11612; High-visibility workwear certified to EN ISO 20471; Chemical-splash resistant coveralls for industrial use; General industrial workwear sets (jackets, trousers, shirts) in custom colours; Contract dyeing and finishing for small external garment batches
tech: Straight-knife fabric cutting with manual lay-up; Single-needle and double-needle lockstitch industrial sewing machines; In-house reactive and vat dyeing with open-width jigger units; Jet dyeing machine for tubular knit components; Thermosol interlining bonding press; EN ISO 11612 and EN ISO 20471 in-house pre-compliance flammability testing (vertical flame spread, limited flame spread); Manual marker-making on paper with CAD-assisted pattern grading via Gemaks software
challenges: C080-CH1: Our protective jackets are tested to EN ISO 11612 but we keep failing the vertical flame spread test on the collar seam — roughly 3 out of every 10 sample batches — and we can't pinpoint whether it's the thread, the interlining adhesive, or the dye chemistry on that specific fabric blend. | C080-CH2: Our dyeing unit uses roughly 18,000 litres of water per shift, and the municipal wastewater utility just told us we'll face a 40% surcharge starting next year unless we bring our effluent COD below 180 mg/L — right now we're averaging around 420 mg/L and we have no treatment step at all. | C080-CH3: We want to break into the German and Austrian B2B market for certified PPE but we have no idea how to register our EN-certified products under the EU PPE Regulation 2016/425, find a notified body, or handle the technical file — our accountant handles all paperwork and she's overwhelmed. | C080-CH4: We cut roughly 2,400 metres of fabric per week by hand with straight-knife cutters, and our fabric utilisation is sitting at about 71% — we're throwing away almost a third of every roll, which at current fabric prices costs us around €3,200 a month in waste alone.
plans: Over the next two years the company intends to qualify two product lines for the EU market under PPE Regulation 2016/425 and begin direct sales to industrial clients in Germany and Austria. In parallel, management is evaluating a modest expansion of the dyeing unit's capacity if the wastewater situation can be resolved at reasonable cost.
rd_capacity: The company has no dedicated research or development staff, but the production manager and the pattern technician together can allocate roughly one day per week to testing and documentation work on a defined technical project.
past_collaborations: The company completed a one-year supplier development programme with Tekstilni Centar Vojvodine, a regional industry association, in 2019, which covered lean production basics and quality system documentation, but has not worked directly with a university or research institute.
about: Košava Tekstil d.o.o. was founded in 1991 by Miroslav and Danica Vujanović in Zrenjanin, starting with four sewing machines in a rented workshop on the edge of the industrial zone. Today the company employs 87 people across two sewing lines and a small in-house dyeing unit, and it remains fully family-owned, now managed by the second generation — Nikola Vujanović as director and his sister Jelena Vujanović-Marić as production manager. We make workwear and certified protective clothing for industrial clients: factories, logistics operators, chemical plants, and construction contractors in Serbia and Romania. Our main customers are mid-size industrial firms that need reliable supply, consistent sizing, and documentation that satisfies their own health-and-safety auditors. What separates us from importers is that everything — cutting, sewing, dyeing, and finishing — happens under one roof in Zrenjanin. When a client needs a batch of 300 high-visibility jackets with a custom pocket layout and a specific colour matched to their brand standard, we can sample, approve, and deliver without routing the job through three countries. We are not the cheapest option and we do not try to be. We focus on repeat clients who value short lead times, traceable production, and a team that answers the phone.

name: Lumetek Systems d.o.o.
products: LED driver ploče za javnu rasvetu (10–150 W); IoT kontroler za pametne svetiljke sa DALI-2 i NB-IoT interfejsom; Grow-light modul sa podesivim spektralnim kanalima (R/B/FR); Cloud platforma za daljinsko praćenje i planiranje rada svetiljki; Usluga EMC pred-testiranja i pripreme tehničke dokumentacije za tendere
tech: PFC (Power Factor Correction) kola zasnovana na NCP1654 kontroleru; DALI-2 i NB-IoT protokoli; ARM Cortex-M4 mikrokontroler (STM32G4 serija); KiCad za šematiku i PCB layout; FreeRTOS operativni sistem u realnom vremenu; Python skripte za automatizovano testiranje i logovanje mernih podatuta; LTspice za simulaciju napajanja i filtera; CI/CD pipeline za firmware (GitLab + openOCD)
challenges: C081-CH1: Our LED driver produces a total harmonic distortion of around 19% at partial load, which disqualifies us from EN 61000-3-2 Class C compliance and has already caused us to lose two Hungarian municipal tenders worth a combined €280,000; we need to reduce THD below 8% without increasing board size. | C081-CH2: We are developing an adaptive spectral tuning algorithm for grow-light applications that should adjust red/blue/far-red ratios based on a plant growth model, but none of our team has a biology background and we do not know which photomorphogenic parameters to optimise for or how to validate the model. | C081-CH3: Our luminaire controller runs a small Cortex-M4 MCU and needs to execute a local scheduling and dimming optimisation for up to 64 nodes; the current greedy algorithm causes visible flicker synchronisation artefacts at 3 a.m. low-load periods and we do not know how to formally model the problem. | C081-CH4: We applied for a €150,000 Horizon Europe EIC Accelerator grant eight months ago and have heard nothing; our accountant says our books are not structured the way EU auditors expect and we may have to return pre-financing if we ever receive it.
plans: U narednih 12 meseci planiramo da prođemo EN 61000-3-2 sertifikaciju za naš driver naredne generacije i da apliciramo na najmanje tri komunalna tendera u Mađarskoj i Austriji. Istovremeno radimo na prvoj komercijalnoj verziji grow-light modula za tržište zaštićenih uzgajališta u Vojvodini.
rd_capacity: Interni tim za razvoj broji sedam inženjera koji mogu da odvoje do 40% kapaciteta za zajednički istraživačko-razvojni rad sa spoljnim partnerima.
past_collaborations: U 2022. godini sarađivali smo s jednim privatnim elektrotehničkim laboratorijem u Novom Sadu na EMC merenjima za našu prvu generaciju drivera, bez formalizovanog istraživačkog projekta.
about:
Lumetek Systems d.o.o. osnovana je 2019. godine u Subotici od strane dva inženjera koji su prethodnu deceniju proveli u razvoju elektronike za automobilsku industriju. Nakon što smo videli koliko je tržište pametne rasvete u Centralnoj Evropi tehnički zaostalo, odlučili smo da primenimo isti nivo pouzdanosti i preciznosti koji se traži u automotive sektoru na LED upravljačku elektroniku i IoT kontrolere za javnu i hortikultruralnu rasvetu.

Danas imamo 18 zaposlenih i isporučujemo vlastite LED driver ploče i mrežne kontrolere osvjetljenja gradovima i distributerima u Srbiji, Mađarskoj i Austriji. Naši proizvodi se integrišu u rasvetnu infrastrukturu koja mora da radi bez nadzora godinama, u svim vremenskim uslovima, sa minimalnim troškovima održavanja.

Tim čine elektronski inženjeri, firmware programeri i jedan specijalist za EMC testiranje. Razvoj i prototipovanje radimo interno, a serijsku proizvodnju realizujemo kroz kooperante u Subotici i Novom Sadu. Razlikujemo se od uvoznih rešenja time što nudimo lokalnu podršku, kratke rokove isporuke i mogućnost prilagođavanja hardvera specifičnim zahtevima tendera. Naši klijenti su uglavnom komunalna preduzeća i distributeri svetlosne opreme koji učestvuju na javnim nabavkama.

name: AlgaLux Biotech preduzetnik
products: Phycocyanin powder, food-grade, bulk; Astaxanthin oleoresin, cosmetics-grade; Custom microalgae biomass cultivation under client specification; Pigment purity testing and certificate-of-analysis service for third parties
tech: Open raceway pond cultivation; Closed-loop tubular photobioreactor; Spray drying and freeze drying; Ion-exchange and size-exclusion chromatography; ICP-MS heavy-metal trace analysis; HPLC pigment quantification; LED supplemental lighting control (GPIO-based timer system); ISO 22000-aligned batch documentation
challenges: C082-CH1: Our phycocyanin purity after the first chromatography pass sits at around 70%, but buyers in the German nutraceutical market need 95%+ purity with documented heavy-metal content below EU limits; every extra purification step we try costs more than we can recover in margin. | C082-CH2: Our outdoor raceway pond loses 30–40% of its productivity in October–March compared to summer — we tried supplemental LED lighting but the electricity cost wiped out the revenue gain — and we need a smarter way to manage the light-temperature trade-off through the cold months. | C082-CH3: We are selling direct to two cosmetics companies now but we have no formal distribution agreement, no exclusivity clauses and no IP assignment clause in our supply contracts — one buyer has already asked us to sign their standard terms, which we think are unfair but we can't afford a lawyer to review them.
plans: AlgaLux plans to install a small polycarbonate greenhouse over the raceway pond by late 2025 to stabilise winter productivity and reduce reliance on electrical supplementation. In parallel, the founders are exploring a co-development arrangement with a nutraceutical formulator that would fund the second chromatography step in exchange for a preferred-supplier clause.
rd_capacity: One full-time process engineer and the two founders can dedicate roughly 30% of working hours to development work outside production cycles, with access to the in-house HPLC and ICP-MS instruments.
past_collaborations: AlgaLux completed a short paid consultancy in 2023 with Zelena Hrana d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based functional food startup, to assess whether phycocyanin could be incorporated into a cold-pressed juice product without colour degradation.
about:
AlgaLux Biotech was founded in 2021 by Milena Vukić and Dragan Toš, two food-technology graduates who spent years watching Serbian agriculture export raw ingredients while the value-added processing happened elsewhere. We set up a small cultivation facility at NTP Novi Sad and started growing Spirulina platensis and Haematococcus pluvialis under controlled conditions to extract the pigments those plants produce naturally — phycocyanin from Spirulina, astaxanthin from Haematococcus. Both are in steady demand from nutraceutical formulators and cosmetics makers in Germany, Austria and the Netherlands who want plant-derived, traceable colour and antioxidant ingredients.

We are a team of seven: two process engineers, a lab analyst, a quality technician, a logistics coordinator and the two founders who split commercial and technical responsibilities. Our outdoor raceway pond sits on 180 square metres of NTP yard space, supplemented by two indoor photobioreactor tanks for winter continuity. We do our own extraction and run a first-pass chromatography step in-house.

What makes us different is that we do not buy biomass from third-party growers — every batch is ours from inoculation to dry powder, which means we can trace heavy-metal exposure and contamination risk at every stage. We are not the cheapest supplier on the market, and we do not try to be.

name: RouteWise
products: RouteWise Planner – multi-stop route optimisation for dispatch teams; RouteWise Driver App – turn-by-turn guidance and proof-of-delivery for mobile; RouteWise Live – real-time fleet visibility dashboard for operations managers; RouteWise Connect – REST API and webhook integration layer for warehouse and ERP systems; RouteWise Insights – weekly and monthly delivery performance reports
tech: Java 17 (Spring Boot microservices); Google OR-Tools (VRP and CVRPTW solvers); Apache Kafka (event streaming between services); PostgreSQL with PostGIS; React (dispatcher web console); Flutter (driver mobile app); Docker and Kubernetes on-premise cluster; Python (data pipeline and reporting jobs)
challenges: C083-CH1: Same-day deliveries with narrow time windows: our planner takes too long when orders change during the day. | C083-CH2: Retail clients ask us to forecast store demand so deliveries match it.
plans: Dynamic re-planning in 2027.
rd_capacity: Optimization team of three.
past_collaborations: Student projects with PMF.
about:
RouteWise was founded in 2016 by a small team of developers and logistics veterans who were tired of watching courier fleets burn fuel on poorly sequenced routes. We set up at NTP Novi Sad and started with a single retail client running five vans across three cities. Today we serve more than forty courier operators and regional retail chains across Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia, helping them plan, execute, and track last-mile delivery with software that actually fits how their day works.

Our core product, RouteWise Planner, takes a list of orders and produces optimised multi-stop routes in seconds. Our driver app keeps dispatchers informed in real time without requiring drivers to do anything complicated. We are not a marketplace and we do not own vehicles. We write software and we know the domain well.

The team is thirty-five people: developers, an optimisation group, product, support, and a small data team that joined in 2022. Most of us have worked in or alongside logistics at some point, which keeps the product grounded. We work out of NTP Novi Sad, with a support office in Belgrade. Our clients include Vektor Dostava, Brzi Paket, and the distribution arm of the Sunce Retail group.

name: PaketBus Subotica d.o.o.
products: Next-day parcel delivery across 14 towns in northern Vojvodina; Cross-border parcel relay to two stops in southern Hungary; Web shop plugin integration for small e-commerce merchants; Business-account parcel subscription with volume pricing; Parcel pickup points at partner bus stations
tech: Custom PHP/Laravel dispatch and manifest web application; Barcode scanning with Zebra handheld scanners; PostgreSQL database for parcel and route records; WooCommerce and OpenCart integration plugins; SMS notification gateway via a local Serbian telecom reseller; Google Sheets for manual capacity planning and scheduling; Printed bus manifests cross-checked against driver sign-off sheets
challenges: C084-CH1: Bus schedules change seasonally and parcel volumes on each route swing by up to 60% week to week; right now the owner manually decides which parcels go on which bus the evening before, and we miss the optimal loading about 30% of the time, leaving capacity unused or making customers wait an extra day. | C084-CH2: We have a small web shop integration but our tracking page is only in Serbian and Hungarian. We want to expand to B2B clients in Austria and Germany but we have no one to maintain a German-language customer interface and none of our three developers speak German. | C084-CH3: At our Subotica hub we handle about 800 parcels a day and the floor space is 140 m². Congestion at the inbound belt slows throughput by about 25% during the 07:00–09:00 peak. We've looked at reorganising the floor but every layout we try on paper seems to make something else worse.
plans: PaketBus intends to add three new towns to its network in Bačka by end of 2025 and is in early talks with a second bus operator in southern Hungary to extend cross-border coverage. The company also wants to launch a simple mobile app for merchant customers to book pickups and check manifests without calling the office.
rd_capacity: Our three developers can contribute roughly 20 hours per week combined to a collaboration, and Tibor Kovačević can act as domain expert and primary point of contact for any logistics or operations work.
past_collaborations: PaketBus received a small digitalisation grant in 2022 from the Vojvodina regional development fund and used it to build the current web tracking system with an external freelance developer; no formal university or research institution collaboration to date.
about: PaketBus Subotica was started in 2017 by Tibor and Erzsébet Kovačević, a husband-and-wife team who noticed that intercity buses running between Subotica, Sombor, Kikinda, and a dozen other towns in northern Vojvodina were leaving with empty luggage compartments every single day. Rather than build a separate delivery fleet, they negotiated co-loading agreements with four regional bus operators and began moving parcels the same way people have always moved packages between towns: on the bus. Today the company serves 14 towns across northern Vojvodina and two stops in southern Hungary, delivering small parcels the next day for roughly 30–40% less than traditional courier services charge on the same routes. Our 22-person team includes drivers' liaisons, a small sorting crew at the Subotica hub, three in-house developers, and a customer service team fluent in Serbian and Hungarian. Most of our clients are small web shops, pharmacies, spare-parts dealers, and craftspeople who ship regularly but not in large volumes. We are not trying to compete with national couriers on speed or scale; we compete on price, reliability for the routes we cover, and the fact that a real person answers the phone. The Kovačević family still runs daily operations from our hub on Sendićeva Street.

name: Labos Dijagnostika a.d.
products: Clinical chemistry and haematology testing for hospitals and GP surgeries; Microbiology and antimicrobial susceptibility testing for human patients; Veterinary microbiology and susceptibility testing for livestock farms; Urgent sample processing with four-hour turnaround for contracted clinics; Periodic population screening panels for occupational health providers
tech: Beckfeld Axiom 9000 series automated chemistry analysers (×2) and Beckfeld Axiom 7 haematology analyser (×1); Deltasoft LabCenter 5.2 laboratory information management system (LIMS); VITEK-style automated microbiology identification and susceptibility cards (third-party compatible); Middleware rule engine (custom-configured in Deltasoft) for reflex flagging; ISO 15189 quality management framework; WHONET-compatible data export for antimicrobial resistance surveillance; Barcode-based chain-of-custody sample tracking
challenges: C085-CH1: We run 1,400 blood samples a day across three analysers and our middleware flags about 60 samples daily for manual technician review, but we estimate at least half of those reflex reviews are unnecessary — that alone costs us 2.5 extra technician-hours every shift. | C085-CH2: Our new veterinary microbiology line is growing fast — revenue up 40% in two years — but we keep getting inconclusive antimicrobial susceptibility results for Enterococcus strains coming from poultry farms, and we have no in-house expertise to investigate why. | C085-CH3: We need to upgrade our laboratory information management system to comply with the new national e-health interoperability standard by Q1 next year, but the two developers we have don't know HL7 FHIR and vendor quotes are 120,000–180,000 EUR, which is way over our IT budget.
plans: We plan to expand our veterinary diagnostics capacity with a dedicated sample reception point serving farms in the Bačka Topola area and to introduce PCR-based pathogen identification for veterinary samples by the end of 2025. We are also evaluating options to offer remote result access to GP surgeries through a secure web portal.
rd_capacity: We have no dedicated research staff, but our senior microbiologist and two laboratory specialists can contribute time to structured pilot studies when workload allows, typically a few hours per week.
past_collaborations: We participated in a two-year antimicrobial resistance surveillance project coordinated by the regional public health institute in Novi Sad, ending in 2022, which involved joint sample collection and data sharing with four other laboratories in Vojvodina.
about:
Labos Dijagnostika a.d. has been operating in Subotica since 1983, making us one of the oldest independent reference laboratories in the Vojvodina region. What started as a small clinical chemistry unit serving the local hospital network has grown into a full-service diagnostic facility employing 187 people across three laboratory divisions: clinical chemistry and haematology, microbiology, and — most recently — veterinary diagnostics.

We process samples for more than 40 hospitals, general practices, and outpatient clinics across northern Vojvodina, from Subotica to Sombor and as far south as Bečej. Our veterinary microbiology line, launched in 2021, now serves poultry and swine farms throughout the region and is the fastest-growing part of our business.

Our laboratory director, Dr. Marta Vuković, has led the team since 2009 and holds specialist accreditation in clinical biochemistry. Day-to-day operations are managed by Slobodan Fekete, our operations manager, who joined from a hospital laboratory network in 2015. The senior microbiologist, Dragana Molnar, oversees both the human and veterinary microbiology sections.

What sets us apart is the combination of volume, turnaround time, and a long-standing relationship with the primary healthcare system in the north of the province. We are ISO 15189 accredited and participate annually in external quality assessment schemes run through the national institute.

name: Kriptolog a.d.
products: KL-HSM hardware security module family (KL-300 and KL-500 series); CertiCore PKI platform for certificate issuance and lifecycle management; OCSP and CRL responder services for high-availability revocation checking; Managed PKI for government and critical-infrastructure clients; Security integration and consulting services
tech: Custom ARM Cortex-M firmware in C for HSM cryptographic operations; Java EE backend for CertiCore certificate management platform; PostgreSQL with custom indexing for certificate and revocation databases; PKCS#11 and RFC 5280 / RFC 6960 (OCSP) standards; Epoxy potting and anti-tamper mesh for HSM physical enclosures; Common Criteria evaluation methodology (targeting EAL4+); OpenSSL and Bouncy Castle cryptographic libraries; Serbian GAAP accounting, transitioning toward IFRS
challenges: C086-CH1: Clients ask whether our firmware signing will survive quantum computers — we've been telling them 'we're looking at it' for eighteen months and that answer is wearing thin; we need a concrete migration path to post-quantum algorithms in our HSM product line. | C086-CH2: Our PKI certificate issuance platform handles about 380,000 certificates a year and the database query time on revocation checks has climbed to 900 milliseconds on peak days — clients in the payment sector are complaining that OCSP responses are too slow. | C086-CH3: We're trying to raise a Series A round of about €4 million to expand into the German and Austrian government markets, but every VC we've spoken to wants three years of IFRS-consolidated financials and we've been reporting under Serbian GAAP only. | C086-CH4: Our hardware security module enclosure needs to pass tamper-evidence tests for Common Criteria EAL4+ certification, but our in-house mechanical team keeps seeing micro-fractures in the epoxy potting layer under thermal cycling between -10°C and 60°C.
plans: Kriptolog intends to achieve Common Criteria EAL4+ certification for the KL-500 HSM by the end of 2025 and use that certification as the primary credential for entering German and Austrian government procurement frameworks. In parallel, we plan to release a post-quantum-ready firmware branch for the KL-HSM line and grow the CertiCore platform toward handling one million certificates annually.
rd_capacity: We have a core R&D group of twelve engineers working on firmware, cryptographic protocols, and the CertiCore platform, with modest capacity to take on collaborative projects if the scope is well-defined and the output is practically applicable.
past_collaborations: Kriptolog completed a joint testing project with Sigurnost-Pro d.o.o. from Belgrade in 2021, validating interoperability between our OCSP responder and their identity management gateway for a shared government client.
about:
Kriptolog a.d. has been building security infrastructure since 1997, when a small team of network engineers in Novi Sad started integrating hardware and software for Yugoslav state institutions. After the turbulent early 2000s, we refocused: instead of reselling other vendors' equipment, we designed our own. Today we develop encryption hardware, public-key infrastructure software, and managed security services used by government agencies, national utilities, and payment processors across the Western Balkans.

Our core product is the KL-HSM line of hardware security modules, manufactured and tested at our facility on the outskirts of Novi Sad. Alongside it, we maintain CertiCore, a certificate issuance and lifecycle management platform that currently issues and tracks roughly 380,000 certificates per year for about a dozen institutional clients. We also offer integration services for customers who need PKI woven into existing identity or payment systems.

The company employs 140 people, roughly half in engineering and the rest split between operations, sales, and support. Our technical leads have backgrounds in cryptographic engineering, embedded systems, and network security. We are not a fast-moving startup; we move deliberately, because the clients who trust us with signing keys and root certificates need exactly that. What sets us apart is that we design, manufacture, and support the full stack — firmware, hardware enclosure, and management software — without outsourcing the sensitive parts.

name: CropAir Technologies a.d.
products: Variable-rate application drones (hardware lease with flight service); Prescription map generation service (soil and yield analysis); Flight logistics and pilot deployment (seasonal contracting)
tech: Multirotor drone platforms (DJI Matrice 350 RTK base); Optical and multispectral ground sensors (NDVI calibration); Manual GIS overlay (yield maps, soil surveys, satellite imagery); Proprietary flight logging and dose-tracking software; Field-scale GPS and weather station network; Agronomic decision support tables (threshold-based rules)
challenges: C087-CH1: Our spraying drone deposits 80% of the target dose on average, but drift measurements on windy days (above 3 m/s) show we miss up to 35% of the intended strip, and one large client in Bačka is threatening to switch supplier after two suboptimal fungicide runs this spring. | C087-CH2: We have 14 agronomists on staff who write prescription maps manually by overlaying yield maps and soil surveys; this takes two to three days per farm per season and we simply cannot service more than 40 clients this way — we need to automate prescription generation. | C087-CH3: We raised a Series A round 18 months ago but our investors are now pushing for a formal EBITDA improvement plan before the next tranche, and our internal finance team has no experience building the kind of three-year financial model with scenario analysis that the investors' term sheet requires.
plans: We are seeking a university partner to help us model spray drift and optimise nozzle placement for wind resistance, and separately to help our finance team build a scenario-based forecast model that satisfies our investors' due-diligence requirements.
rd_capacity: We have two software engineers (40 hours/week) and one senior agronomist (available part-time for research collaboration) who could dedicate effort to applied research projects with 2–4 month timelines.
past_collaborations: None formal; we have purchased custom soil analysis from a private lab in Zemun and commissioned trial protocols from an independent farm consultant in Subotica.
about: CropAir Technologies was founded in 2014 by agronomist Dragan Marković and engineer Željko Nikolić to solve a simple problem: grain farmers in Vojvodina were losing 15–20% of their crop to fungal disease because they could not apply fungicides evenly across large fields. We built the first variable-rate spraying drone for the region and have spent the last decade refining the hardware and the workflow. Today we work with 40 farms across northern Vojvodina and southern Hungary, covering approximately 18,000 hectares each season. Our team of 118 includes pilots, agronomists, software engineers, and field technicians. We do not sell drones alone; we sell a service. Our agronomists visit farms, analyse soil and yield history, create prescription maps, and supervise application flights. Most of our customers are family operations with 500–2000 hectares. They trust us because we know the Pannonian soil and weather, and because we take responsibility for the result—not just the hardware.

name: ReVita Water
products: ReVita MBR units — custom-sized membrane bioreactor systems for industrial wastewater; Annual and multi-year service contracts covering maintenance, membrane replacement, and remote monitoring; Pilot-scale treatability studies for new clients or new waste streams; Retrofit upgrades for existing biological treatment systems; PLC-based remote monitoring and alarm packages
tech: Submerged hollow-fibre membrane bioreactors (MBR); PLC-based process control (Siemens S7 series); SCADA and remote HMI for plant operators; CIP (clean-in-place) chemical dosing systems; Aerobic activated-sludge biological treatment; Bench-scale jar testing and membrane flux trials; Chemical oxygen demand (COD) and TSS bench analytics; UV disinfection post-treatment modules
challenges: C088-CH1: A pharmaceutical client must remove drug residues (diclofenac, carbamazepine) that our biological step doesn't catch. | C088-CH2: Membranes in dairy plants foul quickly and need cleaning every week.
plans: Pharma-grade line by 2028.
rd_capacity: Process engineer and a lab technician.
past_collaborations: Sampling campaign with a faculty in 2019.
about: ReVita Water was founded in 2014 by a small group of process engineers who spent years installing wastewater systems for large utilities and decided there was a better way to serve mid-sized industrial clients. We design, build, and commission compact wastewater treatment units for food processing and pharmaceutical manufacturing plants across the region. Our core product is the ReVita MBR unit — a membrane bioreactor system we size and configure for each client's flow rate, load, and discharge permit. We also offer multi-year service contracts that cover scheduled maintenance, membrane replacement, and remote PLC monitoring. Our team of 27 includes process engineers, automation technicians, a lab analyst, and field service crews. We are headquartered at NTP Novi Sad, where our small R&D lab lets us run pilot tests before committing to full installations. Clients include dairy cooperatives, soft-drink bottlers, a generics pharmaceutical manufacturer, and a cosmetics plant. What sets us apart is that we do not sell off-the-shelf units — every system is engineered to the client's actual loading data, and our service contracts mean we stay involved long after commissioning. We are currently developing a pharma-grade treatment line that targets trace pharmaceutical compounds, aiming for market readiness by 2028.

name: Bela Ruža Kozmetika preduzetnik
products: Cold-process bar soaps in olive, oat and lavender varieties; Beeswax lip balms in plain and wild-rosehip variants; Shea-and-cocoa body butters in 200 ml glass jars; Small-batch gift sets sold seasonally through the webshop
tech: Cold-process saponification; Hot-process rebatching; Sodium hydroxide lye calculation by hand and with a soap-calc spreadsheet; Sodium lactate additive trials; Temperature-controlled curing racks; WooCommerce webshop on a shared hosting plan; Basic Instagram and Facebook posting for product photos; Manual stock tracking in an LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet
challenges: C089-CH1: Our cold-process soaps sometimes develop a white powdery layer called soda ash within 48 hours of unmoulding — it doesn't affect quality but about 15% of bars look unsellable and we have to rebatch them, wasting roughly 8 working hours a week. We've tried covering the moulds and using sodium lactate but nothing works consistently. | C089-CH2: We use shea butter and cocoa butter as our main base materials and their price has gone up 40% in the last two years, which is squeezing our margin below 18%. We'd like to explore locally sourced Vojvodina plant-oil alternatives — sunflower, hemp, pumpkin seed — but we don't know how their fatty-acid profiles will affect product texture and skin feel. | C089-CH3: We sell about 1,200 units a month through our webshop but our abandoned-cart rate is 71% and we don't know whether it's the checkout flow, the photos, or the product descriptions. We've never done any structured customer behaviour analysis.
plans: Over the next two years Dragana wants to expand the webshop to cover the whole of Serbia and potentially Slovenia and Croatia, and to introduce a small subscription box sent monthly. The team is also considering moving soap production into a purpose-built outbuilding to give more consistent temperature control year-round.
rd_capacity: The team can set aside one afternoon per week for testing and documentation, and Dragana's daughter Milica, who joined in 2023, has a background in biology and can follow technical guidance with support.
past_collaborations: Bela Ruža participated in a one-day product-labelling workshop run by the Zrenjanin Regional Chamber of Commerce in 2022 but has not had any formal collaboration with a research institution or technology partner.
about: Bela Ruža Kozmetika has been making handmade skin-care products in Zrenjanin since 2008, when Dragana Vuković started pressing her first batches of cold-process soap on the kitchen table of the family home on Temišvarska street. Sixteen years later the business employs six people — most of them family or neighbours — and ships to independent health and organic stores across Vojvodina, while a growing share of orders comes through our own webshop. Everything we make is produced in small batches of no more than forty units. We use no parabens, synthetic fragrances or artificial colours. Our soap lines are built around olive, sunflower and castor oils; our lip balms use beeswax sourced from a beekeeper in Melenci; our body butters rely on shea and cocoa butter blended by hand in a temperature-controlled back room we converted from a garage in 2014. We are not a laboratory and we do not claim to be. We are a small family operation that takes the time to get the recipe right before anything leaves the door. Our regular customers find us at the Zrenjanin Saturday market, in a handful of stores in Novi Sad, Subotica and Kikinda, and on our webshop, which we launched properly in 2021. We do not advertise heavily. Most new customers come through word of mouth.

name: Adria Ecotrail d.o.o.
products: Guided nature and cultural day tours in Vojvodina protected areas; Multi-day eco-tour packages with accommodation and catering; TrailSense — mobile nature-interpretation app (iOS and Android); EcoDesk — B2B booking and documentation portal for travel agencies; Private and corporate group tours on request
tech: React Native (TrailSense app); Node.js / PostgreSQL (EcoDesk backend); QGIS for trail mapping and spatial visualisation; Garmin GPS devices for track logging (GPX format); iNaturalist taxonomy database (integrated into TrailSense species lists); Google Cloud Storage for tour photo archives; Stripe and wire-transfer invoicing for agency payments; Trello and Slack for internal operations
challenges: C090-CH1: Our nature-interpretation app lists 210 species but the automatic species identification from guest photos is wrong about 35% of the time for birds and insects, which embarrasses guides in front of guests and has led to three formal complaints from ornithologist clients this season. | C090-CH2: We want to add a carbon-footprint score to each tour package so that sustainability-conscious agencies in the Netherlands and Scandinavia can use it in their own marketing, but we have no validated methodology for calculating transport, catering and accommodation emissions at the per-guest level. | C090-CH3: Our trails cross three protected natural areas and getting annual permits renewed takes six to eight months of back-and-forth with provincial and national inspectorates — last year we lost the entire spring season on one trail because the permit renewal was delayed, costing us roughly €34,000 in cancelled bookings. | C090-CH4: We have GPS track logs from 4,800 guided tours over seven years but we use them only for navigation; we suspect there are patterns in where guests slow down, photograph and linger that could help us redesign tour itineraries and set better pricing tiers, but nobody on our team knows how to analyse spatial movement data.
plans: Over the next two seasons we want to add two new multi-day routes — one along the Tisa oxbow lakes and one linking Fruška Gora monasteries — and expand EcoDesk with a self-service contract module so agencies can onboard without email back-and-forth. We are also exploring whether TrailSense can be licensed to other regional eco-tourism operators as a white-label product.
rd_capacity: We have one full-time and one part-time developer on staff, both focused on EcoDesk and TrailSense maintenance, with limited bandwidth for new research or experimental work.
past_collaborations: In 2021 we received a small co-development grant through the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture and partnered with a regional GIS consulting firm, Geopanon d.o.o. from Novi Sad, to produce updated digital trail maps for the Fruška Gora national park administration.
about: Adria Ecotrail d.o.o. was founded in 2007 by two former park rangers who wanted to show visitors that Vojvodina is more than flat farmland. Seventeen years later we run guided nature and cultural tours across Fruška Gora, the Deliblato Sands and the Ramsar-listed wetlands along the Tisa and Danube rivers, and we have welcomed guests from twenty-three countries. Our team of twenty-seven includes certified nature guides, a small in-house software team, and logistics staff who handle transport, catering partnerships and accommodation coordination. What keeps agencies coming back — we work mostly with travel wholesalers and specialist eco-tourism retailers in the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark and Slovenia — is that our guides know the ground. We do not subcontract. Every tour leader has completed at least two seasons on the trails they lead. In 2019 we launched the TrailSense app so guests can identify plants, birds and insects during tours and read short interpretive texts in five languages. We also operate a B2B booking portal, EcoDesk, where partner agencies access live availability, per-guest pricing and downloadable trip documentation. We are a small company and we are careful about growth; we prefer to improve the quality of existing routes before opening new ones.

about:
CardioTrack d.o.o. was founded in 2021 by a small group of engineers and clinicians who spent years watching patients leave cardiology appointments without answers because a standard 24-hour Holter simply wasn't long enough to catch an intermittent arrhythmia. We set out to build something a general practitioner in Novi Sad could hand a patient on a Friday afternoon, knowing that by the following week they would have seven days of continuous ECG data waiting in a structured, readable portal.

Our core product is the CardioTrack patch — a single-use, adhesive ECG monitor worn on the chest for up to seven days. Paired with our clinician portal, it gives cardiologists a timestamped record they can review at their own pace, with automatic flagging of candidate events. We currently supply a handful of private cardiology practices and one outpatient clinic in Vojvodina. The team is twelve people: two biomedical engineers, three firmware and software developers, two quality and regulatory specialists, a clinical liaison, and three people handling operations and sales. We are based at NTP Novi Sad, which gives us access to lab space and keeps us close to the university hospital ecosystem we depend on. What sets us apart is that we built the patch hardware and the clinical software in-house from day one, so we are not dependent on a third-party OEM for either.

about: AxleWave Systems d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2016 by a small group of engineers who had spent years working on embedded diagnostics for agricultural machinery and wanted to bring the same thinking to long-haul trucking. We moved into NTP Novi Sad in 2017 and have been based there since. Today we are 58 people — hardware, firmware, data and backend — and we sell a wireless condition-monitoring platform to commercial fleet operators across Central and Eastern Europe, with our strongest markets in Germany, Poland and Austria. Our platform puts a compact wireless sensor node on the gearbox, driveshaft and wheel-end of each truck; the node reads vibration, temperature and torque-proxy signals continuously and pushes processed data to our cloud dashboard, where fleet maintenance teams can see the health of every drivetrain in one view. We are not a consultancy and we do not resell third-party telematics. Every layer of the stack — sensor firmware, edge logic, ingestion pipeline and the fault-analysis models — is built and maintained in-house. Our current reference customers include fictional operator Nordtrans Spedition GmbH and Polish regional haulier Karpacki Przewóz Sp. z o.o. We have fifteen people working purely on signal processing and machine learning.

about:
EkoTok Solutions d.o.o. was founded in 2020 in Novi Sad by a small group of people who had spent years watching small consumer electronics and spent batteries disappear into general waste streams across Central and Eastern Europe. We built our first smart collection cabinet prototype in a rented workshop on Futoška Street and placed ten units around Novi Sad by the end of our first year. Today we operate over 340 cabinets across Serbia, Hungary and Romania, and we run a material-recovery facility in the Novi Sad Science Technology Park where our disassembly teams process incoming devices by hand, separating plastics, metals and battery cells for downstream recyclers.

Our main customers are municipalities, large retail chains and electronics manufacturers who need a documented, audit-ready take-back service that satisfies EU producer-responsibility rules. Our downstream partner for recovered black mass and copper fractions is Halvard Material Group, based in Rotterdam. On the collection side we work with local courier operator BrzaTranzit to handle last-mile cabinet servicing.

The team is 46 people. Roughly half work on the disassembly floor; the rest cover software, logistics, sales and administration. We do not chase volume for its own sake. Our focus is on closing the loop between the consumer drop-off moment and a verified material output that meets the data requirements of the revised EU Battery Regulation. That means traceability at the cell level, not just the batch level, and it means improving our own processes rather than outsourcing the hard parts.

We set up a small workshop at NTP Novi Sad to find out whether those modules could be turned into reliable stationary storage for the kinds of customers that grid-scale systems price out entirely: family farms, grain dryers, small plastics factories, cold-store operators. Two years later we ship self-contained battery cabinets built entirely from second-life EV modules, each one with our own battery management firmware running on top. Our flagship product, the VoltCell 50 kWh cabinet, is now running at seven sites across Vojvodina. Every cabinet carries a two-year capacity warranty, which forces us to know exactly what we are putting inside. That is the hard part of this business. We decided to build something different: a SaaS platform that combines industrial cameras with low-cost sensor arrays and fuses the data in real time, so a production supervisor can open a browser tab and immediately see what is wrong, where, and why.

Today we have twelve people in Subotica and a small field-support presence in Hungary, where three pilot clients in the metalworking and plastic-injection sectors are running our system on live production lines. Our clients are small manufacturers with between thirty and two hundred employees — companies that cannot afford a dedicated quality engineer but cannot afford scrap rates above two percent either.

What separates us from larger vendors is that our stack runs almost entirely on hardware the client already owns: a standard industrial camera, an off-the-shelf vibration sensor, and a mid-range edge computer. No proprietary black boxes. Our team includes computer-vision engineers, a signal-processing specialist, and two people who have actually stood on factory floors and understand what operators will and will not tolerate.

The idea was simple: the paperwork burden on Serbian sole traders and micro-businesses is real, and most off-the-shelf accounting software was built for larger firms with dedicated finance staff. We built something that fits the way a small bakery owner or a freelance electrician actually works. Today roughly 1,400 paying subscribers use our web application to handle their monthly bookkeeping, VAT declarations and payroll in one place, without needing to hire a dedicated accountant for routine tasks. Our team of seven people handles everything from product development to customer support, and most of us live in Zrenjanin or the surrounding area. What sets us apart is that we have focused exclusively on the Serbian regulatory environment — the Kontni plan, the PPP-PD payroll form, the POPDV VAT form — rather than trying to adapt a foreign product. We update the tax rules ourselves when the law changes, and our customers notice. We are not the flashiest product on the market, but our churn rate is low because the software does what it promises and our support team picks up the phone.

What we do is write quantum algorithms that help pharmaceutical and biotech companies simulate molecular interactions faster than they can with classical hardware. Our first paying clients are two mid-sized drug discovery firms based in the Netherlands and one in South Korea; none of them have in-house quantum expertise, so they rely on us to translate their chemistry problems into circuits that run on today's gate-based quantum processors. Pulmoteh d.o.o. has been building respiratory diagnostics equipment in Zrenjanin since 2013. The company was founded by Miroslav and Snežana Kovačević, who spent the previous decade servicing imported spirometry equipment for hospitals across Vojvodina and grew frustrated with long lead times and expensive spare parts from abroad. Their answer was to design and manufacture devices locally, using components sourced as much as possible from within Serbia and the broader region.

Today, Pulmoteh employs 27 people across design, assembly, calibration, and field service. Our customers include pulmonology clinics, occupational health centres, and workplace medical services in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. Our flagship product, the SP-400 portable spirometer, has been placed in more than 340 clinical sites since 2017.

What distinguishes us is straightforward: we answer the phone, we stock our own spare parts, and our service technicians can reach most customers in the Western Balkans within 48 hours. We do not claim to compete on brand recognition with multinational suppliers, but our pricing, response times, and willingness to adapt device firmware or reporting formats to local regulatory requirements have built a loyal client base. The Kovačević family continues to own and manage the business, and every assembly decision is made in-house.

Vojvođanska Energetika d.o.o. has been working in the energy services sector since 1997, when a small team of engineers from Novi Sad began offering metering and audit services to the grain-handling cooperatives and food-processing plants that make up the backbone of Vojvodina's economy. Over nearly three decades we have grown to 88 people — engineers, energy auditors, project managers, and finance staff — and we now operate as a full energy service company, meaning we design, finance, and guarantee the results of efficiency retrofits rather than simply recommending them.

Our clients are mostly mid-size industrial and agro-industrial facilities: oilseed presses, flour mills, cold-storage operators, brick manufacturers, and commercial dairy farms. We write the contracts, arrange the financing, and recover our investment through the energy savings we deliver, measured on-site over the life of each project.

What sets us apart from consulting firms is that our own money is in every project. That keeps our assessments honest. Our audit team, led by senior engineer Branislav Čović, has completed more than 130 facility audits across the region. Project director Milena Savin oversees our retrofit portfolio, which currently covers roughly 40 active contracts. We are not a technology vendor; we work with whatever equipment the data tells us is right for a given facility.

Poljoelektronika Kovačević has been building measurement electronics for Vojvodina's fields since 1993, when Branimir Kovačević set up a small repair workshop on the edge of Zrenjanin. What started as fixing irrigation pump controllers for local cooperatives gradually turned into designing and assembling our own sensor hardware. Today Branimir's daughter Milica runs the engineering side while her brother Dragan handles sales and field support. We are seven people in total, and every node that leaves our workshop has been tested by hand.

Our main product is a ruggedised sensor node that measures soil moisture at two depths, soil temperature, air temperature, relative humidity, and leaf wetness. The nodes transmit over LoRa to a small base station, and readings appear in our web dashboard within minutes. We currently have around 1,200 active units deployed with irrigation cooperatives and larger family farms across Vojvodina, from Subotica down to Pančevo.

What makes us different is straightforward: we know this soil, this climate, and these farming routines. Our enclosures are designed to survive the mud, the dust, and the heat of a Pannonian summer. When something breaks in the field, Dragan drives out and fixes it the same day. We do not outsource support. Our customers have been with us for years because of that reliability, not because of a marketing campaign.
