about:
GenovaMed d.o.o. was founded in 2019 by a small group of molecular biologists and clinical pharmacists who noticed that Serbian prescribers had almost no practical way to check whether a patient's genetics would affect how they metabolise a prescribed drug. We set up in Novi Sad's Science and Technology Park and spent our first two years validating a pharmacogenomic testing panel focused on the CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 enzyme genes — the two variants responsible for a large share of adverse drug reactions and treatment failures in everyday cardiology and psychiatry prescribing.

Today we work with private clinics and independent pharmacies across Serbia, returning genotype reports that help prescribers choose the right drug and dose from the start rather than adjusting after a bad outcome. Our laboratory is accredited under ISO 15189 and every report is reviewed by a clinical pharmacist before it leaves the building.

The team is twelve people: four in the wet lab, two in bioinformatics, two in clinical reporting, and the rest in operations, sales, and finance. We are small on purpose — we want to stay close to the samples and close to the prescribers who use our results. What makes us different is not the technology itself, which is broadly available, but the care we put into the clinical interpretation layer and the speed at which a pharmacy or clinic gets a usable answer.

Naš posao je da iz operativnih podataka koje klijenti već imaju izgradimo nešto upotrebljivo — dashboard koji menadžer može otvoriti ujutru i odmah znati gde stoji, prediktivni model koji upozorava pre nego što dođe do zastoja, ili pipeline koji eliminiše ručno izveštavanje. We set up inside NTP Novi Sad with one selective laser melting machine, a surface-finishing bench, and a straightforward idea: short-run metal parts, made locally, delivered fast. Today we run four SLM machines and a full post-processing line covering stress relief, heat treatment, shot peening, and CNC finishing. Our customers come mostly from the automotive supply chain, fluid-handling equipment makers, and a handful of mold-and-die shops that need replacement tooling before a production line goes cold. We work in 316L stainless, 17-4 PH, AlSi10Mg, and Ti-6Al-4V on request. What keeps customers coming back is not marketing — it is that we pick up the phone, we understand tolerances, and we do not oversell what powder-bed fusion can actually do. about: HempTex Vojvodina was founded in 2017 by Miroslav Bačić and his sister Dragana Bačić on a family-owned plot of land outside Bačka Palanka, where industrial hemp had been grown intermittently since the 1980s. We started with twelve hectares and a single retting pond. Today we farm just over sixty hectares, run a full decortication line, and supply hemp fibre and yarn to mid-sized textile manufacturers across Central Europe. Our customers include a woven-fabric mill in Hungary, a technical-textile converter in Slovenia, and two smaller Serbian clothing producers. We employ forty people, most of them from the surrounding villages, and we try hard to keep that number stable through the off-season by running secondary processing work into the winter months. What makes us different from larger commodity suppliers is that we stay close to the raw material: we grow our own feedstock, control the retting process, and do our own fibre grading. We do not buy in baled hemp from outside. That gives us a consistent input and lets us trace quality problems back to the field. We are a small team and we move slowly on new investment, but we take quality seriously and we are honest with customers about what our fibre can and cannot do.

about: VitaMonitor started in 2021 when Dragana Lukić, a physiotherapist with fifteen years of outpatient orthopaedic practice, watched her mother struggle to follow a printed exercise sheet after knee replacement surgery. Together with her brother Nikola Lukić, also a physiotherapist, and their cousin Tamara Vukić, a mobile software developer, they built a prototype that used a phone camera to watch a patient move and tell them in plain language whether they were doing the exercise correctly. That prototype became VitaMonitor's home-rehabilitation platform. Today the platform serves post-operative orthopaedic patients — mostly total knee and hip replacement cases — who are discharged from clinics in Vojvodina and guided through six to twelve weeks of structured rehabilitation at home. Patients receive a weekly schedule, record short exercise sessions on their phone, and get immediate visual feedback on joint angles and movement tempo. Their physiotherapist logs in to review flagged sessions rather than watching every video. The team of six — three physiotherapists, two developers, and one operations person — works out of NTP Novi Sad. What makes us different is that the core clinical logic was written by people who have personally corrected thousands of patients in a gym setting. We do not chase features; we focus on whether the angle feedback actually changes what the patient does next.

about:
Kognitiva a.d. was founded in 2008 by a small team of statisticians and software engineers who believed that banks and insurers in South-East Europe deserved the same quality of analytical tooling available to institutions in Western markets. Sixteen years later, we are the largest pure-play data company in Vojvodina, with 210 people across our headquarters in Novi Sad and offices in Zagreb and Bucharest.

We build and operate end-to-end analytics platforms: from raw data ingestion and governance through to scoring models, dashboards and regulatory reporting. Our clients include retail banks, insurance groups, leasing companies and several public-sector bodies across Serbia, Croatia, Romania and Bosnia-Herzegovina. Over the past five years we have processed more than four billion transactions on behalf of clients and maintain live scoring pipelines that evaluate several hundred thousand credit and insurance applications every month.

What separates us from generalist consultancies is depth. We do not sell strategy decks; we deliver running software that our clients' compliance officers, actuaries and IT teams can operate themselves. Our staff includes certified actuaries, licensed data engineers and former central-bank analysts. We keep roughly a third of our engineers on internal research so that improvements flow directly into client products rather than sitting in academic papers.

about:
Polje360 d.o.o. was founded in 2008 by a small group of agricultural engineers in Novi Sad who believed that precision farming did not have to mean expensive imported equipment that large estates could afford and everyone else could not. We build variable-rate fertilisation controllers and ISOBUS-compatible cab terminals designed for the scale and budget of farms across the Western Balkans. Our hardware is assembled at our facility on Futoška cesta and our software is written entirely in-house.

Today we have 61 people — hardware engineers, embedded software developers, field agronomists, and a support team that speaks Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, and Macedonian. Our 340 active terminals are running on farms from Vojvodina to North Macedonia, managing fertiliser application across hundreds of thousands of hectares each season. Our customers include large commodity producers, cooperative buying groups, and the dealers who service them.

What makes us different is that we stay close to the machine. Our agronomists spend time in the field with customers. Our engineers have driven the tractors. We do not sell promises about yields; we sell a controller that applies the right rate in the right place, and software that gives the operator a clear record of what happened.

Počeli smo sa manjim krovnim instalacijama za prerađivačke pogone u okolini Novog Sada, a danas upravljamo portfoliom od više od 140 aktivnih lokacija, ukupne instalisane snage oko 18 MW. ŠtitNet d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2014 by a small team of network engineers who had spent the previous decade working inside Serbian banks and telecoms. Our team of 28 includes analysts, incident responders, threat hunters, and infrastructure engineers. We do not resell foreign platforms under a local label — we build our own detection logic on top of open and commercial tooling, tuned specifically for the threat landscape our clients actually face. Most of our clients are Serbian companies with between 200 and 2,000 employees. A handful operate across the Western Balkans.

We moved into NTP Novi Sad in our first month and have stayed close to the research community ever since, even if we have not run a formal collaboration yet.

Our software connects network topology, meter readings and billing records into a single working environment. Dispatchers see the pipe network on a live map, billing clerks pull consumption histories without switching applications, and engineers can run hydraulic simulations without exporting data to a separate tool. Everything sits on open-source foundations—QGIS for mapping, PostgreSQL for storage, EPANET for hydraulics—so a utility does not need expensive vendor licences to keep the lights on.

We currently serve four municipal water utilities in Vojvodina, with a combined subscriber base of roughly 120 000 metered connections. Our main product, HidroLogik Net, went into production at Komunalac Zrenjanin in 2020 and has been extended each year since. The team is eleven people: six in software, two in field support, two in sales and one office manager. We are small enough that a customer can call an engineer directly, which is the way we prefer to work.

about: Vizura Studio d.o.o. was founded in 2011 in Novi Sad by graphic designer Milena Horvat and art director Dragan Čović, who had spent the previous decade working at larger Belgrade agencies and wanted to run something smaller and more precise. Today the studio has fourteen people and works primarily with mid-size consumer goods and retail brands in Serbia and Croatia. name: Analitika Petrović preduzetnik
products: Izrada prilagođenih poslovnih izveštaja i kontrolnih tabla; Integracija i čišćenje podataka iz industrijskih senzora i ERP sistema; Jednostavni prediktivni modeli za praćenje procesa (fermentacija, skladištenje, potrošnja); Periodično održavanje i ažuriranje postojećih analitičkih rešenja; Obuka zaposlenih za rad sa izveštajnim alatima

challenges: C120-CH1: One of our agri-food clients collects temperature, humidity and CO₂ readings every five minutes across 22 storage silos, but the time-series database is growing at 40 GB per month and our queries for monthly reports already take 45 minutes — we can't afford cloud and need a smarter on-premise approach. | C120-CH2: The brewery client wants a dashboard that predicts fermentation completion time within ±2 hours, but fermentation curves shift with each new grain batch and our fixed regression model drifts badly after about three batches without manual recalibration. | C120-CH3: We only have two people who can write code and one of them is Milica who is going on maternity leave; we have three active contracts and won't be able to deliver all of them on time — we need to either hire or subcontract within the next six weeks.
plans: U naredne dve godine planiramo da proširimo tim za još jednog junior programera i da standardizujemo naša rešenja dovoljno da ih možemo lakše prenositi između klijenata sličnog profila. Razmatramo i proširenje na klijente u prehrambenoj industriji u širem regionu Vojvodine.
rd_capacity: Nemamo formalni istraživački program, ali Milica povremeno testira nove biblioteke i pristupe na internim podacima pre nego što ih ponudimo klijentima.
past_collaborations: Nismo imali formalnu saradnju sa naučnim institucijama; jedina bliska saradnja bila je neformalna konsultacija sa bivšim profesorom matematike koji nam je pomogao da postavimo statistički model 2019. godine.
about:
Analitika Petrović osnovana je 1997. godine u Zrenjaninu, kada je Dragan Petrović, tada računovođa sa iskustvom u prerađivačkoj industriji, uvideo da lokalne firme gomilaju podatke koje niko ne čita. Počeli smo sa dva klijenta i jednim računarom; danas smo petočlani tim koji pokriva čitav lanac od prikupljanja podataka do gotovog izveštaja na stolu direktora. Naša kćerka Milica Petrović priključila se firmi 2016. godine i donela sa sobom znanje iz statistike i programiranja koje je gurnulo naše alate korak dalje — od statičnih tabela prema jednostavnim prediktivnim modelima.

Radimo sa prerađivačima hrane i voća iz okoline Zrenjanina, sa regionalnom pivarom, i sa dva javna komunalna preduzeća. Svaki od ovih klijenata ima specifične tokove podataka i specifične ljude koji te podatke moraju razumeti — od tehnologa do komunalnih inspektora. Naš posao je da između tih podataka i tih ljudi stavimo nešto što stvarno funkcioniše, a ne nešto što izgleda lepo na prezentaciji.

Nismo konsultantska kuća koja dolazi, uzme novac i ode. Petnaest od naših dvadeset i sedam dosadašnjih klijenata sarađuje sa nama više od tri godine. To nam govori da radimo pravu stvar.

name: ChemoSpec Solutions d.o.o.
products: Custom synthesis of organic reference standard compounds; Small-batch API intermediate preparation; Analytical characterisation packages (NMR, MS, HPLC purity); Impurity profile studies for generic drug submissions; Solvent and process screening for early-stage synthesis routes
tech: Multi-step organic synthesis (2–10 synthetic steps); 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy (300 MHz Bruker instrument); High-resolution ESI mass spectrometry; Reversed-phase HPLC with UV and DAD detection; Rotary evaporation and short-path distillation; Manual LIMS record-keeping in Excel and structured PDF reports; Beta-lactam chemistry and ring-forming cyclisation reactions; ICH Q2(R1) method validation protocols
challenges: C121-CH1: We're producing about 12 novel organic reference standard compounds per month for clients, but our NMR interpretation and mass-spec data reporting is done manually and takes one senior chemist nearly half their working week. We need a faster pipeline but can't afford a €50,000 commercial LIMS solution right now. | C121-CH2: Two of our synthesis routes for beta-lactam intermediates generate halogenated solvent waste streams totalling about 800 litres per month, and our hazardous-waste disposal contract costs us 4,200 EUR monthly. We want to redesign those steps to use greener solvents but we're not sure which alternatives are compatible with the reaction conditions. | C121-CH3: We want to apply for an INOVACIJE fund grant from FREN to scale up one of our synthesis lines, but we've never prepared a project budget in the required format and we have no one internally with grant-writing experience.
plans: ChemoSpec intends to add a preparative HPLC system in 2025 to support higher-purity isolations and expand the range of reference standards it can offer to pharmacopoeial quality. The company is also exploring a framework agreement with a generic pharmaceutical manufacturer in Hungary that would provide more predictable order volume.
rd_capacity: The team includes four chemists with active synthesis responsibilities and one dedicated analytical chemist, all of whom contribute to method development and process improvement alongside client work.
past_collaborations: ChemoSpec has worked informally with the Faculty of Sciences chemistry group in Novi Sad on NMR interpretation for two reference standard projects and completed a short sub-contract for Pharmateh d.o.o., a generic drug manufacturer based in Zrenjanin.
about: ChemoSpec Solutions d.o.o. was established in 2019 by a small group of analytical and synthetic chemists who had worked in contract research labs across Central Europe and wanted to build something closer to home. We are based at the Novi Sad Science Technology Park and serve pharmaceutical manufacturers, agrochemical formulators, and generic drug developers across the Western Balkans and Central European markets. Our core work is custom synthesis of organic reference standards and small-batch API intermediates, supported by in-house analytical characterisation. Clients come to us when they need a compound made to a defined purity specification, documented with full analytical data, and delivered on a short timeline that larger contract organisations cannot match. We are a team of nineteen people, most of them bench chemists, with a lean administrative structure. Our founding chemist, Dragana Miletić, previously led a synthesis team at a contract lab in Vienna before returning to Serbia. We do not chase volume; we focus on technically demanding requests that require close communication with the client's development team. Most of our work is repeat business from clients who value reliable turnaround and traceable data.

name: Sunčana Mreža d.o.o.
products: Rooftop PV design and installation for industrial and commercial buildings; Ground-mounted PV systems up to 2 MW; SolarPulse — proprietary web-based monitoring and performance reporting platform; Grid connection engineering and coordination with the distribution operator; Annual performance review and preventive maintenance contracts
tech: SolarPulse (in-house Python/Django backend, React frontend); PVsyst for yield modelling and shading analysis; Modbus TCP and SunSpec protocol for inverter data acquisition; SCADA-lite data logger hardware (Janitza and compatible units); AutoCAD Electrical for single-line diagrams; drone-based aerial surveys for rooftop mapping; PostgreSQL time-series storage with custom aggregation pipelines; REST API layer for external data export
challenges: C122-CH1: Our inverters generate fault codes we can't interpret fast enough — last quarter we had 11 sites sitting at reduced output for more than 48 hours before a technician even arrived. plans: Sunčana Mreža intends to extend SolarPulse to support battery storage monitoring as the first battery-backed commercial projects in the portfolio come online in 2025. The company is also evaluating a move into community energy schemes under the new Serbian prosumer legislation.
rd_capacity: Two in-house software developers maintain SolarPulse and can contribute to applied projects on a part-time basis alongside their regular platform work.
past_collaborations: Sunčana Mreža completed a small data-sharing pilot with the meteorology department of a regional technical college in Subotica in 2021 to compare on-site irradiance sensors with gridded satellite data, but the collaboration did not continue beyond that study.
about:
Sunčana Mreža d.o.o. was founded in 2014 by two electrical engineers, Dragan Kovačević and Milena Ostojić, who had spent the previous decade commissioning medium-voltage substations across northern Serbia. They noticed that Vojvodina's flat agricultural and industrial landscape was well-suited to photovoltaic generation but almost entirely untouched by serious solar development. The company started with a single 180 kW rooftop installation on a cold-storage facility outside Zrenjanin and has since built and connected more than 60 MW of capacity across the region.

Today the team of 34 covers the full project lifecycle: site survey and shading analysis, electrical and structural design, procurement, installation, grid connection, and long-term monitoring through the company's own platform, SolarPulse. Clients include food processors, logistics operators, building materials manufacturers, and a small number of municipal buildings. Most projects fall between 200 kW and 2 MW.

What sets Sunčana Mreža apart from larger integrators is the combination of in-house monitoring software and field engineers who know how to read what it tells them. The SolarPulse dashboard gives clients live yield and performance-ratio data, automated monthly reports, and alarm notifications. The team is based in Novi Sad, which keeps travel times to most Vojvodina sites under ninety minutes.

name: FermenTech Vojvodina d.o.o.
products: Lacto-fermented vegetable spreads (red pepper, beetroot, mixed brassica) in 200 g and 500 g retail and foodservice formats; Plant-based kefir analogue drink, oat and sunflower base, with live cultures, 330 ml bottle; Functional fermented beverage range — low-sugar, kvass-style and water-kefir variants; Bulk fermented vegetable paste for HoReCa and ready-meal manufacturers, 5 kg and 20 kg pails; Custom starter-culture development and small-batch contract fermentation for other regional food producers
tech: Defined multi-strain LAB starter cultures (Lactobacillus plantarum, Leuconostoc mesenteroides, Lactobacillus kefiranofaciens blends); Controlled-temperature jacketed stainless-steel fermentation vessels (200 L pilot, 2,000 L production); Inline pH and temperature logging via PLC-connected sensors with batch data exported to spreadsheet archives; Standard plate count and selective media colony enumeration for CFU/ml tracking at bottling and during shelf-life; Modified-atmosphere and nitrogen-flush filling on a semi-automatic rotary filler; ISO 22000 food safety management system with HACCP documentation; Cold-chain logistics at 2–6 °C from filling to retail delivery; In-house sensory panel for texture, acidity and flavour consistency checks between batches
challenges: C123-CH1: Our kefir-analogue drink shows live cell counts of 10^8 CFU/ml at bottling but drops to under 10^5 CFU/ml by day 21 in the fridge, which kills our 'live cultures' marketing claim and we have had two retail listings pulled as a result. | C123-CH2: We are scaling from 200-litre pilot tanks to 2,000-litre production vessels and the fermentation profile is completely different — pH drop timing is off by 6–8 hours and texture is inconsistent batch to batch. | C123-CH3: We need a seed investment of €400,000 to buy a second filling line and none of the three banks we approached would lend to a company with only 5 years of history and a product range that changes seasonally. | C123-CH4: Our labels for Germany carry health-related phrases like 'supports gut balance' and we have received two warnings from a German legal firm saying these phrases may breach EU Regulation 1924/2006; we need to know exactly which claims we can keep.
plans: By the end of 2025 we aim to have a stable, validated process protocol for the 2,000-litre scale and to add at least two new HoReCa markets in Western Europe. We are also evaluating a dried or freeze-dried format of our starter culture blends as a potential B2B product line.
rd_capacity: We have one dedicated fermentation technologist, Milena Đurić, and access to basic microbiology lab equipment including an autoclave, anaerobic jars, a colony counter and a refrigerated centrifuge, with roughly 20 % of her working time available for non-production R&D.
past_collaborations: In 2021–2022 we ran a six-month applied research project with the food technology unit of a regional vocational institute in Sremska Mitrovica, focused on mapping indigenous LAB strains from local vegetable ferments, which resulted in two of the strains now used in our spread starter blend.
about:
FermenTech Vojvodina d.o.o. was founded in 2018 by a small group of food technologists and fermentation enthusiasts who believed that the lacto-fermentation traditions of Vojvodina — sauerkraut, ajvar, pickled peppers — deserved a modern, science-backed production facility. We are based at the Novi Sad Science Technology Park and currently employ 34 people across production, quality control, logistics and sales.

Our product range covers lacto-fermented vegetable spreads, plant-based kefir analogues and functional fermented beverages. We sell to HoReCa distributors and health-food retailers in Serbia, Germany, Austria and the Netherlands. Regular customers include the Grünbach organic retail chain and the Nordalto food-service distributor in Hamburg.

What makes us different is that every product starts with a defined starter culture blend developed in our in-house fermentation lab, and every batch is tracked from raw vegetable intake through to cold-chain dispatch. We are not a craft producer scaling up carelessly — we keep detailed fermentation logs, run routine colony counts and maintain ISO 22000 certification. Our team is led by head of production Dragana Vukić and quality manager Tomislav Horváth, both of whom spent years in larger food manufacturing before joining us. We make honest products and we want the science behind them to be as transparent as the glass jars we fill.

name: Petrović & Lukić IT Preduzetnik
sector: Custom software and IT services for EU clients

tech: C# / .NET Framework and .NET 6 for desktop applications; PHP 8 with Laravel for web modules; SQLite and Microsoft SQL Server for local and small-server deployments; WPF for Windows desktop UI; REST API integration with cloud accounting platforms; Python scripts for legacy data parsing and migration; Git with self-hosted Gitea for version control; Manual keyword indexing and basic full-text search via SQL

rd_capacity: We can dedicate one junior developer to a research or pilot project for up to three months per year, provided the topic connects directly to one of our active client problems.
past_collaborations: None formal; Dragan Petrović attended a one-day workshop at the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad in 2019 on database optimisation but no project followed.
about: Petrović & Lukić IT Preduzetnik was founded in 2008 by Dragan Petrović and Miroslav Lukić, two software developers from Zrenjanin who had spent the previous decade building financial tools for domestic clients and wanted to serve the more demanding Central European market. Today we write, maintain, and support desktop and web applications for small accounting offices in Austria and Slovenia — firms that handle between two and fifteen staff and need software that fits their exact workflow rather than a general-purpose package. Our clients tend to stay with us for years: Buchhalter Brandner & Söhne in Graz has been using our document management suite since 2011, and Računovodski servis Kovačič in Ljubljana has run our invoicing module daily since 2014. The four of us — Dragan, Miroslav, and junior developers Jelena Stanković and Nikola Đorđević — handle everything from initial specification through to Monday-morning support calls. We do not outsource and we do not sell licences to strangers; every client gets a direct phone number and a developer who knows their data. What makes us different is the combination of long relationships, multilingual interface support, and a willingness to keep older installations running reliably rather than pushing clients toward rewrites they do not need.

name: AquaVoj d.o.o.
sector: Water treatment and municipal water services
products: Design and construction of drinking water treatment plants; Wastewater treatment plant installation and upgrade; Distribution and sewer network rehabilitation; Long-term operations and maintenance contracts for municipal waterworks; Hydraulic modelling and network condition assessment
tech: Pressure sand filtration and multi-media filtration; Aeration towers and cascade aerators for iron and manganese removal; Chlorination and UV disinfection systems; SCADA-based remote monitoring of plant parameters; GPS fleet tracking (Garmin Fleet system); AutoCAD Civil 3D for network design; Grundfos and KSB pump systems; Stainless steel (AISI 316L) and ductile iron pipework
challenges: C125-CH1: Our iron and manganese removal units at three municipal plants keep failing to meet the 0.05 mg/L manganese limit after heavy rainfall events; we've tried adjusting aeration rates but the problem returns within 48 hours and we're facing regulatory fines. | C125-CH2: We won a tender in Zrenjanin to upgrade a 12,000 m³/day drinking water plant but the EU co-financing requires a full Environmental Impact Assessment and hydrogeological model of the aquifer before the end of Q3 — we don't have the in-house expertise and the consultants we called quoted 90,000 EUR. | C125-CH3: We're seeing accelerated corrosion on our stainless-steel pipe welds in the Sremska Mitrovica network — we're replacing about 200 metres of pipe per year unexpectedly and we can't explain why the corrosion is so much worse there than in other towns. | C125-CH4: Our field crews spend roughly 30% of their time travelling between maintenance sites in scattered villages; we have GPS logs for every vehicle but nobody has ever analysed them to build a better schedule.
plans: AquaVoj is preparing tenders for two wastewater network rehabilitation projects in the southern Bačka district expected to open in late 2024 and is evaluating whether to add a small in-house laboratory for routine water quality analysis to reduce turnaround time on permit compliance checks.
rd_capacity: We have no dedicated R&D budget or staff, but our chief engineer and two senior process engineers can commit time to a well-defined collaboration project if it directly addresses an operational problem.
past_collaborations: In 2019 we worked with the Institute for Low-Temperature Processes Maretić in Subotica on a pilot aeration trial at our Temerin plant, though the engagement was informal and produced no published output.
about: AquaVoj d.o.o. has been designing, building and maintaining drinking water and wastewater treatment systems across Vojvodina since 1998. We started as a four-person workshop in Novi Sad and have grown to a team of 87 engineers, technicians and field crews who know the region's groundwater and its quirks better than most. Our customers are municipalities — from mid-size cities to villages of a few hundred households — and we work with them from the first site survey through commissioning and long-term service contracts. Over the past 25 years we have put into operation or refurbished more than 40 treatment plants and extended or rehabilitated over 600 kilometres of distribution and sewer network in the province. We do the detailed engineering ourselves; we do not subcontract the parts that matter. Our project engineers carry the job from drawing board to final handover, and our field crews are on call around the clock for breakdowns. What makes us different is that we do not sell equipment — we sell working systems. If a plant is not hitting its permit limits, that is our problem to fix, not the client's. Chief engineer Dragan Mirković and plant commissioning lead Snežana Torović have together overseen the largest projects in our portfolio, and their teams maintain direct relationships with waterworks operators in every municipality we serve.

name: Geodata Pro d.o.o.
products: High-resolution aerial photogrammetric survey; LiDAR point-cloud acquisition and classification; Cadastral and utility GIS database integration; Orthoimage and digital terrain model production; GIS consulting and spatial data quality auditing
tech: Leica ALS series airborne LiDAR sensors; LAStools for point-cloud processing and classification; ESRI ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Enterprise; QGIS with custom PyQGIS processing scripts; Agisoft Metashape for photogrammetric reconstruction; PostGIS spatial database; FME (Feature Manipulation Engine) for data transformation; Python (GeoPandas, Shapely, PDAL) for automation
challenges: C126-CH1: Our LiDAR point clouds for urban areas are enormous — a single city-block survey runs to 80 GB — and clients want classified, feature-extracted outputs delivered within 48 hours of the flight, but our current processing pipeline takes five to seven days on our own hardware. | C126-CH2: We integrate cadastral data from five different municipalities and the data schemas are inconsistent — parcel IDs don't match, coordinate reference systems differ, and topology errors cause overlaps that our clients notice in the final maps. | C126-CH3: Two EU-funded project bids were rejected last year because our consortium agreement templates didn't comply with Horizon Europe partner liability clauses; we don't have an in-house lawyer and the consultants we hired gave us conflicting advice.
plans: Geodata Pro intends to expand its service area into Montenegro and Albania over the next two years by partnering with local survey firms rather than opening branch offices. We are also evaluating whether to develop a lightweight web portal that lets municipal clients view and query their delivered datasets without needing GIS desktop software.
rd_capacity: We allocate roughly one day per week of developer time to internal tooling and pipeline improvements, though this competes directly with billable project work.
past_collaborations: We completed a joint data-collection project with the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica in 2019, supplying raw LiDAR datasets for a research study on floodplain terrain modelling along the Danube.
about: Geodata Pro d.o.o. was established in 2011 in Novi Sad by a small team of surveyors and software engineers who saw that local governments and utility operators in Serbia were making decisions from outdated paper maps. Today we are a team of thirty-four specialists offering aerial survey, LiDAR acquisition, and GIS consulting from our offices at the Science and Technology Park Novi Sad. Our clients include municipal public utility companies, regional water management authorities, and road-maintenance agencies across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. We operate two fixed-wing survey aircraft and maintain our own ground control infrastructure, which allows us to control quality from the moment of flight through final data delivery. What sets us apart is a deliberate focus on practical output: we do not hand clients raw data and walk away. Every engagement ends with a verified, coordinate-referenced dataset that plugs into the client's existing workflows. Our survey coordinator Milica Vranić and GIS team lead Dragan Koprivnik have together delivered more than 140 municipal projects since the company was founded. We are not the largest geospatial firm in the region, but our repeat-client rate — over seventy percent in the last three years — reflects the value we place on long-term working relationships over one-off contracts.

name: Prosveta Digital preduzetnik
products: BrojOtkrij Kit — arithmetic and number-sense board game for ages 8–10; GeoPriča Kit — geometry and spatial reasoning card game for ages 10–12; Starter Bundle — both kits at a reduced price; School Enrichment Pack — classroom licence with ten kit copies and a teacher guide; Web progress portal — free companion site for kit purchasers
tech: Laser-cut and digitally printed cardboard components; Custom PHP/Laravel web portal for progress tracking; WooCommerce webshop; Inkscape and Affinity Publisher for print artwork; Google Sheets for order tracking and inventory; Basic speech-input prototyping via Web Speech API; Manual playtesting protocol with recorded observation notes
challenges: C127-CH1: We designed our game mechanics intuitively, but we have no evidence they actually build mathematical reasoning skills — two schools tried the kits last year and the teachers said the kids had fun but their test scores didn't noticeably improve, and we need real evidence before we can pitch to the Ministry. | C127-CH2: The cardboard components of our kit warp in humid conditions — three batches shipped to schools in Srem last autumn arrived unusable after two weeks in storage, and we had to replace them at our own cost, which wiped out margin on that entire run. | C127-CH3: We want to add a companion app that listens to a child reading a problem aloud and checks whether they understood it correctly, but the child-speech recognition models we tested have word-error rates above 40% for Serbian-speaking children aged 8 to 10.
plans: We want to release a third kit targeting fractions and basic data literacy for ages 11–12 before the end of 2025, and we are exploring a small pilot with a private primary school in Novi Sad that would give us a controlled setting to test our updated learning outcomes measurement approach.
rd_capacity: Milena can dedicate roughly one day per week to structured research or testing activity alongside running the business, and our developer can contribute about four hours per week to any technical prototyping.
past_collaborations: We have had no formal research collaborations; our two school pilots last year were informal arrangements with classroom teachers who volunteered their time.
about: Prosveta Digital was started in 2021 by Milena Ostojić, a former primary-school teacher from Zrenjanin who spent eight years watching children disengage from mathematics the moment word problems appeared on the page. Her answer was simple in concept and harder in practice: make the problem a game first, a lesson second. Each Prosveta Digital kit arrives in a flat cardboard box containing printed game boards, wooden tokens, illustrated story cards, and a booklet of challenges tied to the Serbian primary curriculum for children aged 8 to 12. A short web portal lets parents track which concepts their child has touched and suggests next steps. There are no subscriptions, no screens required to play, and no complicated setup. Parents buy directly from our webshop and occasionally through two small toy distributors in Vojvodina. We have sold just over 1,400 kits since launch, mostly to families in Novi Sad, Zrenjanin, and Subotica, and two primary schools ran our kits as an after-school enrichment activity last year. The team is five people: Milena handles product and curriculum, one part-time graphic designer handles all print artwork, one developer maintains the web portal, and two part-time assistants handle packing and customer questions. We are small, we move carefully, and we are trying to build something that a teacher would actually trust.

name: Bačka Mlin Savremeni a.d.
products: Type 500 bread flour for industrial bakeries; Type 400 confectionery flour for pastry manufacturers; Semolina for pasta producers; Certified organic wheat flour (limited volume); Custom-blend flour for long-term contract customers
tech: Six Bühler MDDK roller mills (1988 vintage); Inline NIR moisture and protein analyser (Perten AM 5200A); Falling number determination by Hagberg-Perten method (ICC 107/1); Wet gluten analysis using Glutomatic centrifuge system; Pneumatic conveying and cyclone dust separation; Sieving and plansifter grading system; ERP system (custom-developed, MS Access-based, in use since 2009)
challenges: C128-CH1: Our biggest customer — a Slovenian industrial bakery — is asking us to guarantee consistent falling number above 280 seconds and wet gluten content within a 1% band per delivery lot, but our current blending is done by feel and we overshoot or undershoot about 30% of loads, causing expensive reformulation on their side. | C128-CH2: We are running six roller mills dating from 1988 and unplanned bearing failures cost us an average of 14 hours of downtime and 60,000 dinars per incident last year — we had nine such incidents — but we do not have vibration sensors on any of the machines and do not know where to start. | C128-CH3: Dust concentrations in our B-mill building regularly hit 28–35 mg/m³ during peak shifts, which is above the legal occupational exposure limit and has triggered two labour-inspection warnings this year — we have tried adding extraction hoods but it does not seem to help enough. | C128-CH4: We want to add a whole-grain spelt and emmer flour line to capture the premium health-food segment in Germany and Austria, but we have no idea how to certify and label these products under EU Regulation 1169/2011 or whether our existing organic certificate covers the new raw materials — we need a legal opinion before we invest in equipment.
plans: We plan to expand export volume to Germany and Austria by introducing a premium whole-grain line and to replace at least two of the oldest roller mill units with refurbished modern frames before 2027. We are also evaluating whether to bring grain intake measurement fully inline to reduce lab turnaround time per lot.
rd_capacity: We have no dedicated R&D staff, but our quality lab operates two shifts and our chief miller and quality manager together can allocate roughly four to six hours per week to testing new methods or piloting small changes alongside a partner.
past_collaborations: We participated in a two-year technology transfer project with the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad in 2018–2019 focused on starch damage characterisation, which resulted in revised milling diagrams for our Type 400 line, but we have had no formal research partnerships since.
about:
Bačka Mlin Savremeni a.d. has been milling grain in Subotica since 1975. What started as a regional cooperative mill supplying local bakeries has grown into a mid-size operation processing roughly 180 tonnes of wheat per day and serving customers from Belgrade to Ljubljana. We employ 214 people, most of them from the Subotica area, and we take that responsibility seriously.

Our flours go into bread, pastry, pasta, and confectionery lines at manufacturers across Serbia, and we export to five EU markets including Slovenia, Austria, Germany, Hungary, and Romania. Our longest-standing export relationship is with an industrial bakery in Slovenia that has taken our bread flour for eleven consecutive years.

What sets us apart is consistency and direct communication. Our milling team — led by chief miller Branko Vukić, who has worked the roller floor since 1993 — knows the behaviour of Bačka wheat across seasons and adjusts blends accordingly. We hold ISO 22000 food safety certification and an organic certificate covering a portion of our incoming raw material stream.

We are not the largest mill in Serbia, and we do not try to be. We focus on reliable supply, honest specifications, and solving problems alongside our customers rather than after the fact.

about:
PlastiForm Vojvodina a.d. has been making precision injection-moulded parts in Zrenjanin since 1994. What started as a twelve-person workshop servicing local household-goods producers has grown into a 134-person operation running 14 injection presses between 50 and 650 tonnes. We supply automotive component suppliers across the region, white-goods manufacturers, and consumer-product brands that need consistent, dimensionally accurate plastic parts at volume.

Our production floor in Zrenjanin covers 6,400 square metres and includes a fully equipped in-house toolmaking cell. Having our own mould-design and mould-maintenance team means we can respond to engineering changes faster than companies that outsource that work. Our quality system is certified to ISO 9001 and IATF 16949, and we run a dedicated metrology room with a coordinate measuring machine and optical comparators.

Our materials range covers ABS, PP, PA6, PA66, POM, PC and glass-filled variants. We process both commodity and engineering-grade resins depending on what the application demands. Most of our customers have been with us for more than seven years, which we take as a sign that we are doing something right. We are not the largest moulder in Vojvodina, but we are probably the most willing to take on a technically difficult part and work through it methodically.

about:
Konverzija Labs was founded in Novi Sad in 2016 by a small team that had spent years running paid-media campaigns and grew tired of sending traffic to landing pages that converted poorly. We built the tooling we wished we had: a platform that runs structured experiments on e-commerce stores and turns the results into clear recommendations rather than dashboards full of numbers nobody acts on.

Today we serve around 90 online retailers in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, ranging from mid-size fashion brands to specialty outdoor-equipment shops. Our platform, Konverzija Optimize, covers A/B and multivariate testing, on-page heatmaps, scroll tracking and session replay. A dedicated professional-services team handles client onboarding, test design and monthly reporting so merchants do not need an in-house CRO specialist to get value from the product.

We are 38 people based primarily in Novi Sad, with a small account-management presence in Vienna. Our analysts and engineers sit in the same building, which means fixes ship fast and client questions get real answers. We do not claim to be an AI company or a data-science firm — we are practitioners who built software around a repeatable testing process that works in real retail conditions.

tech: ESP32-based custom wristband firmware; MQTT over TLS for device-to-cloud telemetry; Python data pipelines (pandas, scikit-learn) for signal processing; PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB for time-series session data; React frontend for ResortView dashboard; Flutter for Termalis Go mobile app; AWS IoT Core and RDS, hosted in Frankfurt region; Rule-based fatigue detection model with threshold logic and moving-average smoothing
challenges: C131-CH1: Our platform collects heart rate, skin temperature and galvanic skin response from wristbands during spa sessions, but the algorithm that recommends treatment duration keeps flagging healthy guests as 'fatigued' — false positive rate is around 22%, and three resort partners have threatened to switch off the feature entirely. | C131-CH2: We have 14 resorts live, but our mobile app reviews average 3.1 stars mostly because guests say the recommendation texts feel robotic and generic — we need the in-app wellness coaching content to feel personal and motivating, not like a medical pamphlet. | C131-CH3: We want to expand into Germany and Austria but our data processing agreement with resort partners does not clearly comply with GDPR Article 28 requirements, and two prospective clients in Bavaria already asked for a legal opinion we cannot currently provide.

about:
Termalis d.o.o. was founded in 2011 by a small team of engineers and hospitality professionals who noticed that spa and thermal resort operators had no reliable way to track how guests actually felt during treatments — only how long they stayed. We built our first wristband prototype in a rented workshop on the outskirts of Novi Sad and piloted it at a thermal resort in Bačka Topola. Thirteen years later, we work with fourteen resorts across Serbia, Hungary and Slovakia, and our platform processes roughly 2,400 guest sessions per day.

Our core product is a sensor platform that reads heart rate, skin temperature and galvanic skin response from lightweight wristbands, then feeds that data into a web dashboard that resort staff can actually use during a shift. We also run a guest-facing mobile app called Termalis Go, which gives visitors personalised session recommendations and wellness summaries.

The team is 38 people: hardware engineers, backend and mobile developers, a small data science group and a customer success team that spends a lot of time on-site with resort partners. Our head of product, Milena Kostadinović, joined from a medical device startup in 2018 and pushed us toward stricter signal-quality standards. We are not a research institute and we are not a luxury lifestyle brand — we are a practical tools company for resort operators who need measurable outcomes.

name: Lex Automatika d.o.o.

about: Lex Automatika d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2017 by a small group of lawyers and software engineers who were tired of watching contract review eat up entire working weeks. We built a contract lifecycle management platform — KlozuraPro — that handles drafting, clause-level review, approval routing and electronic signature in one place. Today we serve around sixty mid-size companies across Serbia, with clients in manufacturing, distribution, leasing and professional services. Our team of thirty-four people works out of NTP Novi Sad, which lets us stay close to the research community and hire strong engineering talent from the University of Novi Sad. What makes us different is that KlozuraPro was built specifically for the legal and regulatory environment of the Western Balkans. Our clause library, risk logic and template sets reflect Serbian contract law out of the box, so clients are not adapting a tool built for another market. We do not sell legal advice; we sell time savings and a clear audit trail. Our first big customer was a Novi Sad-based food distributor, Agrotrans Vojvodina d.o.o., which cut its average contract turnaround from eleven days to under two. That case study opened doors across the region and we have been growing steadily since.

name: FlexBot Systems d.o.o.

tech: Structured-light and time-of-flight depth cameras (in-house evaluated: Zivid, Photoneo class devices); Point cloud processing with PCL and Open3D; ROS 2 for robot middleware and motion planning; PyTorch-based pose estimation models trained on synthetic and real part scans; Real-time control firmware written in C++ on embedded ARM targets; Python task-planning layer with custom heuristic search and MoveIt 2 integration; Onshape for mechanical CAD and in-house FDM/SLA rapid prototyping; GitLab CI with hardware-in-the-loop test rigs for regression testing gripper firmware

about: FlexBot Systems d.o.o. was founded in 2019 by a small group of engineers who had spent years working on factory automation projects across Vojvodina and wanted to build something closer to home. We design and manufacture collaborative robot end-effectors — the grippers and tool heads that actually touch the part — and the vision-guided software that tells a robot arm where and how to pick it. Our customers are small-batch manufacturers: metal fabricators, plastics processors, and assembly shops that run ten different part numbers a day and cannot afford a dedicated robot cell for each one. We give them flexible automation that can be retrained on a new part in under an hour. Our team of eighteen works out of the Novi Sad Science and Technology Park. We have mechanical engineers who machine prototype fingers in-house, embedded software developers who write the real-time control layer, and computer vision engineers who train the perception models on data we collect directly at customer sites. Our current installed base includes production lines at four manufacturers in the Vojvodina region. We are not the largest robotics company in the region, but we know this manufacturing community, we can be on-site the same day, and we build tools that reflect what these factories actually need rather than what looks good in a catalog.

about: BuildTwin d.o.o. was founded in 2019 by three architects and engineers who had spent years watching public construction projects go over budget because nobody could agree on what a building actually looked like before the first brick was laid. We set up at the Science and Technology Park in Novi Sad and started building detailed BIM models for municipal clients across Vojvodina and central Serbia. Today our team of fourteen covers everything from early-stage 3D modelling to full energy audits and IFC-compliant handover packages that a city's facility management team can actually use years later. Our main customers are municipal infrastructure departments, school boards, and regional development agencies that manage portfolios of older public buildings. What separates us from larger consultancies is that we stay small enough to know every file in a project personally, and we do not subcontract the modelling work. Our energy engineer, Milena Horvat, runs every audit in-house using EnergyPlus simulation, so the numbers clients receive come from one consistent methodology. We are currently expanding toward a full digital-twin service so municipalities can monitor building performance after handover, not just at the point of design.

about:
Korventa IT j.d.o.o. was founded in 2019 by three developers who had spent years building enterprise HR tools for larger software houses and wanted to work on something they owned themselves. We are based in Subotica, Serbia, and we build workforce scheduling software for residential care operators in Central Europe.

Our core product, ShiftFrame, is a white-label SaaS platform that care-home managers use to build rotas, track availability, and handle last-minute swaps without chasing people by phone. We currently serve three paying clients — two in Hungary and one in Austria — and we are in active pilot discussions with two larger Austrian chains.

The team is twelve people: eight developers, one QA engineer, one product manager, one part-time sales contact, and one office coordinator. Most of us work remotely across Serbia and Hungary. Our founding trio — Miroslav Fekete, Anita Vörös, and Dragomir Stanić — still write production code alongside the rest of the team.

What makes us different from bigger scheduling vendors is that we adapt the product to fit each operator's naming conventions, approval flows, and labour-law rules without charging for a lengthy implementation project. Care-home groups with up to eighty staff can be live within a week. We are now working to push that ceiling higher so we can serve larger operators without changing what makes the product easy to use.

about:
Voltara Elektronika d.o.o. was founded in 2011 by a small group of electronics engineers who had spent the previous decade working in contract manufacturing for the automotive and utility sectors. We set up our first workshop at the NTP Novi Sad campus and have stayed here ever since. Today we employ 47 people across hardware design, firmware development, production, and quality assurance.

We design and manufacture custom embedded sensor nodes and wireless telemetry units, primarily for industrial customers in Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, and the Czech Republic. Our clients operate in factory automation, district heating, water treatment, and cold-chain logistics. We handle everything from schematic capture and PCB layout through small-batch SMT assembly and functional test, so a customer gets a finished, tested unit rather than a reference design they still have to turn into a product.

What keeps customers coming back is straightforward: we answer technical questions honestly, we meet delivery dates, and we do not sell a platform when a customer needs a specific solution. Our production runs typically range from 50 to 2 000 units per order. We are not a volume manufacturer, and we do not try to be. We are an engineering company that also builds things.

name: Industrijska Automatika Horvatić

rd_capacity: The company has one programmer with about one day per week available for internal tool development, and Tibor contributes evenings when project load allows, but there is no dedicated research time and no formal R&D budget.

about: Industrijska Automatika Horvatić preduzetnik has been wiring up food factories since 2007. Founder and lead engineer Tibor Horvatić started the company after eight years running maintenance crews at a vegetable canning plant outside Subotica, where he saw how much production time was lost to equipment that could not talk to each other. The company now serves eight regular clients across northern Vojvodina and southern Hungary — grain dryers, cold-storage facilities, a sunflower-oil press line, two dairy operations — connecting their machines to modern SCADA dashboards so plant managers can see what is happening in real time and get an alert before something breaks rather than after. The team is six people: Tibor handles engineering and customer relationships, two technicians do on-site wiring and sensor installation, one programmer maintains the SCADA screens and historian databases, and two part-time field workers handle routine service rounds. What keeps clients coming back is straightforward: when a conveyor throws a fault at two in the morning, someone from this company answers the phone and is on-site within two hours if the plant is within 80 kilometres of Subotica. No subcontractors, no call centres. The work is not glamorous but it keeps food moving.

about:
PakTeh d.o.o. radi od 2008. godine iz Subotice i bavi se izradom ambalaže od valovite kartone za prehrambenu industriju, elektronsku montažu i farmaceutsku logistiku. Osnivač i vlasnik Miroslav Fekete počeo je sa pet zaposlenih i jednom mašinom za sečenje; danas nas je 28 i opslužujemo kupce duž čitavog severnog dela Vojvodine, kao i više partnera u južnoj Mađarskoj.

Naš fokus su kratke serije i brzi rokovi isporuke. Kada kupcu treba nestandardni uložak, ojačana kutija za hladan lanac ili die-cut ambalaža za specifičan oblik proizvoda, mi to možemo da isporučimo za dva do četiri radna dana — što veće štamparije uglavnom ne mogu.

Radimo sa firmama kao što su Vojvodinapek-Komerc, Elmont Sistemi i farmaceutski distributer MedLogis Panonija. Svaki kupac dobija kontakt osobu koja prati narudžbinu od probnog rezanja do isporuke. Ekipa u hali ima prosečno devet godina iskustva na mašinama koje koristimo, a svaka serija prolazi merenje tlačne čvrstoće pre izlaska iz pogona.

Nismo najveći, ali smo pouzdani. To je razlog što nas kupci vraćaju.

about:
Farmavita d.o.o. has been manufacturing solid-dose pharmaceuticals and dietary supplements in Novi Sad since 1994. What started as a small compounding operation of twelve people has grown into a GMP-certified contract manufacturer employing 87 staff across production, quality, logistics, and administration. Our 6,400 m² facility sits two kilometres from the Science and Technology Park Novi Sad, and it has been continuously upgraded to meet current EU GMP Annex 1 and Annex 15 requirements.

We specialise in film-coated tablets, hard-shell capsules, and softgel supplements for pharmacy chains, private-label brands, and regional distributors. Our clients include Apotek Centrala, Medicor Pharma Distribution, and several private-label brands operating across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Slovenia. We do not own brands of our own — our business is making other people's products reliably and on schedule.

Our team is led by Director Jelena Marković and Production Manager Dragan Popović, supported by a 14-person quality unit and a six-person formulation group. We believe that honest communication with clients, tight process documentation, and consistent batch records are what keep long-term relationships going. We are not the largest contract manufacturer in the region, but repeat business from clients who have been with us for over a decade suggests we are doing something right.

name: Paladin Osiguranje Tehnologije d.o.o.
products: Parametric crop insurance with rainfall and temperature triggers for grain and oilseed producers; Usage-based motor insurance with telematics scoring for private and fleet vehicles; Cargo-in-transit insurance for road freight operators in Serbia and neighbouring markets; Paladin Broker Portal — proprietary web platform for independent insurance brokers; Annual agricultural risk assessment reports for farming cooperatives
tech: Python-based actuarial pricing models; OBD-II and CAN-bus telematics devices with a custom mobile data gateway; PostgreSQL with PostGIS for spatial policy and claims data; REST APIs connecting the broker portal to national motor vehicle registry; ERA5 reanalysis weather data and national hydrometeorological station feeds; OpenCV-based image processing pipeline for vehicle damage triage; React front-end for the broker portal; Internal rules engine for parametric trigger calculation and automated payout initiation
challenges: C140-CH1: Our parametric crop insurance pays out when rainfall drops below a threshold, but we have had three disputes this year where our weather-station reading differed from what the farmer experienced on the ground; we need a more spatially accurate precipitation estimate at field level rather than relying on a single station 15 km away. | C140-CH2: Our telematics-based motor insurance scores drivers on braking and cornering, but we cannot yet detect distracted driving — phones, fatigue, eye gaze — which our actuaries say accounts for roughly 40% of the high-severity claims we are seeing in the 22–35 age band. | C140-CH3: We want to automate the first-notice-of-loss process for minor vehicle damage claims — customers upload three photos and we want a repair cost estimate within two minutes — but our current computer vision model was trained on Western European car models and performs poorly on the older domestic vehicle fleet we insure. | C140-CH4: We have been trying to raise a €3 million Series A for eight months; two VC funds walked away saying our cap table from the 2009 family founding round is messy and needs restructuring before they will invest, so the real blocker is a corporate restructuring and investor-readiness issue, not a technical one.
plans: In 2025 we plan to launch a pilot of our parametric product in Romania through a local broker partner and to extend our telematics product to light commercial vehicles. If the Series A closes, we intend to hire five additional engineers and one experienced actuary with regional market experience.
rd_capacity: We have two data engineers and one junior data scientist on staff who can collaborate on applied research projects, with direct access to our production datasets under a data-sharing agreement.
past_collaborations: We completed a three-month data-sharing pilot with the Faculty of Agriculture in Novi Sad in 2022 to validate historical yield-loss correlations for our parametric trigger design, though no formal research partnership followed.
about: Paladin Osiguranje Tehnologije d.o.o. was founded in 2009 by the Vukičević family in Subotica, starting as a small broker serving agricultural clients in the Vojvodina region. Over fifteen years we have grown to 112 people and built our own software platform that lets licensed brokers quote, bind, and manage parametric and usage-based policies without paper. Our customers are farmers growing sunflower, corn, and wheat across northern Serbia, and transport operators running fleets between Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Croatia. We do not resell off-the-shelf products — we design the trigger logic, price the risk ourselves, and carry reinsurance arranged through Vienna and Ljubljana partners. What makes us different is that we sit close to the customer: our field staff visit farms before planting season, and our fleet team installs telematics hardware on-site. We are not a large insurance group and we do not pretend to be. Decisions move fast, our actuarial and engineering teams sit in the same office, and when something does not work we change it. We are regulated by the National Bank of Serbia and hold a composite insurance licence. Our headquarters remain in Subotica, with a satellite office in Novi Sad opened in 2021.

rd_capacity: Nemamo zvaničan istraživačko-razvojni odeljak, ali tehnički direktor i dvoje inženjera periodično rade na optimizaciji preseka profila i prilagođavanju legura zahtevima kupaca.

about: AluStar Profili d.o.o. postoji od 1979. godine i jedan je od najstarijih prerađivača lakih metala u Vojvodini. Nastali smo kao državno preduzeće, a danas smo u vlasništvu zaposlenih — što znači da svaka odluka ostaje unutar fabrike u Novom Sadu. Radimo sa aluminijumom od prvog dana: ekstrudiramo, režemo i površinski obrađujemo profile koji završavaju u prozorima, industrijskim okvirima i sistemima za montažu solarnih panela širom Balkana i centralne Evrope. Naši kupci su fabricatori stolarije kao što su Termopan Sistem iz Subotice i Frame&Go iz Budimpešte, zatim proizvođači automatizacijske opreme i sve veći broj kompanija koje grade solarne elektrane. Ekipa broji 211 ljudi, od kojih je većina u fabrici. Imamo sopstvenu livnicu alata, anodizacioni pogon i liniju za elektrostatičko lakiranje. Nije to najmodernija oprema na svetu, ali znamo kako da iz nje izvučemo maksimum. Ono što nas razlikuje od većih konkurenata je što radimo i manje serije po meri i što ne odbijamo nestandardne preseke. Naš komercijalni tim, koji vode Miroslav Đuričić i Jelena Kovač, može da odgovori na upit za dva dana.

about:
LearnBit Solutions d.o.o. was founded in Novi Sad in 2017 by a small group of software developers and instructional designers who believed that corporate training in the Western Balkans deserved better tools than PDF slide decks and one-size-fits-all video courses. We moved into NTP Novi Sad in 2018 and have been building from there ever since.

Today we serve around forty corporate and vocational training clients across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Hungary, and Austria. Our platform, called Orbita, handles course authoring, learner tracking, and — in theory — adaptive content delivery. Our clients include regional manufacturing firms, logistics operators, and vocational training centres that need to certify large numbers of employees on a recurring schedule.

The team is thirty-four people: engineers, learning designers, customer success managers, and a small product team. Most of us came out of the Faculty of Technical Sciences crowd or from the regional ed-tech scene that grew up around NTP in the late 2010s.

What sets us apart is that we built Orbita specifically for mid-size organisations that cannot afford a dedicated L&D department. The platform is multilingual by default, it integrates with the HR systems most common in this part of Europe, and it produces the compliance reports that regulators in Serbia and the EU actually ask for. We are not the flashiest product on the market, but we are the one that works reliably in the environments our clients actually have.

name: Voltis Pay d.o.o.
products: White-label open-banking API platforma za banke i kreditne unije; Agregacija računa i upravljanje finansijskim podacima korisnika; Modul za iniciranje plaćanja usklađen sa PSD2; Analitički dashboard za poslovne korisnike sa prikazom tokova gotovine; Sandbox okruženje za testiranje integracija trećih strana

rd_capacity: Imamo tim od šest inženjera koji u svakom trenutku mogu da odvoje do 20% radnog vremena za istraživački ili eksperimentalni rad, uz pristup sandbox okruženju sa anonimizovanim podacima o transakcijama.
past_collaborations: Tokom 2023. godine sarađivali smo sa timom iz Fakulteta tehničkih nauka u Novom Sadu na pilot projektu anonimizacije finansijskih skupova podataka, koji nije završen objavljivanjem ali je dao korisne interne smernice.
about: Voltis Pay d.o.o. je osnovana 2017. godine u Novom Sadu, sa sedištem u Naučno-tehnološkom parku Novi Sad. Počeli smo kao tim od petoro inženjera i jednog pravnika koji su hteli da bankama u regionu ponude praktičan način da ispune zahteve PSD2 direktive, a da pritom ne grade skupu infrastrukturu od nule. Danas nas je 47 i radimo sa mid-tier bankama i kreditnim unijama u Srbiji, Bosni i Hercegovini, Severnoj Makedoniji, Rumuniji i Slovačkoj. Naši partneri dobijaju white-label API platformu za open banking, agregaciju računa i iniciranje plaćanja — sve pod sopstvenim brendom, bez da zapošljavaju veliki razvojni tim. Tokom 2022. godine prošli smo kroz program podrške Fonda za inovacionu delatnost, što nam je pomoglo da stabilizujemo prodajni ciklus i dobijemo prve klijente van Srbije. Tehnički tim drži visok standard: svaki API endpoint ima definisan SLA, pratimo svaki centimetar koda kroz interne preglede i automatizovane testove. Ono što nas razlikuje nije marketinška priča nego konkretna stvar: nismo vendor koji proda licencu i nestane — ostajemo kao tehnički partner tokom celokupne integracije i posle nje.

name: Ferment-Pro d.o.o.
products: Contract production of industrial-grade bacterial proteases; Contract production of thermostable amylases for starch processing; Custom enzyme blends for detergent formulation customers; Concentrated liquid enzyme preparations in bulk and IBC packaging; Toll fermentation service for third-party microbial strains
tech: Submerged aerobic fermentation in stirred-tank bioreactors (1,000 L and 5,000 L working volumes); Bacillus subtilis and Bacillus licheniformis expression platforms; Ultrafiltration and diafiltration using spiral-wound polyethersulfone membranes; Enzyme activity assays: Anson method for proteases, DNS colorimetric for amylases; In-house fed-batch feeding control via DO-stat and pH-stat strategies; Spray drying for powdered enzyme products; Alkaline and acid clean-in-place (CIP) protocols for membrane and vessel cleaning; Working cell bank maintenance under glycerol cryopreservation at −80 °C
challenges: C144-CH1: Our protease yield from the main Bacillus fermentation has dropped about 18% over the past 18 months and we can't pin down the cause — we've changed nothing intentionally in the process, but we suspect strain drift since we've been sub-culturing the working bank for years without refreshing it. | C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with residual biomass within 36 hours; we're doing two cleaning cycles per batch instead of one, and that alone adds 11% to our production cost. | C144-CH3: A large German detergent customer is asking us to provide a full environmental footprint figure — scope 1, 2 and 3 — for our amylase product within six months, or they will move to an Austrian supplier; we have never done a life cycle assessment and don't know where to start. | C144-CH4: We need to raise 800,000 EUR to install a second 10,000-litre fermenter but local banks are quoting us 9.5% interest and require collateral we don't have; we've heard about EU Horizon and EBRD instruments but don't have the staff to write the applications.
plans: Ferment-Pro intends to expand fermentation capacity within the next two years and to add at least one more validated Bacillus strain to the production portfolio to reduce dependence on a single product line. We are also looking at whether small-scale solid-state fermentation could open a different enzyme segment for us.
rd_capacity: We have one process development technologist, Ana Vuković, who splits her time between ongoing production troubleshooting and small-scale (5-litre bench) fermentation trials.
past_collaborations: Between 2014 and 2017 we ran a joint process optimisation project with a regional food-technology institute in Novi Sad under a national innovation fund grant, focused on improving amylase thermostability, which resulted in our current high-temperature amylase formulation.
about: Ferment-Pro d.o.o. has been producing industrial enzymes in Zrenjanin since 1997, when Dragan and Milena Kovačević converted a former food-processing hall into a small but capable fermentation facility. Twenty-seven years later the company remains family-owned and employs 58 people, most of them from the surrounding region. We operate under contract for food processors and detergent manufacturers across Central and Eastern Europe, delivering batch-produced proteases and amylases that meet customer specifications rather than catalogue standards. Our main fermentation platform is submerged aerobic cultivation using Bacillus strains, supported by downstream concentration and ultrafiltration steps that we have refined over decades of practical operation. Customers come to us because we are flexible on batch size, transparent about our process data, and willing to adjust enzyme activity profiles to fit their formulations. Long-term supply relationships are the rule here rather than the exception: our oldest active customer has been ordering from us since 2003. The production team is led by our process manager Svetlana Borojević, who has been with the company since 2001, and our quality and regulatory work is handled by Nemanja Filipov. We are not the largest enzyme producer in the region, and we do not try to be. What we offer is reliable, documented output from a team that knows its process intimately.

about:
Mediavox a.d. has been making sound work for brands since 1994, when our founders Dragan Vukić and Mirjana Ostojić set up a two-room studio on Dunavska Street to produce radio jingles for local retailers. Three decades later we are a 87-person multimedia production house headquartered in Novi Sad, with a Croatian subsidiary opened in 2023 to serve Zagreb-based advertising clients.

Today our work falls into three connected areas. Our podcast network carries 24 original Serbian-language shows covering business, culture and sport, with a combined monthly listenership of roughly 310,000. Our branded-content team produces documentary-style audio and video series for regional FMCG, banking and retail clients including Veronika Stores, Dunav Credit and Breza Dairy. And our adtech product, SoundSlot, sells programmatic pre-roll inventory to roughly 40 local broadcasters and podcast publishers who do not want to manage their own ad operations.

What makes us different is that we still treat craft seriously. Every show on our network goes through the same editorial review process we designed in 1999 for radio. That discipline, combined with eight years of first-party listener data from our panel programme, gives advertisers something most digital audio sellers cannot offer: transparent, audited audience insight rather than platform estimates. Our engineering and production teams sit in the same building, which keeps turnaround times short and quality arguments honest.

name: BioVitrum d.o.o.
products: Rapid lateral-flow test strip for Salmonella detection in food and environmental samples; Rapid lateral-flow test strip for Listeria monocytogenes in food and surface swabs; Coliform indicator strip for hygiene monitoring in food processing environments; Custom antibody conjugation and strip development service for third-party clients; Batch testing and result interpretation support for food manufacturers under service contract
tech: Lateral-flow immunochromatographic strip design and assembly; In-house nitrocellulose membrane coating on a slot-die coating line; Colloidal gold nanoparticle synthesis for antibody conjugation; Monoclonal antibody selection and characterisation for strip capture and conjugate lines; Statistical process control for membrane coating parameter monitoring; Sandwich and competitive immunoassay format development; Environmental and food matrix validation protocols; ISO 13485 quality management system
challenges: C146-CH1: Our lateral-flow strip for Salmonella gives false positives when the food matrix has high fat content — roughly 1 in 8 results is wrong on meat samples above 15% fat, and two retail clients have already threatened to switch suppliers. | C146-CH2: We produce nitrocellulose membranes in-house on a single coating line, and our batch rejection rate has crept up to 22% this year — we lose about 18,000 EUR worth of membrane per quarter and we still don't know which process variable is driving it. | C146-CH3: We want to register our Salmonella strip under EU IVDR but the regulatory consultant we hired left the project halfway through and we can't find a replacement who knows IVDR for Class B devices — we've been stuck for four months.
plans: BioVitrum intends to complete IVDR registration for the Salmonella strip by late 2024 and use that approval as the basis for entering food safety markets in the EU, starting with Slovenia and Croatia. In parallel, the team is evaluating a multiplex strip format that would detect Salmonella and Listeria in a single run.
rd_capacity: The R&D team consists of six people working on assay development and membrane processing, with access to a microbiological validation lab, a materials characterisation bench, and shared NTP analytical equipment including a scanning electron microscope and a plate reader.
past_collaborations: BioVitrum worked with the Institute of Food Technology in Novi Sad (FINS) between 2018 and 2020 on a Ministry of Science co-funded project to validate strip performance against ISO reference methods for Salmonella in poultry.
about:
BioVitrum d.o.o. was founded in 2011 in Novi Sad by a small team of biochemists and engineers who believed that reliable pathogen detection should not require a fully equipped central laboratory. Working from the Science and Technology Park Novi Sad, we develop and manufacture lateral-flow immunochromatographic test strips aimed at food safety and public health applications. Our strips are designed for use by food production facilities, contract testing laboratories, and public health institutes that need a clear result within fifteen minutes, without specialist equipment.

Over the past thirteen years we have built distribution relationships with food manufacturers, slaughterhouses, and public health laboratories across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. Our current product range covers detection of Salmonella, Listeria monocytogenes, and total coliform indicators in food and environmental swab samples.

We keep membrane coating, antibody conjugation, and final strip assembly in-house. This gives us direct control over quality at each stage and lets us adapt formulations when customer matrices present unexpected interference. Our team of thirty-four includes microbiologists, polymer chemists, quality assurance specialists, and field application scientists. We work with food producers who run high-throughput lines and need answers before product leaves the facility, and with public health labs that need portable, low-cost tools for field surveillance.

challenges: C147-CH1: Farmeri žele upozorenje na mastitis pre nego što se vide simptomi.
