about:
MlekoSmart d.o.o. je osnovana u februaru 2022. godine u Naučno-tehnološkom parku Novi Sad, od strane dvojice prijatelja koji su odrasli na porodičnim farmama u Vojvodini. Nikola Bjelogrlić, inženjer elektronike, i Tamara Vuković, veterinar po obrazovanju, umorili su se od gledanja kako farmeri kasne sa dijagnozama i gube mleko i novac. Ideja je bila prosta: staviti pametan uređaj na vrat krave i dati farmeru korisnu informaciju na telefon, pre nego što se pojavi vidljiv problem.

Danas MlekoSmart ogrlica prati aktivnost kretanja, broj žvakanja pri preživanju, temperaturu kože i obrazac odmora. Podaci idu na naš oblak svakih petnaest minuta. Farmer dobija obaveštenje na Android ili iOS aplikaciju čim naši algoritmi procene da nešto nije u redu.

Trenutno radimo sa dvanaest farmi u Srbiji, od kojih je najveća farma Radovanović kod Bečeja sa oko tri stotine grla. Naš tim broji osam ljudi: dva firmware inženjera, dva mobilna programera, jedan data inženjer, Tamara kao stručnjak za stočarstvo, jedan prodajni saradnik i Nikola kao tehnički direktor. Mali smo, ali svaki član tima zna zašto dolazi na posao svako jutro.

name: MediSoft Vojvodina d.o.o.
products: MediCore HIS — hospital information system for admissions, discharge, laboratory, and pharmacy; TeleKonsult — telemedicine module for video consultations between rural health centres and specialist hospitals; MediArh — electronic health record storage and retrieval for outpatient clinics; StatReport — automated statistical reporting package for the Institute of Public Health obligations; MediMig — data migration and integration toolkit for legacy health databases
tech: Java (Spring Boot) backend; PostgreSQL relational database; HL7 v2 messaging; FHIR R4 (in progress); WebRTC for video consultations; Angular frontend; Docker and on-premises deployment; ICD-10 coding and Serbian Ministry of Health reporting schemas
challenges: C148-CH1: We have twelve years of anonymised discharge records from three hospitals — roughly 480,000 patient episodes — but we can't build reliable readmission-risk scores because our data scientists say the ICD-10 codes were entered inconsistently before 2018 and half the comorbidity fields are blank. | C148-CH2: Our telemedicine module sends video consultations over standard internet connections at rural health centres, and call quality collapses whenever bandwidth drops below 2 Mbps — we lose about 30% of scheduled teleconsultations in Bačka Topola and Kanjiža because of this. | C148-CH3: The Ministry of Health is requiring us to migrate all patient data to a national FHIR R4 repository by Q3 next year, but our legacy database schema is relational and over 200 custom fields have no direct FHIR equivalent — we estimate 14 months of migration work with our current team of five developers.
plans: MediSoft Vojvodina plans to complete FHIR R4 compliance across all deployed MediCore HIS installations by the Ministry deadline and to expand TeleKonsult to at least four additional rural health centres in South Bačka District in 2025. We are also evaluating whether to offer MediArh as a standalone hosted service to smaller private clinics.
rd_capacity: We can assign up to two developers and one data scientist part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our anonymised hospital dataset under a formal data-sharing agreement.
past_collaborations: Between 2019 and 2021 we worked with Informatički Centar Zdravlja Srbije, a Belgrade-based health IT consultancy, to align our HL7 v2 message formats with the national e-Health platform requirements.
about: MediSoft Vojvodina d.o.o. has been developing software for public health institutions in Vojvodina since 2004. We started as a small team in Subotica writing custom reporting tools for the General Hospital Subotica, and over the past two decades we have grown into a regional software house with 67 employees and deployments across more than twenty health centres and hospitals between Sombor and Zrenjanin. Our flagship product, MediCore HIS, manages patient admissions, discharge documentation, laboratory ordering, and pharmacy workflows for six district hospitals. In 2021 we added a telemedicine module, TeleKonsult, which allows rural general practitioners to connect their patients with specialists in larger centres without the patient travelling. Our customers are almost entirely public health institutions funded through the Republican Health Insurance Fund, which means procurement cycles are long and reliability matters more than novelty. We do not chase trends; we maintain systems that staff actually use every day, often under difficult network and hardware conditions. Our development team works in Subotica, with field support staff based in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin. What makes us different is twenty years of accumulated knowledge of how Vojvodina's hospitals actually work — the workarounds, the reporting obligations to the Ministry, and the particular way ICD-10 is applied in Serbian clinical practice.

challenges: C149-CH1: We sell 18,000 tonnes of bran a year as cheap animal feed; we'd like a higher-value use. | C149-CH2: Electricity is our second-largest cost and peaks at bad times.

about: Zlatni Klas Mlin a.d. has been milling grain on the southern edge of Novi Sad since 1974, when the original cooperative elevator and stone-ground mill were built alongside the road to Petrovaradin. Over the decades we rebuilt the facility twice, and today we run a fully enclosed roller-mill line with a daily throughput of roughly 550 tonnes of wheat. Our customers are industrial bakeries, pasta manufacturers and wholesale distributors across Serbia and the wider region; many have bought from us continuously for more than twenty years. The current management team is led by director Branko Savić and production manager Jelena Horvatović, who together have over four decades of milling experience between them. What makes us different is consistency: we source wheat from a tight network of about sixty farms in Vojvodina, we test every intake lot for moisture, protein and falling number in our on-site quality lab, and we mill to tolerances that our bakery customers rely on for automated dough lines. We employ 140 people across milling, logistics, quality control and administration. We are not a flashy company; we do one thing carefully and we have done it for fifty years. Our current focus is on widening our product range into higher-value food ingredients while keeping the core flour business running without disruption.

name: SanaFarma Digitale d.o.o.
products: PillaBox smart pill dispenser (tabletop hardware unit with compartment locking and reminder system); SanaApp family-facing mobile application (iOS and Android); Caregiver dashboard for home-care organisations (web-based, subscription); Onboarding and device-setup service for pharmacies and GP practices
tech: Embedded C on STM32 microcontroller family; Acoustic event detection via onboard MEMS microphone and threshold-based classifier; Capacitive touch sensing for compartment interaction logging; React Native for cross-platform mobile application; Node.js REST API backend hosted on DigitalOcean; PostgreSQL for event and adherence data storage; Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) for dispenser-to-phone communication; Figma for UI prototyping
challenges: C150-CH1: Our dispenser's acoustic sensor is supposed to detect the click of a pill being taken, but in real home environments — TV on, background noise — it produces a false-positive rate of about 22%, which destroys patient trust and generates useless alerts for caregivers. | C150-CH2: We interviewed 60 elderly users and found that 40% stop using the app within three weeks because the font sizes and navigation flow do not match the cognitive and motor patterns of people over 70; we need a systematic redesign but our two-person team has no UX research background. | C150-CH3: A potential distribution partner in Hungary wants exclusivity for two years and our lawyer says the contract draft they sent has clauses that would prevent us from selling through pharmacies in Slovakia and Austria; we need specialised cross-border commercial contract review but cannot afford a full international law firm.
plans: Over the next twelve months we plan to complete a hardware revision of PillaBox, launch a paid pilot with a home-care network in Vojvodina covering at least 150 patients, and establish at least one cross-border distribution arrangement in a neighbouring EU country. We are also preparing an application for an Innovation Fund Serbia early-stage grant to fund a clinical validation study.
rd_capacity: We have two developers who can dedicate part of their time to collaborative research projects, and we maintain a dataset of labelled acoustic events and anonymised app-usage logs from our pilot deployments.
past_collaborations: We worked informally with a biomedical engineering student from a technical college in Novi Sad in 2023, who helped us run the initial acoustic sensor bench tests as part of his final-year project.
about:
SanaFarma Digitale d.o.o. was founded in Subotica in 2021 by two nurses-turned-engineers who spent years watching elderly patients leave hospitals with complex medication schedules and no reliable way to follow them at home. We build tools that sit between a patient's bedside and a family member's phone, making it easier to take the right pill at the right time without turning the patient into someone who feels monitored.

Our core product is a smart pill dispenser paired with a mobile application for family members and informal caregivers. The dispenser organises up to seven daily compartments, sends gentle audio and light reminders, and logs whether a dose was taken. The app translates that data into plain language so a son or daughter in another city knows whether their parent is on track without having to call every morning.

Our eight-person team combines backgrounds in embedded hardware, mobile software, and clinical care. We have run pilots in Subotica and Sombor with a small group of patients referred through a network of general practitioners and home-care organisations. Those pilots taught us a great deal about what actually fails in a real living room, and that experience shapes every design decision we make.

We are not trying to replace a pharmacist or a doctor. We are trying to reduce the gap between a prescription leaving a clinic and a patient reliably following it.

name: KreditNova d.o.o.

tech: Python-based ML pipeline (scikit-learn, XGBoost) for credit and fraud scoring; PostgreSQL with partitioned loan-event tables; REST and OAuth2 PSD2 open-banking integration layer; React front-end for borrower-facing application flow; Docker and Kubernetes on a local cloud provider; Grafana and Prometheus for model-performance monitoring; Internal labelling tool for manual review queue management; Segment for funnel analytics and drop-off tracking
challenges: C151-CH1: Our fraud detection model flags about 8% of applications as suspicious, but manual review shows that roughly 60% of those flags are false positives — we're turning away good customers and the review team is overwhelmed. | C151-CH2: We want to use open banking transaction data to enrich our scoring, but the PSD2 consent flows we've built convert at only 23% — most applicants abandon before granting access. | C151-CH3: We have three years of repayment data now — roughly 41,000 closed loans — but we still can't quantify how much of the default risk is explained by macroeconomic conditions versus individual borrower behaviour, and the regulator is asking us to separate the two.
plans: KreditNova intends to launch its broker API to two mid-sized gig platforms operating in Serbia by the end of 2025, extending lending access without building a direct acquisition channel for each platform. Longer term, the team is evaluating whether FlowScore can be licensed to other non-bank lenders in the Western Balkans region.
rd_capacity: We can dedicate one senior data engineer and our head of risk as working counterparts for any research collaboration, with access to anonymised loan data under a signed data-sharing agreement.
past_collaborations: KreditNova completed a six-month data consultancy engagement in 2022 with Analitika Soft d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based analytics firm, to rebuild the feature pipeline underlying FlowScore.
about:
KreditNova d.o.o. was founded in 2018 by a small team that had watched friends and family — delivery couriers, translators, designers, and seasonal workers — get rejected by every bank they approached, not because they were unreliable but because their income came in irregular patterns that standard credit bureaus could not read. We built our platform to change that.

We are based at the Novi Sad Science Technology Park and we lend to people whose work lives do not fit a salary slip: freelancers on project contracts, ride-share drivers, remote workers paid in foreign currencies, and self-employed tradespeople. Our scoring engine looks at real behaviour — payment cadence, cash-flow consistency, platform activity signals — rather than just a monthly net figure stamped by an employer.

Since our first loan went out in early 2019 we have processed more than 60,000 applications and closed over 41,000 loan agreements. Our average loan is around 85,000 RSD, repaid over six to eighteen months. We have 34 people across product, engineering, risk, operations, and customer support. Our head of risk is Dragana Filipović, who spent seven years in consumer credit at a regional bank before joining us in 2020. Our CEO, Marko Vujić, founded the company after completing a data-science programme in Vienna.

We do not claim to be perfect lenders. We claim to be honest ones — fast decisions, plain-language contracts, and a genuine attempt to say yes when the data supports it.

name: NutriKod d.o.o.
products: White-label whey–pea protein blend sachets in single-serve 32 g format; Functional food pouches with added vitamins and electrolytes for endurance clients; Custom flavour development and stability testing for private-label customers; Batch documentation and regulatory dossier preparation for EU market entry; Small-run pilot batches (5,000–10,000 units) for new brand launches
tech: Twin-shaft ribbon blender with variable speed control; Vertical form-fill-seal (VFFS) sachet filling line; Near-infrared (NIR) inline protein analyser; Multilayer laminate packaging (PET/ALU/PE construction); In-house dissolution and sieve testing per client SOP; ERP-lite production tracking built on an open-source platform; Water-activity meter (aw) for humidity-related shelf-life checks; Nitrogen flushing at the filling station for oxygen control
challenges: C152-CH1: Our whey-pea protein blend clumps in humid warehouse conditions above 60% RH, causing roughly 8% of sachets to fail the dissolution test that our German client requires, and we are getting chargebacks on about 2,000 units per month. | C152-CH2: We need to design a sachet packaging that keeps oxygen transmission below 0.5 cc/m²/day but every laminate supplier we talk to quotes a 12-month MOQ that we can't fund at our current volume of 60,000 sachets per month. | C152-CH3: We claim 27 g of protein per 32 g sachet on the label, but our NIR inline measurement drifts by ±2 g over a production run because the instrument was calibrated only on pure whey and our blend ratio changes per client recipe.
plans: NutriKod plans to add a second VFFS line by mid-2026 to reach 120,000 units per month and begin supplying a third DACH distributor currently in negotiation. We are also evaluating a small range of finished-goods branded products for the Serbian retail channel as a long-term margin improvement.
rd_capacity: We have one full-time food technologist, Maja Kovačević, dedicated to formulation and stability testing, supported part-time by the quality manager during new product development cycles.
past_collaborations: We completed a three-month applied project with a private food-testing laboratory in Novi Sad, LabTeh d.o.o., to validate our in-house dissolution method against their reference protocol.
about: NutriKod d.o.o. was founded in 2021 in Novi Sad by two food technologists who spent the previous decade working for contract manufacturers in Central Europe. We set up inside the Science and Technology Park Novi Sad because we wanted short connections to applied research and fast iteration cycles, not a classic factory floor. What we do is straightforward: sports-nutrition brands send us a target nutritional profile, a flavour direction and a delivery format, and we handle formulation, blending, filling and quality documentation from our 420 m² facility. Our main output is single-serve protein sachets and functional food pouches sold under our clients' own labels. Current regular customers include a Serbian gym-chain brand called FormaLine and two DACH distributors, SupraNutrition GmbH and Alpenfit Handels GmbH. Production runs between 50,000 and 70,000 units per month depending on season. The team of eighteen people covers formulation, production, quality assurance and logistics. Our production manager, Dragan Miletić, built the blending and filling line himself, sourcing components from three different equipment markets to keep capital costs low. That practical approach defines how we work: we solve problems with the materials and data we already have rather than waiting for ideal conditions.

name: Panonska Slanica a.d.
products: Vojvodina-style kulen (paprika-cured pork sausage), whole and sliced; Slanina (dry-cured pork belly), smoked and unsmoked variants; Air-dried beef (govđa pršuta), whole muscle, vacuum-packed; Mixed charcuterie gift assortments for retail and food-service
tech: Controlled-atmosphere drying chambers with passive airflow regulation; Cold-smoke generation using beech and cherry wood chips; Manual brine injection and dry-rub curing lines; Single-point thermostat and humidity sensor per drying room (analogue readout); Vacuum skin-pack and modified-atmosphere packaging lines; HACCP-based manual logbook system with daily supervisor sign-off; Third-party microbiological testing laboratory (contracted monthly swab analysis); ERP system for inventory and batch tracking (locally customised, installed 2017)
challenges: C153-CH1: Our drying chambers run for 21 days per batch and energy costs for those chambers rose 38% last year; we have no real-time monitoring inside the chamber, just one thermostat and one humidity sensor per room, so we can't tell where we are wasting energy. | C153-CH2: We found Listeria monocytogenes in environmental swabs in two of our slicing rooms three times in the last 18 months; we have intensified cleaning but can't identify the persistent harborage point and this is threatening our BRCGS Grade A certificate. | C153-CH3: The collagen casings we import from Austria jumped 60% in price since 2022; we want to know if locally sourced natural casings from Serbian slaughterhouses can meet our standardised calibre tolerances at scale.
plans: Panonska Slanica is preparing to open a second slicing and packaging line by early 2026 to handle growing demand from a Romanian retail partner. We are also evaluating whether a small on-site laboratory could reduce our dependency on contracted third-party microbiological testing.
rd_capacity: We do not have a dedicated research team; technical questions are handled by our head of production and two senior process technicians who can allocate roughly one day per week to collaborative work.
past_collaborations: We participated in a one-semester student project with the food technology faculty in Novi Sad in 2019 focused on salt-reduction trials in slanina, which did not lead to a formal partnership but produced data we still reference.
about: Panonska Slanica a.d. has been making cured and dried meat products in Subotica since 1975. We started as a small cooperative serving local markets in the northern Vojvodina region and have grown into a mid-size producer with 312 employees and a product range that reaches retail shelves in Serbia, Hungary and Romania. Our core products — kulen, slanina and air-dried beef — follow recipes and drying methods that have been part of this region for generations. We have not replaced those methods; we have tried to make them consistent enough to supply modern retail chains without losing the character that makes them worth buying. Our production facility covers 8,400 square metres and includes dedicated curing cellars, drying chambers and a slicing and packaging hall. Commercial director Milena Vukašin leads our sales relationships with retail partners in all three markets. Head of production Dragan Kereš has worked on the floor here for over twenty years. We hold BRCGS Grade A certification and export under HACCP-compliant protocols. What sets us apart is straightforward: we do not cut drying time, we use whole-muscle cuts, and we sell under our own label rather than as a private-label supplier. We are not trying to be the cheapest option on the shelf.
